akhfash:3-3.t: He said: ﴿وَأَذَانٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ﴿أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَرِيۤءٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾, i.e. "بأَنّ اللهَ بريء" (that Allah is free of …); and likewise ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُخْزِي ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ [2], i.e. "بأَن الله".

akhfash:5-5.t:
He said: ﴿فَإِذَا ٱنسَلَخَ ٱلأَشْهُرُ ٱلْحُرُمُ﴾: He used the plural of paucity because its meaning is "the four". That is because "الأَشْهُر" is used only when "three" to "ten" is mentioned with it; when "three" to "ten" is not mentioned, it is "الشُّهُورُ".
And He said ﴿وَٱقْعُدُواْ لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ﴾, dropping "على" (on). The poet said [in the wāfir metre, and it is the fifty-sixth poetic witness]:
نُغالِى اللَّحْمَ للأَضْيافِ نِيْئاً * وَنَبْذُلُه إذا نَضِجَ القُدُورُ
(We pay dearly for meat for our guests while it is raw, and give it freely when the pots are cooked.)
He meant: "نُغالِى باللحم" (we pay dearly for the meat).

akhfash:6-6.t:
He said: ﴿وَأَنْ أَحَدٌ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ ٱسْتَجَارَكَ﴾. [Translator's note: the source prints «وَأَنْ»; the Qur'anic text has «وَإِنْ».] He began a nominal clause after (أنْ), though making أحد nominative by an implied verb is the more analogical of the two ways, because a nominal clause does not begin after the particles of condition. However, they have said that with "أَنْ" because of its firm standing and its elegance when nouns follow it and there is no verb after it that is overtly jussive, as [the poet] said [in the basīṭ metre, and it is the one hundred and seventy-eighth poetic witness]:
* عاوِدْ هَراةَ وأَنْ مَعْمُورُها خَرِبا *
(Return to Herat, even if its inhabited part has become ruined.)
And [another] said [in the kāmil metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-fourth poetic witness]:
لا تَجْزَعِي أَنْ مُنْفِساً أَهْلَكْتُهُ * وأَذا هَلَكْتُ فَعِنْدَ ذلِكَ فَاجْزَعي
(Do not grieve if I have squandered something precious; but when I perish, then grieve.)
They have claimed that the poet's words [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-fifth poetic witness]:
أَتَجْزَعُ أَنْ نَفْسٌ أَتَاهَا حِمامُها * فَهَلاَّ الَّتِي عَنْ بينِ جَنْبَيْكَ تَدْفَعُ
(Do you grieve that a soul has met its death? Why then do you not defend the one between your own two sides?)
are recited only with the nominative, the verb having fallen on something connected with it. Here a nominal clause has begun after "أنْ"; and if you wish, you may make it nominative by an implied verb.

akhfash:7-7.t: He said: ﴿كَيْفَ يَكُونُ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ عَهْدٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَعِندَ رَسُولِهِ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ﴾: this is an exception excluded from the beginning of the speech, and (الذينَ) is in the position of the accusative.

akhfash:8-8.t: He said: ﴿كَيْفَ وَإِن يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ لاَ يَرْقُبُواْ فِيكُمْ﴾: He left something implied, as though [He said] "How will you not fight them?", and Allah knows best.

akhfash:12-12.t: He said: ﴿وَإِن نَّكَثُوۤاْ أَيْمَانَهُم مِّن بَعْدِ عَهْدِهِمْ﴾; He said ﴿فَقَاتِلُوۤاْ أَئِمَّةَ ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾: he made the hamza a yāʾ because it is in a position of kasra and what precedes it has fatḥa, and he did not pronounce the hamza because two hamzas come together. Whoever holds that two hamzas may be combined pronounces the hamza.

akhfash:13-13.t: He said: ﴿وَهَمُّواْ بِإِخْرَاجِ ٱلرَّسُولِ﴾, because you say "هَمَمْتُ بكذا" (I intended such-and-such) and "أَهَمَّني كذا" (such-and-such concerned me).

akhfash:25-25.t: He said: ﴿فِي مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةٍ﴾: it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf). Likewise every plural whose third letter is alif, followed after the alif by a doubled letter or by two or more light letters, is a diptote both when definite and when indefinite, such as "محاريب", "تماثيل", "مساجد" and the like — unless it ends in hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa); if it ends in hāʾ, it is triptote when indefinite, such as "طيالِسَة" and "صياقِلَة". The Arabs prevented this plural from being declined only because it is a pattern that does not occur for a singular and occurs only for the plural, and the plural is heavier than the singular; so since this pattern occurs only for what is heavier, it was not declined. As for the one ending in hāʾ, it is declined because the hāʾ is separable, as though it were a noun on its own; and declension falls only at the end of the noun, so it fell on the hāʾ, and that is why it is declined. It was likened to "حَضْرَموت", and "حَضْرَمَوْتَ" is declined when indefinite.

akhfash:28-28.t: He said: ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ عَيْلَةً﴾, which is "الفَقْر" (poverty). You say "عالَ" "يَعِيلُ" "عَيْلَةً", i.e. "he became poor". And "أَعَالَ" "إِعالَةً": when he came to have dependants. And "عالَ عِيالَهُ" (he supported his dependants) and "هو يَعُولُهم" "عَوْلاً" and "عِيَالَةً". And He said "﴿ذٰلِكَ أَدْنَىٰ أَلاَّ تَعُولُواْ﴾, i.e. that you not have to support dependants. And "أعالَ الرجلُ" "يُعِيلُ" when he comes to have dependants.

akhfash:30-30.t: [And He said:] ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ٱبْنُ ٱللَّهِ﴾. Some dropped the tanwīn, and that is poor, because the tanwīn is left out only when the noun can do without "ابن" (son) and is traced to a well-known name. Here the noun cannot do without it: if you said "وَقَالَتِ اليَهودُ عَزَيْزُ" it would not be a complete statement. However, it has been read so, and frequently, and we read it so by way of quotation (ḥikāya), as though they meant "وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ نَبِيُّنا عُزَيْزُ ابنُ اللهِ" (the Jews said: our prophet ʿUzayr is the son of Allah). [Translator's note: the source alternates between «عزير» and «عزيز»; translated as written.]

akhfash:32-32.t: He said: ﴿وَيَأْبَىٰ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ أَن يُتِمَّ نُورَهُ﴾*, because (أن يتم) is a noun [an interpreted maṣdar], as though it were "يَأبَى اللهُ أَلاَّ إِتمامَ نُورِه" (Allah refuses anything but the completion of His light).

akhfash:34-35.t:
He said: ﴿يَكْنِزُونَ ٱلذَّهَبَ وَٱلْفِضَّةَ﴾, then He said ﴿يُحْمَىٰ عَلَيْهَا فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ﴾, so He made the speech refer to the last of them. The poet said [in the munsariḥ metre, and it is the sixtieth poetic witness]:
نَحْنُ بِما عِنْدَنا وَأَنْتَ بِما * عِنْدَكَ راضٍ والرَأْيُ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, and opinion differs.)

akhfash:37-37.t:
He said: ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّسِيۤءُ زِيَادَةٌ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾: it is postponement. You say "أَنْسَأْتُهُ الدَّيْنَ" when you have left it to him to defer. And "نَسَأْتُ عَنْهُ دَيْنَهُ", i.e. I deferred his debt for him. I only said "أَنْسَأْتُهُ الدَّيْنَ" because you say "I made it his to defer", and "نَسَأْتُ عَنْهُ دَيْنَه" "فَأَنَا أنَّسَؤُهُ", i.e. I defer it. Likewise "النَّساءُ في العُمْر" (prolongation of life); it is said: "مَنْ سَرَّهُ النَّساءُ في العُمُر" (whoever would be pleased to have his life prolonged …). And one says "عِرْق النَّسَا" (the sciatic vein) without hamza.
And He said ﴿لِّيُوَاطِئُواْ﴾, because it is from "وَاطَأْتُ" (I agreed with). Like it is (هِيَ أَشَدُّ وِطاءً), i.e. "مواطأة" (accord), which is concordance. Some read (وَطْءا), i.e. standing firm.

akhfash:38-38.t: He said: ﴿ٱثَّاقَلْتُمْ إِلَى ٱلأَرْضِ﴾, because it is from "تَثاقَلْتُمْ"; the tāʾ was assimilated into the thāʾ, so it became quiescent, and an alif was introduced for it so as to begin the speech with it.

akhfash:40-40.t:
He said: ﴿وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلْعُلْيَا﴾, because He did not construe it with (جَعَلَ) but construed it as a mubtadaʾ.
And He said ﴿ثَانِيَ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾, and likewise (ثالثُ ثلاثةٍ, the third of three); this is the speech of the Arabs. "ثاني واحدٍ" (making one into two) and "ثالثُ اثْنَينِ" (making two into three) are also permissible. In the Book of Allah: ﴿مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجْوَىٰ ثَلاَثَةٍ إِلاَّ هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ وَلاَ خَمْسَةٍ إِلاَّ هُوَ سَادِسُهُمْ﴾; and He said ﴿ثَلاثَةٌ رَّابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ﴾, ﴿خَمْسَةٌ سَادِسُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ﴾ and ﴿سَبْعَةٌ وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ﴾.

akhfash:41-41.t: He said: ﴿ٱنْفِرُواْ خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً﴾, in this ḥāl (circumstance). If you wish, (انفِروا) in the dialect of those who say "يَنْفِر", and if you wish, (انْفُرُوا).

akhfash:43-43.t: He said: ﴿عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنكَ لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ﴾, because it is a question, i.e. "for what reason?".

akhfash:46-46.t: He said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن كَرِهَ ٱللَّهُ ٱنبِعَاثَهُمْ﴾, deriving it from "بَعَثْتُهُ" (I roused him), so "انْبَعَثَ" (he was roused). I have heard from the Arabs someone say: "لَوْ دُعِينا لانْدَعَيْنا" (had we been called, we would have responded). You say: "انْبَعَثَ انَبِعاثاً", i.e. "I roused him" so "he was roused, a rousing". And you say "انْقُطِعَ بِهِ" when he speaks and breaks down, and you do not say "قُطِعَ بِهِ".

akhfash:57-57.t:
He said: ﴿لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَئاً أَوْ مَغَارَاتٍ أَوْ مُدَّخَلاً﴾, because it is from "اِدَّخَلَ" "يَدَّخِلُ". Some read (مَدْخَلا), deriving it from "دَخَلَ" "يَدْخُل", and to my knowledge it is the poorer of the two ways. They mention that in the reading of Ubayy it is (مُنْدَخَلاً), meaning one thing after another. He said ﴿مُغَارَاتٍ﴾ only because it is from "أَغَارَ", so the place is "مُغارٌ". The poet said [in the basīṭ metre, and it is the one hundred and seventy-first poetic witness]:
الحمدُ للهِ مُمْسانَا وَمُصْبَحَنا * بِالخَيْرِ صَبْحَنا رَبِّي وَمَسَّانا
(Praise be to Allah at our evening and our morning; with good has my Lord granted us morning and evening.)
because they are from "أَمْسَى" and "أَصْبَحَ". When you pause on "مَلْجَأ" you say "مَلْجَأَا", because it is an accusative with tanwīn, so you pause with alif, as in your saying "رأيتُ زيدَا".

akhfash:58-58.t: He said: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَلْمِزُكَ﴾, and some read (يَلْمُزُكَ).

akhfash:61-61.t:
He said: ﴿قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَّكُمْ﴾, i.e. he is an ear of good, not an ear of evil. Some read (أُذُنٌ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ), but the first is the better of the two, because if you said "هو أُذُنٌ خَيْرٌ لَكُم" it would not be as good as (هو أَذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَكُم); this is permissible on condition that you make (لكم) an adjective of "الأُذُنْ".
And He said ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِنكُمْ﴾, i.e. "and he is a mercy".
And He said ﴿يُؤْمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَيُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾, i.e. he believes them, just as you say of a man "أَنَا ما يُؤمِنُ لي بأَنْ أَقُولَ كذا وكذا", i.e. he does not believe me.

akhfash:62-62.t:
He said: ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ بِٱللَّهِ لَكُمْ لِيُرْضُوكُمْ﴾ and "سَيَحْلِفُوَن بالله لَكُمِ لِيُرْضُوكُمْ"; I understand it only as meaning "لَيُرضُنَّكُم" (they will surely please you), as the poet said [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-sixth poetic witness]:
إِذا قُلْتُ قَدْنِي قالَ باللهِ حِلْفَةً * لَتُغِنِيَ عَنّي ذا أَنائِكَ أَجْمَعا
(Whenever I say "Enough for me!", he says, swearing an oath by Allah: "You shall surely empty this vessel of yours entirely for me.")
i.e. "لَتُغْنِيَنَّ عني". It is like ﴿وَلِتَصْغَىۤ إِلَيْهِ أَفْئِدَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾, i.e. "ولتُصْغِيَنَّ".

akhfash:63-63.t: He said: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوۤاْ أَنَّهُ مَن يُحَادِدِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ﴾: he gave the alif kasra because what follows the fāʾ that is the apodosis of the conditional begins anew.

akhfash:81-81.t: He said: ﴿فَرِحَ ٱلْمُخَلَّفُونَ بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ خِلاَفَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. "مُخالَفَةً" (in opposition). Some read (خَلْفَ, behind); (خِلافَ) is the more correct of the two because they opposed, like "قَاتَلُوا قِتالا", and because it is the maṣdar of "خَالَفُوا".

akhfash:90-90.t: He said: ﴿وَجَآءَ ٱلْمُعَذِرُونَ﴾, light, because it is from "اَعْذَرُوا". Some read (المُعَذِّرُونَ), doubled, meaning "المُعْتَذرُونَ" (those offering excuses), but the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl, as He said ﴿يَخِصِّمُونَ﴾; and that is how we read. It may be (المُعِذِّرُون) with kasra on the ʿayn because of the meeting of two quiescents; [Translator's note: the source prints «المُعْذِرُون», but the context requires kasra on the ʿayn.] it was given fatḥa only because the fatḥa of the tāʾ was transferred to it. The ʿayn may also take ḍamma, following the mīm; this is like (المُرْدِفِين).

akhfash:98-98.t:
He said: ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دَآئِرَةُ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾, just as you say "هذا رَجُل السَّوْءِ" (this is the man of evil). The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre, and it is the two hundred and twenty-seventh poetic witness]:
وَكُنْتَ كَذِئْبِ السَّوْءِ لَمَّا رَأَى دَماً	* بِصاحِبِه يَوْماً أَحارَ عَلَى الدَّمِ
(You were like the wicked wolf: when one day it saw blood on its companion, it turned upon the blood.)
It has been read (دائِرَةُ السُّوءِ), and this is weak; [Translator's note: the reasoning that follows seems rather to favour «السُّوء» in this phrase; translated as written.] for when you say "كانت عليهم دائرة السُوءِ" it is better than "رجل السَوْءِ". Do you not see that you say "كانت عليهم دائرة الهزيمة" (the turn of defeat was upon them)? For "the man" is not annexed to "evil" as this is annexed, since this is explained by good and evil, as we say "سلكتُ طريقَ الشرَ" (I took the path of evil) and "تركتُ طريقَ الخَيْر" (I abandoned the path of good).

akhfash:100-100.t: He said: ﴿وَٱلسَّابِقُونَ ٱلأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَٱلأَنْصَارِ﴾. Some read (والأَنْصارُ) in the nominative, conjoining it to His words (والسَّابِقُونَ); but the right way is the genitive, because the first forerunners were from both groups together.

akhfash:102-102.t: He said: ﴿خَلَطُواْ عَمَلاً صَالِحاً وَآخَرَ سَيِّئاً﴾. In Arabic it may be [in the sense of] "بآخرَ" (with another), just as you say "اِسْتَوىَ الماءُ والخَشَبَةَ" (the water rose level with the post), i.e. "بالخَشَبَةِ", and "خَلَطْتُ الماءَ واللَّبَنَ" (I mixed the water and the milk), i.e. "بِالَّلبَنِ" (with the milk).

akhfash:103-103.t: He said: ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا﴾. His words ﴿وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا﴾ are a new beginning (ʿalā al-ibtidāʾ); or, if you wish, you may make it an adjective (ṣifa) of "الصدقة" (alms) and then bring بها as emphasis (tawkīd). Likewise (تُطَهِّرُهُم).

akhfash:106-106.t: He said: ﴿وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ﴾, because it is from "أَرْجَأْتُ". Some read (مُرْجَوْنَ) in the dialect of those who say (أَرْجَيْتُ). [Translator's note: the two forms are printed identically in the source; one of them is presumably the hamzated «مُرْجَؤُونَ».]

akhfash:108-108.t: He said: ﴿أُسِّسَ عَلَى ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ مِنْ أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ أَحَقُّ﴾: He means "مُنْذُ أوَّلِ يَوْمٍ" (since the first day), because some Arabs say "لَمْ أَرَهُ مِنْ يَوْمِ كَذا" (I have not seen him from such-and-such a day), meaning "since the first day"; by it he means "from the first of the days", like your saying "لَقِيتُ كُلَّ رَجُلٍ" (I met every man), by which you mean "كُلَّ الرِجّال" (all the men).

akhfash:109-109.t: He said: ﴿هَارٍ فَٱنْهَارَ بِهِ﴾. They mentioned that it is from "يَهُورُ" and is metathesised; its origin is "هائِرٌ"*, but it was metathesised just as "شاكِ السِّلاح" (bristling with weapons) was, [and] it is really "شائِك".

akhfash:110-110.t: He said: ﴿رِيبَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ إِلاَّ أَن تَقَطَّعَ﴾, and (تَقَطَّعَ) in the reading of some; and all are good. [Translator's note: the two forms are printed identically in the source; the variant is presumably «تُقَطَّعَ».]

akhfash:112-112.t: He said: ﴿ٱلتَّائِبُونَ ٱلْعَابِدُونَ..﴾ to the end of the verse, then explained (وَبَشِّرِ المُؤْمِنِينَ); because His words — and Allah knows best — (التائبون) are only an explanation of His words ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشْتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمْ﴾; then He explained and said: "they are those who repent".

akhfash:113-113.t: Then He said: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَن يَسْتَغْفِرُواْ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾; he says: "and they were not to seek forgiveness for the polytheists". And He said ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَن تُؤْمِنَ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. faith was not for it except by Allah's leave.

akhfash:114-114.t: He said: ﴿إِلاَّ عَن مَّوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ﴾: He means "إلاَّ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْعِدَةٍ" (except after a promise), just as you say: "ما كان هذا الشرُّ إلاَّ عَنْ قَوْلٍ كانَ بَيَنْكَمُا" (this trouble came only from words that passed between you two), i.e. it came about from that.

akhfash:117-117.t: He said: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ مَا كَادَ يَزِيغُ قُلُوبُ﴾, and some read (تَزِيغُ). He put an implied noun in (كادَ) and (كادَت), and made "القلوب" nominative by (تَزِيغُ). If you wish you may make it nominative by (كادَ) and make (تَزِيغُ) a ḥāl (circumstantial); or, if you wish, you may treat it as resembling "كانَ", implying a noun in (كادَ) and putting (تَزِيغُ قلوبُ) in the position of the khabar (predicate).

akhfash:118-118.t: He said: ﴿وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَن لاَّ مَلْجَأَ﴾: it is like this when you pause on it, and you do not say (ملجأ ا), because there is no nūn [tanwīn] here. Do you not see that if you paused on "لا خَوْفَ" you would not add an alif? As for "لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَأَا", pausing on it is with alif because the accusative in it has tanwīn.

akhfash:123-123.t: He said: ﴿وَلِيَجِدُواْ فِيكُمْ غِلْظَةً﴾, and that is how we read; some read (غُلْظَةَ). They are two dialects.

akhfash:124-124.t: He said: ﴿أَيُّكُمْ زَادَتْهُ هَـٰذِهِ إِيمَاناً﴾: "أيّ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), because the verb has fallen on the hāʾ. If you say: "Why not imply a verb at its beginning, as He said ﴿أَبَشَراً مِّنَّا وَاحِداً﴾?" — it is because before "بشر" there is an interrogative particle, which has more claim to a verb, whereas (أيّ) makes the interrogative particle unnecessary, so nothing with more claim to a verb comes before it; so it became like your saying "زيدٌ ضَرْبتُه" (Zayd, I struck him). Whoever puts "زيداً ضربُته" in the accusative in a statement would put "أيّ" in the accusative here.

akhfash:127-127.t: He said: ﴿نَّظَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ مِّنْ أَحَدٍ﴾. It is as though He said "some of them said to others", because their looking in this place was a gesture or something like it; and Allah knows best.

akhfash:128-128.t: He said: ﴿عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾: He made (ما) a noun and (عَنِتُّم) part of its ṣila (relative clause).

celaleyn:1-1.t: The basmala was not written in it because he ﷺ was not commanded to do so, as is taken from a hadith narrated by al-Ḥākim. He also transmitted in the same sense from ʿAlī that the basmala is a guarantee of safety, whereas it [Translator's note: this surah] was revealed to lift safety by the sword; and from Ḥudhayfa: "You call it Sūrat al-Tawba, but it is the Surah of Punishment." Al-Bukhārī narrated from al-Barāʾ that it was the last surah to be revealed. This is ﴿بَرَاءَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ reaching ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ عَاهَدْتُمْ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ an unrestricted covenant, or one of less than four months or more than that, and [Translator's note: who] broke the covenant, with what is mentioned in His saying:

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿فَسِيحُوا﴾ travel in safety, O idolaters, ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ﴾ the first of which is Shawwāl, as evidenced by what will come, and there is no safety for you after them; ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِي اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. escaping His punishment, ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْزِي الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ humiliating them in this world by killing and in the next by the Fire.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَأَذَانٌ﴾ an announcement ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ إِلَى النَّاسِ يَوْمَ الْحَجِّ الْأَكْبَرِ﴾ the Day of Sacrifice, ﴿أَنَّ﴾ i.e. that ﴿اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ and their covenants, ﴿وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ is also free [Translator's note: of them]. The Prophet ﷺ sent ʿAlī in that year — the year nine — and he announced these ayahs on the Day of Sacrifice at Minā, and that no idolater should make pilgrimage after this year and no naked person circumambulate the House. Narrated by al-Bukhārī. ﴿فَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ﴾ from unbelief, ﴿فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ from faith, ﴿فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِي اللَّهِ وَبَشِّرِ﴾ inform ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ painful, namely killing and capture in this world and the Fire in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ عَاهَدْتُمْ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنْقُصُوكُمْ شَيْئًا﴾ of the terms of the covenant ﴿وَلَمْ يُظَاهِرُوا﴾ aid ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ أَحَدًا﴾ of the unbelievers; ﴿فَأَتِمُّوا إِلَيْهِمْ عَهْدَهُمْ إِلَى﴾ the expiry of ﴿مُدَّتِهِمْ﴾ which you agreed with them. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ by fulfilling covenants.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿فَإِذَا انْسَلَخَ﴾ has passed ﴿الْأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُمُ﴾ which is the end of the period of respite, ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ outside or inside the Sanctuary, ﴿وَخُذُوهُمْ﴾ captive ﴿وَاحْصُرُوهُمْ﴾ in castles and fortresses until they are compelled to [Translator's note: choose between] being killed or Islam, ﴿وَاقْعُدُوا لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ﴾ every road they travel — the accusative of كُلَّ is by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿فَإِنْ تَابُوا﴾ from unbelief ﴿وَأَقَامُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَوةَ فَخَلُّوا سَبِيلَهُمْ﴾ and do not interfere with them. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ to whoever repents.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ nominative (marfūʿ) by a verb that is explained by ﴿اسْتَجَارَكَ﴾ seeks your protection from being killed, ﴿فَأَجِرْهُ﴾ grant him safety ﴿حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ﴾ the Quran, ﴿ثُمَّ أَبْلِغْهُ مَأْمَنَهُ﴾ that is, his place of safety, namely the land of his people, if he does not believe, so that he may consider his affair. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ what has been mentioned ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the religion of Allah, so they must hear the Quran in order to know.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ i.e. there shall not ﴿يَكُونُ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ عَهْدٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَعِنْدَ رَسُولِهِ﴾ while they disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger and are treacherous, ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ عَاهَدْتُمْ عِنْدَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ on the day of al-Ḥudaybiya — they are Quraysh, the ones excepted earlier. ﴿فَمَا اسْتَقَامُوا لَكُمْ﴾ keep to the covenant and do not break it, ﴿فَاسْتَقِيمُوا لَهُمْ﴾ in fulfilling it; مَا is conditional. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ The Prophet ﷺ kept to his covenant with them until they broke it by aiding the Banū Bakr against Khuzāʿa.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ can they have a covenant, ﴿وَإِنْ يَظْهَرُوا عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ gain victory over you, ﴿لَا يَرْقُبُوا﴾ they do not respect ﴿فِيكُمْ إِلًّا﴾ kinship ﴿وَلَا ذِمَّةً﴾ covenant; rather they harm you as much as they can. The conditional clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿يُرْضُونَكُمْ بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ with their fine words, ﴿وَتَأْبَى قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ fulfilling it; ﴿وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ فَاسِقُونَ﴾ breakers of the covenant.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿اشْتَرَوْا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Quran ﴿ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا﴾ of this world, i.e. they abandoned following them for lusts and caprice, ﴿فَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ﴾ His religion. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ سَاءَ﴾ evil is ﴿مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ — it [Translator's note: the suffix هُ completing "يَعْمَلُونَ"], this deed of theirs.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿لَا يَرْقُبُونَ فِي مُؤْمِنٍ إِلًّا وَلَا ذِمَّةً وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُعْتَدُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿فَإِنْ تَابُوا وَأَقَامُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَوةَ فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ﴾ i.e. then they are your brothers ﴿فِي الدِّينِ وَنُفَصِّلُ﴾ We make clear ﴿الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ who reflect.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَإِنْ نَكَثُوا﴾ break ﴿أَيْمَانَهُمْ﴾ their pledges ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ عَهْدِهِمْ وَطَعَنُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ﴾ find fault with it, ﴿فَقَاتِلُوا أَئِمَّةَ الْكُفْرِ﴾ its chiefs — in it the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun — ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لَا أَيْمَانَ﴾ covenants ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ — and in one reading with kasra [Translator's note: إِيمَانَ, "faith"] — ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَنْتَهُونَ﴾ from unbelief.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿أَلَا﴾ for urging (taḥḍīḍ) ﴿تُقَاتِلُونَ قَوْمًا نَكَثُوا﴾ broke ﴿أَيْمَانَهُمْ﴾ their covenants ﴿وَهَمُّوا بِإِخْرَاجِ الرَّسُولِ﴾ from Mecca, when they consulted about him in the Dār al-Nadwa, ﴿وَهُمْ بَدَءُوكُمْ﴾ with fighting ﴿أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ when they fought Khuzāʿa, your allies, together with the Banū Bakr? So what prevents you from fighting them? ﴿أَتَخْشَوْنَهُمْ﴾ do you fear them? ﴿فَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَخْشَوْهُ﴾ in abandoning fighting them, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿قَاتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ by killing them ﴿بِأَيْدِيكُمْ وَيُخْزِهِمْ﴾ humiliate them by capture and subjugation ﴿وَيَنْصُرْكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَيَشْفِ صُدُورَ قَوْمٍ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ by what is done to them — they are the Banū Khuzāʿa —

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَيُذْهِبْ غَيْظَ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ their anguish. ﴿وَيَتُوبُ اللَّهُ عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ by returning to Islam, like Abū Sufyān. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ in the sense of the hamza of disapproving denial (inkār) ﴿حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تُتْرَكُوا وَلَمَّا﴾ not ﴿يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ﴾ with the knowledge of manifestation ﴿الَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ﴾ with sincerity ﴿وَلَمْ يَتَّخِذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلَا رَسُولِهِ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَلِيجَةً﴾ intimates and allies? The meaning is: and the sincere — those described by what was mentioned — have not yet been made manifest [Translator's note: as distinct] from the others. ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ أَنْ يَعْمُرُوا مَسْجِدَ اللَّهِ﴾ in the singular and in the plural [مَسَاجِدَ], by entering it and sitting in it, ﴿شَاهِدِينَ عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ بِالْكُفْرِ أُولَئِكَ حَبِطَتْ﴾ are void ﴿أَعْمَالُهُمْ﴾ for lack of their condition, ﴿وَفِي النَّارِ هُمْ خَالِدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَعْمُرُ مَسَاجِدَ اللَّهِ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَأَقَامَ الصَّلَوةَ وَآتَى الزَّكَوةَ وَلَمْ يَخْشَ﴾ anyone ﴿إِلَّا اللَّهَ فَعَسَى أُولَئِكَ أَنْ يَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿أَجَعَلْتُمْ سِقَايَةَ الْحَاجِّ وَعِمَارَةَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ i.e. the people of that, ﴿كَمَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَجَاهَدَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَا يَسْتَوُونَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ in merit. ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the unbelievers. It was revealed in reply to whoever said that, namely al-ʿAbbās or someone else.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَهَاجَرُوا وَجَاهَدُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً﴾ rank ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ than others; ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَائِزُونَ﴾ those who attain the good.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿يُبَشِّرُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنْهُ وَرِضْوَانٍ وَجَنَّاتٍ لَهُمْ فِيهَا نَعِيمٌ مُقِيمٌ﴾ lasting,

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿خَالِدِينَ﴾ an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial of what is yet to be) ﴿فِيهَا أَبَدًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ And there was revealed concerning those who abandoned emigration for the sake of their families and their trade:

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا آبَاءَكُمْ وَإِخْوَانَكُمْ أَوْلِيَاءَ إِنِ اسْتَحَبُّوا﴾ choose ﴿الْكُفْرَ عَلَى الْإِيمَانِ وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ مِنْكُمْ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنْ كَانَ آبَاؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَاؤُكُمْ وَإِخْوَانُكُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُكُمْ وَعَشِيرَتُكُمْ﴾ your relatives — and in one reading [عَشِيرَاتُكُمْ] — ﴿وَأَمْوَالٌ اقْتَرَفْتُمُوهَا﴾ you have acquired ﴿وَتِجَارَةٌ تَخْشَوْنَ كَسَادَهَا﴾ its not selling ﴿وَمَسَاكِنُ تَرْضَوْنَهَا أَحَبَّ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَجِهَادٍ فِي سَبِيلِهِ﴾ so that you stayed behind from emigration and jihad because of it, ﴿فَتَرَبَّصُوا﴾ wait ﴿حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ اللَّهُ بِأَمْرِهِ﴾ a threat to them. ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿لَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي مَوَاطِنَ﴾ of war ﴿كَثِيرَةٍ﴾ such as Badr, Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr, ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿يَوْمَ حُنَيْنٍ﴾ a valley between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif, i.e. the day you fought Hawāzin in it, and that was in Shawwāl of the year eight, ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for يَوْمَ, ﴿أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ كَثْرَتُكُمْ﴾ so you said: "We shall not be defeated today for lack of numbers"; they were twelve thousand and the unbelievers four thousand. ﴿فَلَمْ تُغْنِ عَنْكُمْ شَيْئًا وَضَاقَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْأَرْضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتْ﴾ مَا is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar, verbal noun), i.e. despite its spaciousness, i.e. its breadth, so you found no place in which to feel secure, because of the severity of the fear that befell you; ﴿ثُمَّ وَلَّيْتُمْ مُدْبِرِينَ﴾ routed. The Prophet ﷺ stood firm on his white mule, with no one with him but al-ʿAbbās, and Abū Sufyān holding his stirrup.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ﴾ His reassurance ﴿عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ so they were brought back to the Prophet ﷺ when al-ʿAbbās called them with his permission, and they fought; ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ جُنُودًا لَمْ تَرَوْهَا﴾ angels, ﴿وَعَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ by killing and capture; ﴿وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿ثُمَّ يَتُوبُ اللَّهُ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ of them, through Islam. ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْمُشْرِكُونَ نَجَسٌ﴾ filth, because of the foulness of their inner selves, ﴿فَلَا يَقْرَبُوا الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ﴾ i.e. let them not enter the Sanctuary ﴿بَعْدَ عَامِهِمْ هَذَا﴾ the year nine of the Hijra. ﴿وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ عَيْلَةً﴾ poverty, through the cutting off of their trade with you, ﴿فَسَوْفَ يُغْنِيكُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ إِنْ شَاءَ﴾ and He did enrich them through the conquests and the jizya. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿قَاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا بِالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ otherwise they would have believed in the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿وَلَا يُحَرِّمُونَ مَا حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ such as wine, ﴿وَلَا يَدِينُونَ دِينَ الْحَقِّ﴾ the firmly established one that abrogates the other religions, namely the religion of Islam, ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ an explication (bayān) of الَّذِينَ, ﴿أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ i.e. the Jews and the Christians, ﴿حَتَّى يُعْطُوا الْجِزْيَةَ﴾ the tribute imposed on them each year, ﴿عَنْ يَدٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. submitting, or with their own hands, not delegating it, ﴿وَهُمْ صَاغِرُونَ﴾ humbled, submitting to the rule of Islam.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ عُزَيْرٌ ابْنُ اللَّهِ وَقَالَتِ النَّصَارَى الْمَسِيحُ﴾ Jesus ﴿ابْنُ اللَّهِ ذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُمْ بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ they have no support for it; rather ﴿يُضَاهِئُونَ﴾ they imitate by it ﴿قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ of their forefathers, in blind imitation of them. ﴿قَاتَلَهُمُ﴾ may He curse them, ﴿اللَّهُ أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ are they turned away from the truth despite the proof being established!

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا أَحْبَارَهُمْ﴾ the scholars of the Jews ﴿وَرُهْبَانَهُمْ﴾ the devotees of the Christians ﴿أَرْبَابًا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ in that they followed them in making lawful what He had forbidden and forbidding what He had made lawful, ﴿وَالْمَسِيحَ ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَمَا أُمِرُوا﴾ in the Torah and the Gospel ﴿إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا﴾ i.e. to worship ﴿إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ as a declaration of His transcendence ﴿عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يُطْفِئُوا نُورَ اللَّهِ﴾ His law and His proofs ﴿بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ with their sayings about it, ﴿وَيَأْبَى اللَّهُ إِلَّا أَنْ يُتِمَّ﴾ make manifest ﴿نُورَهُ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ﴾ Muḥammad ﷺ ﴿بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ﴾ raise it high ﴿عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾ all the religions opposed to it, ﴿وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْأَحْبَارِ وَالرُّهْبَانِ لَيَأْكُلُونَ﴾ take ﴿أَمْوَالَ النَّاسِ بِالْبَاطِلِ﴾ such as bribes in judgement, ﴿وَيَصُدُّونَ﴾ people ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿يَكْنِزُونَ الذَّهَبَ وَالْفِضَّةَ وَلَا يُنْفِقُونَهَا﴾ i.e. the hoards ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. they do not pay from them what is due to Him of zakat and good, ﴿فَبَشِّرْهُمْ﴾ inform them ﴿بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ painful,

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُحْمَى عَلَيْهَا فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ فَتُكْوَى﴾ are burned ﴿بِهَا جِبَاهُهُمْ وَجُنُوبُهُمْ وَظُهُورُهُمْ﴾ and their skins are stretched until all of it is placed upon them, and it is said to them: ﴿هَذَا مَا كَنَزْتُمْ لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ فَذُوقُوا مَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْنِزُونَ﴾ i.e. its recompense.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿إِنَّ عِدَّةَ الشُّهُورِ﴾ reckoned for the year ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ اثْنَا عَشَرَ شَهْرًا فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Preserved Tablet, ﴿يَوْمَ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ مِنْهَا﴾ i.e. of the months ﴿أَرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ﴾ sacred: they are Dhū al-Qaʿda, Dhū al-Ḥijja, al-Muḥarram and Rajab. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. their sacredness ﴿الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ﴾ the straight. ﴿فَلَا تَظْلِمُوا فِيهِنَّ﴾ i.e. the sacred months ﴿أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ by acts of disobedience, for in them they are a greater burden of sin; and it is said: in all the months. ﴿وَقَاتِلُوا الْمُشْرِكِينَ كَافَّةً﴾ all together, in all the months, ﴿كَمَا يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ كَافَّةً وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ with help and victory.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا النَّسِيءُ﴾ i.e. postponing the sacredness of one month to another, as the people of the Jāhiliyya used to do, postponing the sacredness of al-Muḥarram, when it arrived while they were engaged in fighting, to Ṣafar, ﴿زِيَادَةٌ فِي الْكُفْرِ﴾ because of their disbelief in Allah's ruling about it; ﴿يُضَلُّ﴾ with ḍamma and fatḥa on the yāʾ ﴿بِهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُحِلُّونَهُ﴾ i.e. the postponed month ﴿عَامًا وَيُحَرِّمُونَهُ عَامًا لِيُوَاطِئُوا﴾ to agree, by making one month lawful and making another sacred in its place, with ﴿عِدَّةَ﴾ the number ﴿مَا حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ﴾ of months, so they do not go above declaring four sacred nor below it, and they pay no attention to which ones they are, ﴿فَيُحِلُّوا مَا حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ زُيِّنَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ أَعْمَالِهِمْ﴾ so they thought it good. ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ And there was revealed, when the Prophet ﷺ called the people to the campaign of Tabūk while they were in hardship and intense heat, and it was hard on them:

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَا لَكُمْ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمُ انْفِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ اثَّاقَلْتُمْ﴾ with assimilation (idghām) of the tāʾ, originally [تَثَاقَلْتُمْ], into the thāʾ, and the bringing in of the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl), i.e. you were sluggish and inclined away from jihad ﴿إِلَى الْأَرْضِ﴾ and sitting on it? The interrogative is for rebuke. ﴿أَرَضِيتُمْ بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ and its pleasures ﴿مِنَ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. in place of its bliss? ﴿فَمَا مَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا فِي﴾ comparison with the enjoyment of ﴿الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ﴾ paltry.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾ with assimilation of لَا into the nūn of the conditional إِنْ, in both places, ﴿تَنْفِرُوا﴾ go out with the Prophet ﷺ to jihad, ﴿يُعَذِّبْكُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ painful ﴿وَيَسْتَبْدِلْ قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ﴾ i.e. bring them in your place, ﴿وَلَا تَضُرُّوهُ﴾ i.e. Allah, or the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ by abandoning support of him, for Allah is the Supporter of His religion. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ and part of that is supporting His religion and His Prophet.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿إِلَّا تَنْصُرُوهُ﴾ i.e. the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ إِذْ﴾ when ﴿أَخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ from Mecca, i.e. forced him to leave, when they intended to kill him, imprison him or banish him, in the Dār al-Nadwa, ﴿ثَانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. one of two, the other being Abū Bakr. The meaning is: Allah supported him in such a state, so He will not forsake him in any other. ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the إِذْ before it ﴿هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ﴾ a hollow in Mount Thawr, ﴿إِذْ﴾ a second badal ﴿يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ﴾ Abū Bakr, who had said to him, when he saw the feet of the idolaters: "If one of them looked beneath his feet he would see us": ﴿لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا﴾ with His support. ﴿فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ﴾ His reassurance ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ it is said: upon the Prophet ﷺ; and it is said: upon Abū Bakr; ﴿وَأَيَّدَهُ﴾ i.e. the Prophet ﷺ ﴿بِجُنُودٍ لَمْ تَرَوْهَا﴾ angels, in the cave and in the places of his fighting, ﴿وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ i.e. the call of idolatry ﴿السُّفْلَى﴾ the vanquished, ﴿وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. the word of testimony [Translator's note: that there is no god but Allah] ﴿هِيَ الْعُلْيَا﴾ the manifest, the prevailing. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ﴾ in His dominion, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿انْفِرُوا خِفَافًا وَثِقَالًا﴾ eager and not eager; it is also said: strong and weak, or rich and poor. It is abrogated by the ayah {لَيْسَ عَلَى الضُّعَفَاءِ} ("There is no blame on the weak"). ﴿وَجَاهِدُوا بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that it is better for you; so do not be sluggish. And there was revealed concerning the hypocrites who stayed behind:

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ﴾ what you called them to ﴿عَرَضًا﴾ a worldly good ﴿قَرِيبًا﴾ easy to obtain, ﴿وَسَفَرًا قَاصِدًا﴾ moderate, ﴿لَاتَّبَعُوكَ﴾ seeking booty; ﴿وَلَكِنْ بَعُدَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الشُّقَّةُ﴾ the distance, so they stayed behind. ﴿وَسَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ﴾ when you return to them: ﴿لَوِ اسْتَطَعْنَا﴾ to go out ﴿لَخَرَجْنَا مَعَكُمْ يُهْلِكُونَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ by false swearing; ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ in that saying of theirs. He ﷺ had given leave to a group to stay behind, by his own reasoning (ijtihād), so this was revealed as a reproach to him, and pardon was put first to reassure his heart:

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْكَ لِمَ أَذِنْتَ لَهُمْ﴾ to stay behind? Why did you not leave them ﴿حَتَّى يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكَ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا﴾ in their excuse ﴿وَتَعْلَمَ الْكَاذِبِينَ﴾ in it?

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿لَا يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ to stay behind from ﴿أَنْ يُجَاهِدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالْمُتَّقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَسْتَأْذِنُكَ﴾ to stay behind ﴿الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَارْتَابَتْ﴾ have doubted ﴿قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ in religion, ﴿فَهُمْ فِي رَيْبِهِمْ يَتَرَدَّدُونَ﴾ are perplexed.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَرَادُوا الْخُرُوجَ﴾ with you ﴿لَأَعَدُّوا لَهُ عُدَّةً﴾ preparation of equipment and provisions; ﴿وَلَكِنْ كَرِهَ اللَّهُ انْبِعَاثَهُمْ﴾ i.e. He did not will their going out, ﴿فَثَبَّطَهُمْ﴾ made them lazy, ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ to them: ﴿اقْعُدُوا مَعَ الْقَاعِدِينَ﴾ the sick, the women and the children; i.e. Allah the Exalted decreed that.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿لَوْ خَرَجُوا فِيكُمْ مَا زَادُوكُمْ إِلَّا خَبَالًا﴾ corruption, by making the believers lose heart, ﴿وَلَأَوْضَعُوا خِلَالَكُمْ﴾ i.e. they would have hurried about among you spreading slander, ﴿يَبْغُونَكُمْ﴾ seeking for you ﴿الْفِتْنَةَ﴾ by casting enmity; ﴿وَفِيكُمْ سَمَّاعُونَ لَهُمْ﴾ what they say, with a hearing of acceptance. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿لَقَدِ ابْتَغَوُا﴾ for you ﴿الْفِتْنَةَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ when you first came to Medina, ﴿وَقَلَّبُوا لَكَ الْأُمُورَ﴾ i.e. turned over their thoughts in plotting against you and nullifying your religion, ﴿حَتَّى جَاءَ الْحَقُّ﴾ the victory, ﴿وَظَهَرَ﴾ became mighty ﴿أَمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion, ﴿وَهُمْ كَارِهُونَ﴾ of it; so they entered it outwardly.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ ائْذَنْ لِي﴾ to stay behind ﴿وَلَا تَفْتِنِّي﴾ — he was al-Jadd ibn Qays. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Would you like to fight the Banū al-Aṣfar [Translator's note: the Byzantines]?" He said: "I am infatuated with women, and I fear that if I see the women of the Banū al-Aṣfar I will not be able to restrain myself from them and will be tempted." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿أَلَا فِي الْفِتْنَةِ سَقَطُوا﴾ by staying behind — and it has been read سَقَطَ — ﴿وَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمُحِيطَةٌ بِالْكَافِرِينَ﴾ they have no escape from it.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿إِنْ تُصِبْكَ حَسَنَةٌ﴾ such as victory and booty, ﴿تَسُؤْهُمْ وَإِنْ تُصِبْكَ مُصِيبَةٌ﴾ a hardship, ﴿يَقُولُوا قَدْ أَخَذْنَا أَمْرَنَا﴾ with prudence when we stayed behind ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ before this calamity, ﴿وَيَتَوَلَّوْا وَهُمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾ at what has befallen you.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿لَنْ يُصِيبَنَا إِلَّا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَنَا﴾ that it befall [Translator's note: us]; ﴿هُوَ مَوْلَانَا﴾ our Helper and the One in charge of our affairs; ﴿وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ تَرَبَّصُونَ﴾ in it one of the two tāʾs of the original form is omitted, i.e. do you wait for — i.e. [Translator's note: for] there to befall ﴿بِنَا إِلَّا إِحْدَى﴾ the two outcomes, ﴿الْحُسْنَيَيْنِ﴾ the dual of حُسْنَى, the feminine of أَحْسَنَ: victory or martyrdom? ﴿وَنَحْنُ نَتَرَبَّصُ﴾ we wait ﴿بِكُمْ أَنْ يُصِيبَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِعَذَابٍ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ﴾ with a calamity from the sky, ﴿أَوْ بِأَيْدِينَا﴾ by our being given leave to fight you. ﴿فَتَرَبَّصُوا﴾ that for us; ﴿إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُتَرَبِّصُونَ﴾ your outcome.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿قُلْ أَنْفِقُوا﴾ in obedience to Allah ﴿طَوْعًا أَوْ كَرْهًا لَنْ يُتَقَبَّلَ مِنْكُمْ﴾ what you have spent; ﴿إِنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا فَاسِقِينَ﴾. The imperative here has the meaning of a statement (khabar).

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَهُمْ أَنْ تُقْبَلَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ ﴿مِنْهُمْ نَفَقَاتُهُمْ إِلَّا أَنَّهُمْ﴾ — the fāʿil (agent), while أَنْ تُقْبَلَ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) — ﴿كَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ وَبِرَسُولِهِ وَلَا يَأْتُونَ الصَّلَوةَ إِلَّا وَهُمْ كُسَالَى﴾ sluggish, ﴿وَلَا يُنْفِقُونَ إِلَّا وَهُمْ كَارِهُونَ﴾ spending, because they count it a loss.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿فَلَا تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُهُمْ﴾ i.e. do not think well of Our blessings upon them, for they are a gradual leading on [Translator's note: to ruin] (istidrāj). ﴿إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ﴾ i.e. to punish them ﴿بِهَا فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ by the hardship they meet in amassing them and the calamities in them, ﴿وَتَزْهَقَ﴾ depart ﴿أَنْفُسُهُمْ وَهُمْ كَافِرُونَ﴾ so He will punish them in the Hereafter with the severest punishment.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُمْ لَمِنْكُمْ﴾ i.e. believers, ﴿وَمَا هُمْ مِنْكُمْ وَلَكِنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ يَفْرَقُونَ﴾ they fear that you will do to them as [Translator's note: you did] to the idolaters, so they swear out of dissimulation (taqiyya).

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿لَوْ يَجِدُونَ مَلْجَأً﴾ to take refuge in, ﴿أَوْ مَغَارَاتٍ﴾ underground tunnels, ﴿أَوْ مُدَّخَلًا﴾ a place to enter, ﴿لَوَلَّوْا إِلَيْهِ وَهُمْ يَجْمَحُونَ﴾ hurrying to enter it and to turn away from you, a haste which nothing can turn back, like a runaway horse.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَلْمِزُكَ﴾ finds fault with you ﴿فِي﴾ the distribution of ﴿الصَّدَقَاتِ فَإِنْ أُعْطُوا مِنْهَا رَضُوا وَإِنْ لَمْ يُعْطَوْا مِنْهَا إِذَا هُمْ يَسْخَطُونَ﴾

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ رَضُوا مَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ of the spoils and the like, ﴿وَقَالُوا حَسْبُنَا﴾ sufficient for us is ﴿اللَّهُ سَيُؤْتِينَا اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ from another booty, what suffices us; ﴿إِنَّا إِلَى اللَّهِ رَاغِبُونَ﴾ that He enrich us — and the answer of لَوْ is: "it would have been better for them".

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا الصَّدَقَاتُ﴾ the zakats, are to be disbursed ﴿لِلْفُقَرَاءِ﴾ who do not find what makes any substantial contribution to their sufficiency, ﴿وَالْمَسَاكِينِ﴾ who do not find what suffices them, ﴿وَالْعَامِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا﴾ i.e. on the alms: collector, distributor, scribe and gatherer, ﴿وَالْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ so that they become Muslim, or their Islam becomes firm, or their peers become Muslim, or they defend the Muslims — [Translator's note: these are] categories; the first and the last are not given today according to al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, because of the might of Islam, unlike the other two, who are given according to the soundest view; ﴿وَفِي﴾ the freeing of ﴿الرِّقَابِ﴾ i.e. slaves contracted for manumission (mukātabūn), ﴿وَالْغَارِمِينَ﴾ the indebted, if they borrowed for other than disobedience, or repented, and have nothing to repay with, or [Translator's note: borrowed] to reconcile between people, even if they are rich; ﴿وَفِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. those engaged in jihad who have no share of the fayʾ (state revenue), even if they are rich; ﴿وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ the one stranded on his journey. ﴿فَرِيضَةً﴾ accusative (manṣūb) by its implied (muqaddar) verb, ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of His creation, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making. So it is not permissible to disburse it to other than these, nor to withhold it from any category of them if it exists; the imam divides it among them equally, and he may favour some individuals of a category over others. The lām conveys the obligation of covering all its individuals; but that is not obligatory on the owner of the wealth when he distributes it himself, because of its difficulty; rather it suffices to give three of each category, and fewer does not suffice, as the plural form indicates. The Sunna has made clear that the condition of the one given from it is Islam, and that he not be a Hāshimī or a Muṭṭalibī.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the hypocrites ﴿الَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ النَّبِيَّ﴾ by finding fault with him and passing on his talk, ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ when they are forbidden to do that lest it reach him: ﴿هُوَ أُذُنٌ﴾ i.e. he hears everything said and accepts it, so if we swear to him that we did not say it, he believes us. ﴿قُلْ﴾ he is ﴿أُذُنٌ﴾ a listener to ﴿خَيْرٍ لَكُمْ﴾ not a listener to evil; ﴿يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَيُؤْمِنُ﴾ believes ﴿لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in what they inform him of, not others — the lām is redundant (zāʾida), to distinguish between the belief of acceptance and other [Translator's note: belief] — ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾ in the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أُذُنٌ, and in the genitive [رَحْمَةٍ], conjoined to خَيْرٍ, ﴿لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْذُونَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ لَكُمْ﴾ O believers, concerning what has reached you of their harming the Messenger, that they did not do it, ﴿لِيُرْضُوكُمْ وَاللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُرْضُوهُ﴾ by obedience, ﴿إِنْ كَانُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ truly. The pronoun is singular because the two pleasings are inseparable; or else the khabar (predicate) of "اللَّهُ" or of "رَسُولُهُ" is omitted.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the matter (al-shaʾn) [Translator's note: is that] ﴿مَنْ يُحَادِدِ﴾ opposes ﴿اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَأَنَّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ as recompense, ﴿خَالِدًا فِيهَا ذَلِكَ الْخِزْيُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿يَحْذَرُ﴾ fear ﴿الْمُنَافِقُونَ أَنْ تُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. the believers ﴿سُورَةٌ تُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ of hypocrisy — and yet with that they mock. ﴿قُلِ اسْتَهْزِئُوا﴾ an imperative of threat; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْرِجٌ﴾ will bring to light ﴿مَا تَحْذَرُونَ﴾ its being brought out, of your hypocrisy.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the lām of the oath ﴿سَأَلْتَهُمْ﴾ about their mocking you and the Quran while they were travelling with you to Tabūk, ﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ﴾ excusing themselves: ﴿إِنَّمَا كُنَّا نَخُوضُ وَنَلْعَبُ﴾ in talk, to while away the road with it, and we did not mean that. ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿أَبِاللَّهِ وَآيَاتِهِ وَرَسُولِهِ كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿لَا تَعْتَذِرُوا﴾ for it; ﴿قَدْ كَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ﴾ i.e. your unbelief has become manifest after your professing faith. ﴿إِنْ يُعْفَ﴾ with yāʾ, passive, and with nūn [نَعْفُ], active, ﴿عَنْ طَائِفَةٍ مِنْكُمْ﴾ because of its sincerity and repentance, like Makhshī ibn Ḥumayyir, ﴿تُعَذَّبْ﴾ with tāʾ and with nūn [نُعَذِّبْ] ﴿طَائِفَةٌ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ persisting in hypocrisy and mockery [طَائِفَةً] [Translator's note: i.e. with the nūn reading نُعَذِّبْ, طَائِفَةً is read in the accusative.].

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿الْمُنَافِقُونَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتُ بَعْضُهُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ i.e. alike in religion, like the parts of a single thing. ﴿يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمُنْكَرِ﴾ unbelief and acts of disobedience ﴿وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ faith and obedience ﴿وَيَقْبِضُونَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾ from spending in obedience. ﴿نَسُوا اللَّهَ﴾ abandoned obedience to Him, ﴿فَنَسِيَهُمْ﴾ He left them out of His kindness. ﴿إِنَّ الْمُنَافِقِينَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتِ وَالْكُفَّارَ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا هِيَ حَسْبُهُمْ﴾ as recompense and punishment; ﴿وَلَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ He has put them far from His mercy, ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُقِيمٌ﴾ lasting.

celaleyn:69-69.t: You, O hypocrites, are ﴿كَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ كَانُوا أَشَدَّ مِنْكُمْ قُوَّةً وَأَكْثَرَ أَمْوَالًا وَأَوْلَادًا فَاسْتَمْتَعُوا﴾ enjoyed ﴿بِخَلَاقِهِمْ﴾ their share of this world, ﴿فَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ﴾ O hypocrites, ﴿بِخَلَاقِكُمْ كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ بِخَلَاقِهِمْ وَخُضْتُمْ﴾ in falsehood and in reviling the Prophet ﷺ ﴿كَالَّذِي خَاضُوا﴾ i.e. as they indulged. ﴿أُولَئِكَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَأْتِهِمْ نَبَأُ﴾ the news of ﴿الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعَادٍ﴾ the people of Hūd ﴿وَثَمُودَ﴾ the people of Ṣāliḥ ﴿وَقَوْمِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَأَصْحَابِ مَدْيَنَ﴾ the people of Shuʿayb ﴿وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَاتِ﴾ the towns of the people of Lūṭ, i.e. their inhabitants? ﴿أَتَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُمْ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ with miracles, but they gave them the lie and were destroyed. ﴿فَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ﴾ by punishing them without a sin, ﴿وَلَكِنْ كَانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ by committing sin.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتُ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَيُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَوةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَوةَ وَيُطِيعُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ أُولَئِكَ سَيَرْحَمُهُمُ اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾ nothing prevents Him from fulfilling His promise and His threat, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ He puts nothing anywhere but in its proper place.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَمَسَاكِنَ طَيِّبَةً فِي جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾ abiding residence; ﴿وَرِضْوَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ﴾ greater than all of that; ﴿ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ جَاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ﴾ with the sword ﴿وَالْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ with the tongue and with argument, ﴿وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ with rebuke and loathing; ﴿وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ the place of return — it [Translator's note: i.e. هِيَ, the one specified for blame, is Hell].

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ﴾ i.e. the hypocrites ﴿بِاللَّهِ مَا قَالُوا﴾ what reached you from them of abuse; ﴿وَلَقَدْ قَالُوا كَلِمَةَ الْكُفْرِ وَكَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِسْلَامِهِمْ﴾ they showed unbelief after showing Islam, ﴿وَهَمُّوا بِمَا لَمْ يَنَالُوا﴾ of assassinating the Prophet on the night of al-ʿAqaba on his return from Tabūk — they were some ten-odd men — and ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir struck the faces of the mounts when they closed in on him, so they were driven back. ﴿وَمَا نَقَمُوا﴾ they found nothing objectionable ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ أَغْنَاهُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ with the spoils, after their dire need; the meaning is: nothing reached them from him but this, and this is not something to be resented. ﴿فَإِنْ يَتُوبُوا﴾ from hypocrisy and believe in you, ﴿يَكُ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ وَإِنْ يَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ from faith, ﴿يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا فِي الدُّنْيَا﴾ by killing ﴿وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ by the Fire; ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ﴾ to protect them from it ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرٍ﴾ to defend them.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ عَاهَدَ اللَّهَ لَئِنْ آتَانَا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ﴾ in it the tāʾ of the original form is assimilated (idghām) into the ṣād, ﴿وَلَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ — he was Thaʿlaba ibn Ḥāṭib. He asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray for him that Allah would grant him wealth, and that he would pay from it to everyone with a due his due. So he prayed for him, and he was given abundance; then he stopped attending the Friday prayer and the congregation and withheld zakat, as Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا آتَاهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ بَخِلُوا بِهِ وَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ from obedience to Allah, ﴿وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿فَأَعْقَبَهُمْ﴾ i.e. so He made their outcome ﴿نِفَاقًا﴾ firmly fixed ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ i.e. Allah, and that is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿بِمَا أَخْلَفُوا اللَّهَ مَا وَعَدُوهُ وَبِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾ in it. After that he came to the Prophet ﷺ with his zakat, and he said: "Allah has forbidden me to accept it from you," so he began throwing dust on his head. Then he came to Abū Bakr, who did not accept it, then to ʿUmar, who did not accept it, then to ʿUthmān, who did not accept it, and he died in his time.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا﴾ i.e. the hypocrites ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّهُمْ﴾ what they hid in themselves ﴿وَنَجْوَاهُمْ﴾ what they confided to one another, ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ﴾ what is hidden from sight? When the ayah of alms was revealed, a man came and gave a great deal in charity, and the hypocrites said: "Showing off." And a man came and gave a ṣāʿ in charity, and they said: "Allah has no need of this one's charity." So there was revealed:

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿يَلْمِزُونَ﴾ find fault with ﴿الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ﴾ those giving voluntarily ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي الصَّدَقَاتِ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ إِلَّا جُهْدَهُمْ﴾ their capacity, and bring it, ﴿فَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ — and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿سَخِرَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ﴾ He requited them for their mockery — ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿اسْتَغْفِرْ﴾ O Muḥammad, ﴿لَهُمْ أَوْ لَا تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ﴾ giving him the choice between asking forgiveness and leaving it. He ﷺ said: "I was given the choice, and I chose," meaning asking forgiveness. Narrated by al-Bukhārī. ﴿إِنْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً فَلَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ﴾ It is said that what is meant by "seventy" is emphasis on the abundance of asking forgiveness; and in al-Bukhārī there is the hadith: "If I knew that, were I to go beyond seventy, he would be forgiven, I would go beyond it." And it is said that what is meant is the specific number, because of his hadith also: "And I will go beyond seventy." So the cutting off of forgiveness was made clear to him by the ayah {سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَسْتَغْفَرْتَ لَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ} ("It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them"). ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿فَرِحَ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ﴾ from Tabūk ﴿بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ﴾ i.e. at their staying behind ﴿خِلَافَ﴾ i.e. after ﴿رَسُولِ اللَّهِ وَكَرِهُوا أَنْ يُجَاهِدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَقَالُوا﴾ i.e. some of them said to others: ﴿لَا تَنْفِرُوا﴾ do not go out to jihad ﴿فِي الْحَرِّ قُلْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ أَشَدُّ حَرًّا﴾ than Tabūk, so it is more fitting that they guard against it by not staying behind; ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ knew that, they would not have stayed behind.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيلًا﴾ in this world ﴿وَلْيَبْكُوا﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿كَثِيرًا جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾ — a statement (khabar) about their state in the form of an imperative.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿فَإِنْ رَجَعَكَ﴾ brings you back ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ from Tabūk ﴿إِلَى طَائِفَةٍ مِنْهُمْ﴾ of the hypocrites who stayed behind in Medina, ﴿فَاسْتَأْذَنُوكَ لِلْخُرُوجِ﴾ with you on another campaign, ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿لَنْ تَخْرُجُوا مَعِيَ أَبَدًا وَلَنْ تُقَاتِلُوا مَعِيَ عَدُوًّا إِنَّكُمْ رَضِيتُمْ بِالْقُعُودِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ فَاقْعُدُوا مَعَ الْخَالِفِينَ﴾ those who stay behind from campaigns, of women, children and others. And when the Prophet ﷺ prayed over Ibn Ubayy, there was revealed:

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿وَلَا تُصَلِّ عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ مَاتَ أَبَدًا وَلَا تَقُمْ عَلَى قَبْرِهِ﴾ for burial or visiting; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ فَاسِقُونَ﴾ unbelievers.

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَلَا تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَأَوْلَادُهُمْ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ بِهَا فِي الدُّنْيَا وَتَزْهَقَ﴾ depart ﴿أَنْفُسُهُمْ وَهُمْ كَافِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَإِذَا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ﴾ i.e. a portion of the Quran, ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. [Translator's note: saying] that ﴿آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَجَاهِدُوا مَعَ رَسُولِهِ اسْتَأْذَنَكَ أُولُوا الطَّوْلِ﴾ the people of wealth ﴿مِنْهُمْ وَقَالُوا ذَرْنَا نَكُنْ مَعَ الْقَاعِدِينَ﴾

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿رَضُوا بِأَنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الْخَوَالِفِ﴾ plural of خَالِفَة, i.e. the women who stay behind in the houses; ﴿وَطُبِعَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ what is good.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿لَكِنِ الرَّسُولُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ جَاهَدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ وَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمُ الْخَيْرَاتُ﴾ in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ i.e. the triumphant.

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا ذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿وَجَاءَ الْمُعَذِّرُونَ﴾ with the tāʾ of the original form assimilated (idghām) into the dhāl, i.e. الْمُعْتَذِرُونَ ("those offering excuses"), in the sense of "those who are excused" — and it has been read thus [Translator's note: i.e. as الْمُعْذِرُونَ] — ﴿مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ﴾ to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُمْ﴾ to stay behind because of their excuse, and he gave them leave; ﴿وَقَعَدَ الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ in claiming faith — of the hypocrites of the Bedouins — from coming to excuse themselves. ﴿سَيُصِيبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَى الضُّعَفَاءِ﴾ such as the old, ﴿وَلَا عَلَى الْمَرْضَى﴾ such as the blind and the chronically ill, ﴿وَلَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ مَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ in jihad, ﴿حَرَجٌ﴾ sin in staying behind from it, ﴿إِذَا نَصَحُوا لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ while they stay behind, by not spreading alarming rumours or discouraging, and by obedience. ﴿مَا عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ in that ﴿مِنْ سَبِيلٍ﴾ way to blame [Translator's note: them]; ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ﴾ to them, ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them, in granting latitude in that.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَلَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ إِذَا مَا أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ﴾ with you to the campaign — they were seven of the Anṣār, and it is said the Banū Muqarrin — ﴿قُلْتَ لَا أَجِدُ مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾ the answer of إِذَا, i.e. they turned away ﴿وَأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ﴾ overflowing ﴿مِنَ﴾ explicative (li-l-bayān) ﴿الدَّمْعِ حَزَنًا﴾ because ﴿أَلَّا يَجِدُوا مَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ in jihad.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا السَّبِيلُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَسْتَأْذِنُونَكَ﴾ to stay behind ﴿وَهُمْ أَغْنِيَاءُ رَضُوا بِأَنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الْخَوَالِفِ وَطَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — its like has preceded.

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿يَعْتَذِرُونَ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ for staying behind ﴿إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ from the campaign. ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them: ﴿لَا تَعْتَذِرُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكُمْ﴾ believe you; ﴿قَدْ نَبَّأَنَا اللَّهُ مِنْ أَخْبَارِكُمْ﴾ i.e. He has informed us of your states; ﴿وَسَيَرَى اللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ وَرَسُولُهُ ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ﴾ by the resurrection ﴿إِلَى عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ﴾ i.e. Allah, ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and will requite you for it.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿سَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ لَكُمْ إِذَا انْقَلَبْتُمْ﴾ return ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ from Tabūk, that they were excused in staying behind, ﴿لِتُعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ﴾ by not reproaching them. ﴿فَأَعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ رِجْسٌ﴾ filth, because of the foulness of their inner selves, ﴿وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ لِتَرْضَوْا عَنْهُمْ فَإِنْ تَرْضَوْا عَنْهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَرْضَى عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾ i.e. with them; and your being pleased is of no benefit alongside Allah's displeasure.

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿الْأَعْرَابُ﴾ the people of the desert ﴿أَشَدُّ كُفْرًا وَنِفَاقًا﴾ than the people of the towns, because of their harshness, the coarseness of their natures and their distance from hearing the Quran, ﴿وَأَجْدَرُ﴾ more likely ﴿أَلَّا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ of rulings and laws. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of His creation, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He does with them.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿وَمِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ مَا يُنْفِقُ﴾ in the way of Allah ﴿مَغْرَمًا﴾ a fine and a loss, because he does not hope for its reward but spends it out of fear — they are the Banū Asad and Ghaṭafān — ﴿وَيَتَرَبَّصُ﴾ waits ﴿بِكُمُ الدَّوَائِرَ﴾ the turns of fortune, that they turn against you so they may be free. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ دَائِرَةُ السُّوءِ﴾ with ḍamma and with fatḥa [السَّوْءِ], i.e. punishment and destruction will turn upon them, not upon you. ﴿وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of the sayings of His servants, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of their deeds.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿وَمِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ﴾ such as Juhayna and Muzayna, ﴿وَيَتَّخِذُ مَا يُنْفِقُ﴾ in the way of Allah ﴿قُرُبَاتٍ﴾ bringing him near ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَ﴾ a means to ﴿صَلَوَاتِ﴾ the prayers of ﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾ for him. ﴿أَلَا إِنَّهَا﴾ i.e. their spending ﴿قُرُبَةٌ﴾ with ḍamma on the rāʾ and with sukūn [قُرْبَةٌ] ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ with Him; ﴿سَيُدْخِلُهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ His Garden. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to the people of His obedience, ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿وَالسَّابِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصَارِ﴾ — they are those who were present at Badr, or all the Companions — ﴿وَالَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُمْ﴾ until the Day of Resurrection ﴿بِإِحْسَانٍ﴾ in deeds: ﴿رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ﴾ for their obedience ﴿وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾ with His reward, ﴿وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي تَحْتَهَا الْأَنْهَارُ﴾ — and in one reading with the addition of مِنْ — ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا ذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكُمْ﴾ O people of Medina, ﴿مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ مُنَافِقُونَ﴾ such as Aslam, Ashjaʿ and Ghifār, ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ﴾ hypocrites also, ﴿مَرَدُوا عَلَى النِّفَاقِ﴾ persisted obstinately in it and continued; ﴿لَا تَعْلَمُهُمْ﴾ addressed to the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿نَحْنُ نَعْلَمُهُمْ سَنُعَذِّبُهُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ﴾ by exposure or killing in this world, and the punishment of the grave; ﴿ثُمَّ يُرَدُّونَ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿إِلَى عَذَابٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ which is the Fire.

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿وَ﴾ a people ﴿آخَرُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), ﴿اعْتَرَفُوا بِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ of staying behind — its naʿt (adjective) — and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿خَلَطُوا عَمَلًا صَالِحًا﴾ namely their jihad before that, or their confessing their sins, or something else, ﴿وَآخَرَ سَيِّئًا﴾ namely their staying behind. ﴿عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ It was revealed concerning Abū Lubāba and a group who tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque when what had been revealed about those who stayed behind reached them, and swore that none but the Prophet ﷺ would untie them; and he untied them when there was revealed:

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا﴾ from their sins. So he took a third of their wealth and gave it in charity. ﴿وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. pray for them; ﴿إِنَّ صَلَوتَكَ سَكَنٌ﴾ a mercy ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ — and it is said: reassurance that their repentance has been accepted. ﴿وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَأْخُذُ﴾ accepts ﴿الصَّدَقَاتِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ﴾ to His servants, by accepting their repentance, ﴿الرَّحِيمُ﴾ to them? The interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr), and its purpose is to stir them to repentance and charity.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿وَقُلْ﴾ to them, or to people: ﴿اعْمَلُوا﴾ what you will, ﴿فَسَيَرَى اللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ وَرَسُولُهُ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَسَتُرَدُّونَ﴾ by the resurrection ﴿إِلَى عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ﴾ i.e. Allah, ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and will requite you for it.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿وَآخَرُونَ﴾ of those who stayed behind ﴿مُرْجَؤُنَ﴾ with hamza and without it [مُرْجَوْنَ]: deferred from [being granted] repentance ﴿لِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ concerning them, with what He wills: ﴿إِمَّا يُعَذِّبُهُمْ﴾ by making them die without repentance, ﴿وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of His creation, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He does with them. They are the three who come later: Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ, Kaʿb ibn Mālik and Hilāl ibn Umayya. They stayed behind out of laziness and inclination to ease, not out of hypocrisy, and did not make excuses to the Prophet ﷺ as the others did; so their case was suspended for fifty nights and the people shunned them, until their repentance was revealed afterwards.

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿وَ﴾ among them are ﴿الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مَسْجِدًا﴾ — they were twelve of the hypocrites — ﴿ضِرَارًا﴾ to harm the people of the mosque of Qubāʾ, ﴿وَكُفْرًا﴾ because they built it at the command of Abū ʿĀmir the monk, to be a stronghold for him in which he would receive whoever came from him; he had gone to bring troops from Caesar to fight the Prophet ﷺ; ﴿وَتَفْرِيقًا بَيْنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ who prayed at Qubāʾ, by some of them praying in their mosque, ﴿وَإِرْصَادًا﴾ lying in wait ﴿لِمَنْ حَارَبَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ i.e. before its building — he is the aforementioned Abū ʿĀmir. ﴿وَلَيَحْلِفُنَّ إِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَرَدْنَا﴾ by building it ﴿إِلَّا﴾ the deed ﴿الْحُسْنَى﴾ of kindness to the poor in rain and heat and providing room for the Muslims. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ in that. They had asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray in it, so there was revealed:

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿لَا تَقُمْ﴾ pray ﴿فِيهِ أَبَدًا﴾. So he sent a group who demolished it, burned it, and made its site a refuse heap into which carcasses were thrown. ﴿لَمَسْجِدٌ أُسِّسَ﴾ whose foundations were built ﴿عَلَى التَّقْوَى مِنْ أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ﴾ it was laid on the day you arrived at the abode of emigration — it is the mosque of Qubāʾ, as in al-Bukhārī — ﴿أَحَقُّ﴾ than it ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. that ﴿تَقُومَ﴾ you pray ﴿فِيهِ فِيهِ رِجَالٌ﴾ — they are the Anṣār — ﴿يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَتَطَهَّرُوا وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُطَّهِّرِينَ﴾ i.e. will reward them; in it the tāʾ of the original form is assimilated (idghām) into the ṭāʾ. Ibn Khuzayma narrated in his Ṣaḥīḥ from ʿUwaymir ibn Sāʿida that he ﷺ came to them in the mosque of Qubāʾ and said: "Allah the Exalted has praised you well for purification in the story of your mosque; so what is this purification with which you purify yourselves?" They said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing except that we had neighbours from the Jews who used to wash their backsides after relieving themselves, so we washed as they washed." And in a hadith narrated by al-Bazzār they said: "We follow the stones with water," and he said: "That is it, so hold to it." [Translator's note: the Companion is usually known as ʿUwaym ibn Sāʿida.]

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَانَهُ عَلَى تَقْوَى﴾ fear ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ وَ﴾ hope of ﴿رِضْوَانٍ﴾ from Him ﴿خَيْرٌ أَمْ مَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَانَهُ عَلَى شَفَا﴾ the edge of ﴿جُرُفٍ﴾ with ḍamma on the rāʾ and with sukūn: a bank ﴿هَارٍ﴾ about to collapse, ﴿فَانْهَارَ بِهِ﴾ it collapsed together with its builder ﴿فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ — is better? This is a representation of building on the opposite of piety by what it leads to. The interrogative is for affirmation (taqrīr), i.e. the first is better, and it is the likeness of the mosque of Qubāʾ, while the second is the likeness of the Mosque of Harm (masjid al-ḍirār). ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿لَا يَزَالُ بُنْيَانُهُمُ الَّذِي بَنَوْا رِيبَةً﴾ doubt ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ إِلَّا أَنْ تَقَطَّعَ﴾ are severed ﴿قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ by their dying. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of His creation, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in what He does with them.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ اشْتَرَى مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ by their expending them in His obedience, such as jihad, ﴿بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ﴾ — a resumptive clause explaining the purchase; and in one reading with the passive put first, i.e. some of them are killed and the rest fight on — ﴿وَعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا﴾ two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the accusative by their omitted verb, ﴿فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ وَالْقُرْآنِ وَمَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. no one is more faithful than He. ﴿فَاسْتَبْشِرُوا﴾ in it is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person ﴿بِبَيْعِكُمُ الَّذِي بَايَعْتُمْ بِهِ وَذَلِكَ﴾ sale ﴿هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ﴾ that attains the utmost of what is sought.

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿التَّائِبُونَ﴾ nominative by way of praise, with an implied (muqaddar) mubtadaʾ (subject); [Translator's note: repenting] from idolatry and hypocrisy; ﴿الْعَابِدُونَ﴾ those who make worship sincerely for Allah, ﴿الْحَامِدُونَ﴾ Him in every state, ﴿السَّائِحُونَ﴾ the fasting, ﴿الرَّاكِعُونَ السَّاجِدُونَ﴾ i.e. those who pray, ﴿الْآمِرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَالنَّاهُونَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَالْحَافِظُونَ لِحُدُودِ اللَّهِ﴾ His rulings, by acting on them; ﴿وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ of Paradise. And there was revealed concerning his ﷺ asking forgiveness for his uncle Abū Ṭālib, and some of the Companions asking forgiveness for their idolatrous parents:

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ وَلَوْ كَانُوا أُولِي قُرْبَى﴾ kin ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ the Fire, by their having died in unbelief.

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَا إِيَّاهُ﴾ by his saying { سَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّي } ("I will ask my Lord to forgive you"), in hope that he would become Muslim; ﴿فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أَنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ﴾ by his dying in unbelief, ﴿تَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُ﴾ and abandoned asking forgiveness for him. ﴿إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لَأَوَّاهٌ﴾ much given to humble entreaty and supplication, ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾ patient under harm.

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْمًا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَاهُمْ﴾ to Islam ﴿حَتَّى يُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ مَا يَتَّقُونَ﴾ of deeds, and they do not guard against it, and so deserve to be led astray. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ and part of that is who deserves being led astray and who deserves guidance.

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَمَا لَكُمْ﴾ O people, ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him, ﴿مِنْ وَلِيٍّ﴾ to protect you from Him ﴿وَلَا نَصِيرٍ﴾ to defend you from His harm.

celaleyn:117-117.t: ﴿لَقَدْ تَابَ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. He continued His turning in forgiveness ﴿عَلَى النَّبِيِّ وَالْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصَارِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ فِي سَاعَةِ الْعُسْرَةِ﴾ i.e. its time — that was their state in the campaign of Tabūk: two men would share a date, ten would take turns on a single camel, and the heat grew so intense that they drank the contents of [Translator's note: camels'] stomachs — ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا كَادَ تَزِيغُ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ [يَزِيغُ]: incline ﴿قُلُوبُ فَرِيقٍ مِنْهُمْ﴾ away from following him toward staying behind, because of the hardship they were in; ﴿ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ by [Translator's note: granting them] steadfastness. ﴿إِنَّهُ بِهِمْ رَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿وَ﴾ He turned in forgiveness ﴿عَلَى الثَّلَاثَةِ الَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا﴾ from [Translator's note: the acceptance of] repentance for them, by the indication of ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا ضَاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَرْضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتْ﴾ i.e. despite its spaciousness, i.e. its breadth, so they found no place in which to feel secure, ﴿وَضَاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ their hearts, from grief and desolation at the delay of their repentance, so that no joy or comfort could find room in them, ﴿وَظَنُّوا﴾ were certain ﴿أَنْ﴾ lightened [Translator's note: from أَنَّ] (mukhaffafa) ﴿لَا مَلْجَأَ مِنَ اللَّهِ إِلَّا إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ granted them success in repenting, ﴿لِيَتُوبُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ by abandoning acts of disobedience to Him ﴿وَكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ in faith and covenants, by holding fast to truthfulness.

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِأَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ أَنْ يَتَخَلَّفُوا عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ﴾ when he goes on campaign, ﴿وَلَا يَرْغَبُوا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ﴾ by shielding themselves from the hardships he accepted for himself — it is a prohibition in the wording of a statement (khabar). ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the prohibition of staying behind, ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ is because ﴿لَا يُصِيبُهُمْ ظَمَأٌ﴾ thirst ﴿وَلَا نَصَبٌ﴾ fatigue ﴿وَلَا مَخْمَصَةٌ﴾ hunger ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَطَئُونَ مَوْطِئًا﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning a treading ﴿يَغِيظُ﴾ that angers ﴿الْكُفَّارَ وَلَا يَنَالُونَ مِنْ عَدُوٍّ﴾ of Allah ﴿نَيْلًا﴾ killing, capture or plunder, ﴿إِلَّا كُتِبَ لَهُمْ بِهِ عَمَلٌ صَالِحٌ﴾ so that they may be requited for it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ i.e. their reward; rather He rewards them.

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿وَلَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ in it ﴿نَفَقَةً صَغِيرَةً﴾ even a date ﴿وَلَا كَبِيرَةً وَلَا يَقْطَعُونَ وَادِيًا﴾ by travelling ﴿إِلَّا كُتِبَ لَهُمْ﴾ by it a righteous deed, ﴿لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ i.e. its recompense. When they were rebuked for staying behind, and the Prophet ﷺ sent out a raiding party, they all went out, so there was revealed:

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا﴾ to the campaign ﴿كَافَّةً فَلَوْلَا﴾ why then did not ﴿نَفَرَ مِنْ كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ﴾ tribe ﴿مِنْهُمْ طَائِفَةٌ﴾ a group, while the rest stayed, ﴿لِيَتَفَقَّهُوا﴾ i.e. those who stayed, ﴿فِي الدِّينِ وَلِيُنْذِرُوا قَوْمَهُمْ إِذَا رَجَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ from the campaign, by teaching them the rulings they have learned, ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَحْذَرُونَ﴾ the punishment of Allah, by complying with His command and prohibition. Ibn ʿAbbās said: this one is specific to raiding parties, and the one before it to the prohibition of anyone staying behind when the Prophet ﷺ himself went out.

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ يَلُونَكُمْ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ﴾ i.e. the nearest of them, then the next nearest, ﴿وَلْيَجِدُوا فِيكُمْ غِلْظَةً﴾ severity, i.e. be harsh with them; ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ with help and victory.

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿وَإِذَا مَا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ﴾ of the Quran, ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the hypocrites, ﴿مَنْ يَقُولُ﴾ to his companions in mockery: ﴿أَيُّكُمْ زَادَتْهُ هَذِهِ إِيمَانًا﴾ belief? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَزَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَانًا﴾ because of their believing in it, ﴿وَهُمْ يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ﴾ rejoice at it.

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ weakness of belief, ﴿فَزَادَتْهُمْ رِجْسًا إِلَى رِجْسِهِمْ﴾ unbelief upon their unbelief, because of their disbelieving in it, ﴿وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كَافِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿أَوَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّهُمْ﴾ with yāʾ, i.e. the hypocrites, and with tāʾ, O believers, ﴿يُفْتَنُونَ﴾ are tried ﴿فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ مَرَّةً أَوْ مَرَّتَيْنِ﴾ with drought and diseases, ﴿ثُمَّ لَا يَتُوبُونَ﴾ from their hypocrisy ﴿وَلَا هُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ take warning?

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿وَإِذَا مَا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ﴾ in which they are mentioned, and the Prophet ﷺ recited it, ﴿نَظَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ﴾ wanting to flee, saying: ﴿هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ﴾ if you get up? If no one saw them they would get up; otherwise they stayed put. ﴿ثُمَّ انْصَرَفُوا﴾ upon their unbelief. ﴿صَرَفَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ from guidance, ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ the truth, through their failure to reflect.

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ i.e. from among you, Muḥammad ﷺ; ﴿عَزِيزٌ﴾ grievous ﴿عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾ i.e. your distress, i.e. your hardship and your meeting with what is hateful; ﴿حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ that you be guided; ﴿بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌ﴾ intensely merciful, ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ wanting good for them.

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ from believing in you, ﴿فَقُلْ حَسْبِيَ﴾ sufficient for me is ﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ﴾ in Him I have trusted, not in another; ﴿وَهُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ﴾ the Kursī, ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾ — He singled it out for mention because it is the greatest of created things. Al-Ḥākim narrated in al-Mustadrak from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The last ayah revealed was { لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ } to the end of the surah.

daas-irab:61-61.t:
﴿وَمِنْهُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); the wāw is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُؤْذُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿النَّبِيَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿هُوَ﴾ a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿أُذُنٌ﴾ khabar, and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you". ﴿أُذُنٌ﴾ khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو أذن خير", and خير is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is likewise the object of the saying. The clause قل هو أذن.. is resumptive. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to خير before them. ﴿يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", and the clause is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of أذن. The clause ﴿يُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ is conjoined. ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾ conjoined to أذن.
﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ the two are attached to رحمة. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the wāw is resumptive. ﴿يُؤْذُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿رَسُولَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted fronted khabar.
﴿عَذابٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ naʿt. The nominal clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

daas-irab:62-62.t:
﴿يَحْلِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ and ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿لِيُرْضُوكُمْ﴾ the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the implied أن after the lām of causation and the verb is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يحلفون. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿وَرَسُولُهُ﴾ conjoined. ﴿أَحَقُّ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿أَنْ يُرْضُوهُ﴾
the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by a preposition, i.e. "Allah is more entitled to being pleased". ﴿أَنْ﴾ a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive (jāzim). [Translator's note: the source vocalizes the word here as أَنْ; the Quranic text reads إِنْ.] ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its subject (ism). ﴿مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, and the clause كانوا is an initial clause, the clause of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).

daas-irab:63-63.t:
﴿أَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and لم is a particle of negation, jussive-making and tense-reversal. ﴿يَعْلَمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ أنّ, and the hāʾ is its ism (subject). ﴿مَنْ﴾ a conditional noun making the verb jussive, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject).
