harrat-mujtaba:122-122.t: The lām in «لينفروا» is for denial (juḥūd), and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, its implied form being "intending". «كافة»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «ينفروا». The clause «فلولا نفر» is resumptive; «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). The preposition «من كل» is attached to «نفر», and the preposition «منهم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «فرقة». «إذا رجعوا» is a pure adverb attached to «ينذر». The clause «لعلهم يحذرون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:123-123.t: The preposition «من الكفار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الذين», and the preposition «فيكم» is attached to a ḥāl from «غلظة».

harrat-mujtaba:124-124.t: «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), and «إذا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis, i.e. "some of them say, when…". «أيكم»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct); the demonstrative is the fāʿil (agent), and «إيمانا» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «وهم يستبشرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «فزادتهم».

harrat-mujtaba:125-125.t: «رجسا» is the second object, and the preposition «إلى رجسهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رجسا». The clause «وهم كافرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «ماتوا».

harrat-mujtaba:126-126.t: The hamza is for interrogation and the wāw is a conjunction; the clause is conjoined to the preceding conditional clause, with no grammatical position. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أنهم يفتنون» is the object of «رأى». «مرة» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause «ولا هم يذكرون» is conjoined to the clause «يتوبون», in the position of the nominative.

harrat-mujtaba:127-127.t: «ما» is redundant (zāʾida). «أحد» is the fāʿil (agent) of «يراكم», and «مِنْ» is redundant. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «بأنهم قوم» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «صرف». The clause «هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ» is the content of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied verb of saying, and this saying is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of «نظر», i.e. "saying: does anyone see you". The clause «صرف الله» is resumptive, and the clause «لا يفقهون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:128-128.t: The clause «لقد جاءكم» is the answer to an implied oath. The preposition «من أنفسكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول». «عَزِيزٌ عليه ما عَنِتُّمْ»: «عزيز» is a naʿt of «رسول»; the preposition «عليه» is attached to «عزيز»; «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the fāʿil (agent) of «عزيز». «حريص»: a third naʿt, and the preposition «عليكم» is attached to «حريص».

harrat-mujtaba:129-129.t: The clause «فإن تولَّوا» is conjoined to the clause {جَاءَكُمْ}, with no grammatical position. «حسبي الله»: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). «لا» is the lā of generic negation, «إله» is its noun, «إلا» is for restriction, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "deserving of worship". «هو» is a badal (substitute) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar. The clause of transcendence (tanzīh) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the word of majesty (Allah). The clause «عليه توكلت» is a second ḥāl, and the clause «وهو رب» is conjoined to the clause «عليه توكلت».

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «براءة من الله»: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a disavowal"; the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «براءة», and the preposition «إلى الذين» is attached to a second naʿt of «براءة». The preposition «من المشركين» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referring pronoun, i.e. "you made a covenant with them, they being from the polytheists".

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «فسيحوا» is conjoined to the clause «هذه براءة», with no grammatical position. «أربعة» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سيحوا». The interpreted maṣdar «أنكم غير معجزي» takes the place of the two objects of علم, and the second interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: His words «وأذان»: the wāw is a conjunction; «أذان» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and this is an announcement", and the clause is conjoined to the clause «هذه براءة», with no grammatical position. The preposition «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «أذان», and the preposition «إلى الناس» is attached to a second naʿt of «أذان»; «يوم» [Translator's note: the source calls it «الجار», a preposition and its genitive noun] is attached to a third naʿt of «أذان». The interpreted maṣdar «أن الله بريء» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ. His words «ورسوله»: the wāw is a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "and His Messenger is likewise free"; the clause is conjoined to the single word «بريء», in the position of the nominative, as a case of conjoining a clause to a single word. Thus two things were predicated of Allah: the first, His being free of the polytheists, and the second, His Messenger's being free. The clause «فإن تبتم» is resumptive. The interpreted maṣdar «أنكم غير معجزي» takes the place of the two objects of علم. The clause «وبشِّر» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «إلا الذين»: excepted, connected (muttaṣil), from «الذين عاهدتم». The preposition «من المشركين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied (muqaddar) referring pronoun. «نقص» takes two objects: the kāf and «شيئًا». The clause «فأتموا» is resumptive, and the preposition «إلى مدتهم» is attached to a ḥāl from «عهدهم».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), not to the apodosis itself, because what comes after the fāʾ does not govern what precedes it. «حيث» is an adverb of place, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, attached to «اقتلوا». The wāw in «وجدتموهم» is for lengthening (ishbāʿ). «كل مرصد» is accusative by removal of the preposition (على). The conditional clause «فإن تابوا» is conjoined to the conditional clause before it.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «أحد»: the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it, and the preposition «من المشركين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «أحد»; the clause «استجارك» is explicative. «مأمنه» is a second object. The interpreted maṣdar «بأنهم قوم» is genitive, attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «ذلك», and the clause «ذلك بأنهم قوم» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «كيف»: an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial). «يكون» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; the preposition «للمشركين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), and the adverb «عند الله» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «عهد». «الذين» is excepted, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of the accusative. His words «فما استقاموا لكم فاستقيموا لهم»: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «ما» is a conditional noun, an adverb of time attached to استقاموا; the implied form is: "at whatever time they are upright with you, be upright with them". The clause «فما استقاموا» is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) before it.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «كيف»: an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "how can you not fight them?" The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); the clause «وإن يظهروا» is a ḥāl from the wāw in the implied (muqaddar) «تقاتلونهم». His words «إلا»: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «يرضونكم» is resumptive, and the clause «وأكثرهم فاسقون» is conjoined to the verbal clause «تأبى قلوبهم».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «إنهم ساء» is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of ساء, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "their deeds".

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «لا يرقبون» is a second khabar (predicate) of «إن» in the previous verse. «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and the clause «وأولئك هم المعتدون» is conjoined to the clause «لا يرقبون».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «فإن تابوا» is resumptive. His words «فإخوانكم»: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «إخوانكم» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then they are your brothers"; the preposition «في الدين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) إخوانكم because of the verbal meaning in it; the clause «فهم إخوانكم» is the apodosis, in the position of the jussive. The clause «ونفصل» is resumptive, and the clause «يعلمون» is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «وإن نكثوا» is conjoined to the clause {فَإِنْ تَابُوا}. The clause «إنهم لا أيمان لهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أئمة الكفر», and the clause «لعلهم ينتهون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «ألا»: a particle of offering and urging (ʿarḍ wa-taḥḍīḍ). The clause «وهم بدءوكم» is conjoined to the clause «هَمُّوا». «أول مرة»: an adverb of time. The clause «فالله أحق» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e. "if you fear anyone, then Allah is more deserving". The clause «إن كنتم مؤمنين» is resumptive, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: «يعذِّبهم»: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition, and its object.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «أم» is the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa), and it is construed as "rather" plus the hamza. The interpreted maṣdar «أن تُتْرَكوا» takes the place of the two objects of حسب. His words «ولَمَّا يعلم»: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a particle that makes jussive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm). The preposition «منكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «جاهدوا», and the preposition «من دون» is attached to the second object of «اتخذ». «ما» in his words «بما تعملون» is maṣdariyya, and the genitive interpreted maṣdar is attached to «خبير».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن يعمروا» is the noun of kāna, and the preposition «للمشركين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) its khabar (predicate). «شاهدين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the polytheists, and the two prepositions «على أنفسهم» and «بالكفر» are attached to «شاهدين». The clause «وهم خالدون» is conjoined to «حبطت أعمالهم», in the position of the nominative.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «إنما»: a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa), with no governing effect. The clause «فعسى أولئك أن يكونوا» is conjoined to the clause «إنما يعمر». «عسى» is a past abrogating verb (nāsikh), and «أولئك» is its noun; the interpreted maṣdar «أن يكونوا» is the khabar (predicate) of عسى.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The preposition «كمن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a second object of «جعل», and the clause «لا يستوون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «الذين»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is «أعظم», and «درجة» is a tamyīz (specification); the adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعظم». «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and the clause «وأولئك هم الفائزون» is conjoined to «أعظم», as a case of conjoining a clause to a single word.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: The saying of the Exalted {بَرَاءَة}: a maṣdar (verbal noun), nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and إلى الذين is its khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying {وأذان}: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to براءة, and its khabar (predicate) is إلى الناس, so it is the conjoining of a clause to a clause. It has been said that the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) is أن الله بريء من المشركين, on the assumption of "because Allah…" (لأن الله).
And His saying {من الله} in both places is a naʿt (adjective) of براءة and of أذان; for that reason beginning with an indefinite noun is good. You may also make براءة nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is a declaration of disassociation". The meaning of براءة من الله is "a notification from Allah".
His saying {يَوْم الْحَج}: what governs it is the adjective of أذان; it has been said that what governs it is مخزي. It is not good for أذان to govern it, because you have already qualified it, so it has left the status of the verb.
His saying {أَن الله بَرِيء}: أنّ is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) on the assumption of the omission of the lām or the bāʾ. If you make it the khabar of أذان — but it is not the same thing as it — then the omission of the preposition must be assumed in every case.
His saying {وَرَسُوله}: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "and His Messenger is also free of the polytheists"; it was omitted because the first indicates it. Some have allowed its being nominative by conjunction with the position of the name of Allah before أنّ entered, and they said that الأذان has the meaning of "saying", so it is as if [أنّ] did not change the meaning of the speech by entering it. A group rejected that, because the open أنّ has changed the meaning of the nominal sentence (al-ibtidāʾ), since it together with what follows it is a maṣdar; so it is not like the broken إنّ, which indicates nothing but emphasis, so that its entering does not change the meaning of the nominal sentence.
As for conjoining ورسوله to the implied nominative pronoun in بريء, that is ugly according to many grammarians unless it is emphasised; but many of them allowed it in this place even without emphasising it, because the genitive phrase stands in place of the tawkīd (emphasis), so conjoining it to the pronoun in بريء is good and sound. Conjunction to an implied nominative pronoun has come in the Qurʾān without tawkīd and without anything standing in place of the tawkīd: He, exalted be His mention, said ما أشركنا ولا آباؤنا, conjoining الآباء to the implied nominative pronoun. There is no proof in the entering of لا, because it entered only after the wāw of conjunction, whereas what stands in place of the tawkīd comes only before the wāw of conjunction, in the place of the tawkīd; the tawkīd, were it brought, would come only before the wāw of conjunction, as in the saying of the Exalted فاذهب أنت وربك. But that was permitted because the speech was lengthened by the entering of لا, so the length stood in place of the tawkīd.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read ورسولَه in the accusative, conjoined to the wording [of the name of Allah].
His saying {من الله}: the nūn was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; fatḥa was more fitting for it because of the frequency of use and so that two kasras would not come together. Some Arabs give it kasra according to the analogy.
«[Translator's note: the text has «في موضع التأكيد التأكيد», with the word التأكيد repeated; it is translated as two clauses.]»

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying {كل مرصد}: its implied form is "at every place of ambush" (على كل مرصد); when على was omitted it became accusative. It has also been said that it is an adverb (ẓarf).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying {وَإِن أحد}: أحد is nominative by its verb, its implied form being "and if anyone seeks your protection", because إن is the mother of the conditional particles, so it is more fitting that a verb follow it.
«[Translator's note: the text reads «استحارك»; the verse has استجارك.]»

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {كَيفَ وَإِن يظهروا}: the thing asked about is omitted, its implied form being "how [could it be] that you not fight them?"; it has also been said that the implied form is "how could they have a covenant?".

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {أَئِمَّة الْكفْر}: the pattern of أئمة is أفعِلة, the plural of إمام, like حمار and أحمرة. Its original form is أَأْمِمة; then the vowel of the first mīm was cast onto the quiescent hamza, and [the mīm] was assimilated into the second mīm, and the hamza with kasra was replaced by a yāʾ with kasra. This is because its due, before the assimilation, was to be replaced by an alif, since what precedes it has fatḥa, as its origin is quiescence because it is the first radical (fāʾ al-fiʿl) — it is the fāʾ of أفعلة — so its origin is substitution. Therefore it was treated by substitution after the vowel was cast onto it, and it was not treated as "between-between" (bayna bayna), as the kasra-hamza was treated in أئذا, أئنا and أئفكا; for in these the vowel of the hamza is fixed and not transferred, whereas in that one its vowel is accidental, transferred to it from the first mīm. So that one followed its origin in quiescence, which is substitution, and this other followed its origin in having a vowel, which is "between-between" in lightening, i.e. between hamza and yāʾ. I mean in all of this according to the reading of whoever lightens the second [hamza] and does not pronounce it fully.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying {فَالله أَحَق أَن تخشوه}: الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), أن تخشوه is a badal (substitute) from it, and أحق is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. If you wish, you make فالله a mubtadaʾ and أن تخشوه a second mubtadaʾ, with أحق its khabar, and the clause the khabar of the first. It is also permissible that الله be a mubtadaʾ and أحق its khabar, with أن in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition. Similar to it is أحق أن يرضوه. أحق in both places is an afʿal [elative], with which an omission must be assumed by which the speech is completed: its implied form is "Allah is more deserving than anyone else of being feared", if you assume the preposition; and if you make أن a badal or a second mubtadaʾ, the implied form is "fear of Allah is more deserving than fear of anyone else". Likewise is the implied form of أحق أن يرضوه.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {أَن تتركوا}: أن is in the position of the accusative by حسب, and it stands in place of the two objects of حسب according to Sībawayh. Al-Mubarrad said: it is the first object, and the second object is omitted.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t:
His saying {أجعلتم سِقَايَة الْحَاج وَعمارَة الْمَسْجِد الْحَرَام}: in this speech there is an omission of a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), either from its beginning or from its end. If the omission is from its beginning, its implied form is "Have you made the people of the giving of water to the pilgrims and the people of the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque like one who believes in Allah?". If you assume the omission from its end, its implied form is "Have you made the giving of water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque like the faith of one who believes in Allah?". This was needed only so that the mubtadaʾ (subject) would be the same as the khabar (predicate) in meaning, and by it the speech and its sense are sound.
His saying {وَيَوْم حنين}: يوم is accusative by conjunction with the position of في مواطن كثيرة, its implied form being "and He helped you on the day of Ḥunayn".

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying {لَهُم فِيهَا نعيم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of جنات. The hāʾ in فيها is for the gardens; it is a plural with alif and tāʾ by which a large number is intended. It has been said that it refers back to the mercy, and it has been said that it refers back to the good tidings, indicated by His saying يبشرهم. Likewise the hāʾ in the second فيها admits the same aspects as the first.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t:
His saying {وَقَالَت الْيَهُود عُزَيْر ابْن الله}: whoever gives nunation to عزير makes it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with ابن its khabar (predicate). On this view it is not good to drop the nunation from عزير for the meeting of two quiescent letters; the alif of ابن is not dropped from the writing, and the nunation takes kasra because of the meeting of the two quiescent letters. Whoever does not give nunation to عزير also makes it a mubtadaʾ, with ابن an adjective of it; on this view the nunation is dropped for lightness, because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and because the adjective and the qualified noun are like a single noun; the alif of ابن is dropped from the writing, and the khabar is implied, its implied form being "and the Jews said: ʿUzayr son of Allah is our companion" or "our prophet". Or this implied element is the mubtadaʾ and عزير is its khabar. It is also permissible that عزير be a mubtadaʾ and ابن a khabar, with the nunation dropped for the meeting of two quiescent letters, since it resembles the letters of prolongation and softness; then the alif of ابن is kept in the writing when you make it a khabar.
Abū Ḥātim allowed عزير to be a foreign (ʿajamī) noun that is a diptote. That is far-fetched and rejected, because if it were foreign it would be fully declined, since it has three letters and the yāʾ of the diminutive is not counted, and because according to all the grammarians it is Arabic, derived from the saying of the Exalted وتعزروه.
His saying {فِي كتاب الله يَوْم}: كتاب is a maṣdar (verbal noun) governing يوم. كتاب here may not mean the Reminder, nor any other of the books, because then it would be prevented from governing يوم, since nouns that denote concrete things do not govern adverbs, as there is nothing of the meaning of the verb in them. As for في, it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, which is an adjective of اثنا عشر, which is the khabar of إنّ, as if He said: "The number of months with Allah is twelve months, established in the Book of Allah on the day He created". It is not good for في to be attached to عدة, because you would separate between the ṣila (relative clause) and the relative [i.e. the governing maṣdar and its complement] by the khabar, which is اثنا عشر.
«[Translator's note: the second paragraph concerns 9:36.]»

mekki-muskil:32-32.t:
His saying {ويأبى الله إِلَّا أَن يتم نوره}: إلا entered only because يأبى contains the meaning of preventing, and preventing belongs to the category of negation, so إلا entered for affirmation. In the speech there is an omission, its implied form being: "And Allah refuses everything they want of their disbelief except to perfect His light", so أن is in the position of the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā).
And the hāʾ in the saying of the Exalted {وَلَا يُنْفِقُونَهَا} refers back to the treasures, indicated by the saying of the Exalted يكنزون. It has been said that it refers back to the wealth, because gold and silver are wealth. It has been said that it refers back to the silver, and what would refer back to the gold was omitted because the second indicates it. It has been said that it refers back to the gold, because it is treated as both feminine and masculine. It has been said that it refers back to the spending, indicated by ينفقون. And it has been said that it refers back to the gold and the silver, in the sense of "and they do not spend them [both]", but its referring back to the silver sufficed instead of its referring back to the gold, just as the Arabs say أخوك وأبوك رأيته ("your brother and your father, I saw him"), meaning رأيتهما ("I saw them both").
And the hāʾ in {عَلَيْهَا} and {بهَا}: each of them admits the aspects that were mentioned for the hāʾ in ينفقونها.
«[Translator's note: the text reads «رأبته», evidently for «رأيته». The remarks on ولا ينفقونها, عليها and بها concern 9:34–35.]»

mekki-muskil:36-36.t:
His saying {كَافَّة}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the manner of your saying عافاك الله عافية ("may Allah grant you well-being"), عافيك عافية, and رأيتهم عامة وخاصة ("I saw them generally and particularly").
His saying {ثمَّ وليتم مُدبرين}: مدبرين is accusative as an emphasising ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida). It may not be an unrestricted ḥāl, because His saying ثم وليتم indicates turning the back, so it is an emphasising ḥāl of what the beginning of the speech indicated, in the manner of the saying of the Exalted وهو الحق مصدقا, and His saying وأن هذا صراطي مستقيما, and like your saying هو زيد معروفا ("he is Zayd, well known").
«[Translator's note: the text reads «وعافيك عافية» as printed. ثم وليتم مدبرين is from 9:25.]»

mekki-muskil:40-40.t:
His saying {ثَانِي اثْنَيْنِ}: ثاني is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in أخرجه, which refers back to the Prophet, upon him be peace, its implied form being: "when those who disbelieved drove him out, alone among all the people except Abū Bakr"; its meaning is "one of two". It has been said that it is a ḥāl from an omitted implied pronoun, its implied form being "so he went out, the second of two". The hāʾ in عليه refers back to Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, because the Prophet ﷺ already knew that nothing would harm him, since his going out was by the command of Allah, exalted be His mention, to him.
As for His saying {ثمَّ أنزل الله سكينته على رَسُوله وعَلى الْمُؤمنِينَ}, the tranquillity upon the Messenger was sent down on the day of Ḥunayn, because he feared for the Muslims and did not fear for himself; so the tranquillity came down upon him for the sake of the believers, not for the sake of fear for himself.
His saying {وَكلمَة الله هِيَ الْعليا}: all the readers have كلمة in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and that is the proper construction of the speech and more complete in meaning. Al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb al-Ḥaḍramī read it in the accusative, by جعل, and in it there is remoteness both in meaning and in iʿrāb. As for the meaning: the word of Allah has never ceased to be supreme, so making it accusative by جعل is far-fetched, because this suggests that it became so and that this occurred in it. That does not follow for the word of those who disbelieve, because it has always been made lowest in that way by their disbelief. As for its being excluded by iʿrāb: it would require that the noun not be made overt, and that it be said وكلمته هي العليا. Making the noun overt in such a case is permitted only in poetry; some have allowed it in poetry and elsewhere, and there is room for consideration in this, because of His saying وأخرجت الأرض أثقالها.
«[Translator's note: ثم أنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين is from 9:26.]»

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {خفافا وثقالا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in انفروا, i.e. "go forth on foot and riding"; it has also been said that its meaning is "young and old".

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying {أَن يجاهدوا}: أن is in the position of the accusative by omission of في, i.e. "about striving" (في أن يجاهدوا); it has also been said that its implied form is "out of dislike of striving".

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {يبغونكم}: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in ولأوضعوا خلالكم; and خلالكم is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf).

mekki-muskil:51-51.t: His saying {إِلَّا مَا كتب}: ما is in the position of the nominative by يصيبنا.

mekki-muskil:53-53.t: His saying {طَوْعًا أَو كرها}: two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "willing or unwilling".

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {أَن تقبل}: أن is in the position of the accusative by منع, and أنّ in His saying أنهم is in the position of the nominative by منع, because it is the agent.

mekki-muskil:61-61.t:
His saying {قل أذن خير لكم}: أذن is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "Say: he is an ear of good", i.e. he is a listener of good for you; i.e. he listens to what ought to be listened to and accepts what ought to be accepted. What is meant by the ear here is the whole of the owner of the ear, who is the Prophet, Allah bless him; i.e. he is a listener of good and righteousness, not a listener of evil and corruption.
His saying {وَرَحْمَة}: whoever reads it in the nominative conjoins it to أذن, i.e. "he is a listener of good, and he is a mercy for those who believe"; He made the Prophet himself the mercy because of how often it occurs through him and at his hands. It has been said that its implied form is "and he is one of mercy". Ḥamza read رحمة in the genitive, conjoined to خير, i.e. "and he is an ear of mercy", i.e. a listener of mercy; just as He annexed أذن to الخير, He annexed it to الرحمة, because mercy is part of good and good is part of mercy. It is not good to conjoin رحمة to المؤمنين, because the lām in للمؤمنين is redundant (zāʾida), its implied form being "and he believes the believers", i.e. he trusts them; and "he trusts the mercy" is not good — unless you make the mercy here the Qurʾān, in which case it is permissible to conjoin it to المؤمنين, and it is cut off from what precedes it. The exegesis indicates that it is connected to أذن خير لكم, because in the reading of Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd it is ورحمةٍ لكم in the genitive, and al-Aʿmash read it so; this indicates conjunction to خير, and that is the proper construction of the speech.

mekki-muskil:62-62.t:
His saying {وَالله وَرَسُوله أَحَق أَن يرضوه}: the view of Sībawayh is that the first clause is omitted because the second indicates it; its implied form according to him is "and Allah is more deserving that they please Him, and His Messenger is more deserving that they please him", so the first أن يرضوه was omitted because of the indication of the second; so on his view the hāʾ in يرضوه refers back to the Messenger, upon him be peace. Al-Mubarrad said: there is no omission in the speech, but there is a fronting and a postponing; its implied form according to him is "and Allah — that they should please Him — is more deserving, and His Messenger", so the hāʾ in يرضوه according to al-Mubarrad refers back to Allah, exalted be His praise. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "and His Messenger is more deserving that they please him", and والله is an opening of speech.
It follows from al-Mubarrad's view that "what Allah wills and you will" with wāw would be permissible, because he makes the speech a single clause, whereas that has been forbidden except with thumma. That does not follow for Sībawayh, because he makes the speech two clauses. So the view of Sībawayh is the preferred one for the verse. الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), أن يرضوه is a badal (substitute), and أحق is the khabar (predicate); or, if you wish, الله is a mubtadaʾ, أن يرضوه a second mubtadaʾ, أحق its khabar, and the clause the khabar of the first. Similar to it is فالله أحق أن تخشوه, whose explanation has already passed more clearly than this.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t:
His saying {فَأن لَهُ نَار جَهَنَّم}: the view of Sībawayh is that أنّ is a badal (substitute) from the first, in the position of the accusative by يعلموا. Al-Jarmī and al-Mubarrad said: it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first, in the position of the accusative. The fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) on these two views. Both views entail permitting the badal and the tawkīd before the completion of what is substituted for and before the completion of what is emphasised; so both views are deficient according to those versed in reasoning, because أنّ in His saying ألم يعلموا أنه is not complete before the fāʾ, so how can something be substituted for it or emphasise it before it is complete? Its completion is the condition and its apodosis, because the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of أنّ, and it is not complete except with the completion of its khabar.
Al-Akhfash said: it is in the position of the nominative, because the fāʾ has cut off what precedes it from what follows it; its implied form is "then the necessity of the Fire is his". ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: أنّ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "then what is necessary is that the fire of Hell is his". The fāʾ on these two views is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause is the khabar of أنّ. Others said: أنّ in فأن is nominative by "being established" (al-istiqrār), on the assumption of an implied genitive phrase between the fāʾ and أنّ, its implied form being "then for him is that the fire of Hell is his"; that is the view of al-Fārisī and his preference.

mekki-muskil:64-64.t: His saying {أَن تنزل}: أن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "of that it be sent down" (من أن تنزل). On the analogy of the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, it is permissible for it to be in the position of the genitive, intending من, because the preposition is frequently omitted with أن, so it governs while implied; and that is not permissible according to them with anything other than أن, because of how frequently it is omitted with أن specifically.

mekki-muskil:69-69.t:
His saying {كَالَّذِين من قبلكُمْ}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a promising like what those before you were promised".
His saying {كَمَا استمتع}: the kāf is likewise in the position of the accusative, a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "an enjoyment like the enjoyment of those before you".

mekki-muskil:79-79.t: His saying {وَالَّذين لَا يَجدونَ}: الذين is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to المؤمنين. It is not good to conjoin it to المطوعين, because [المطوعين] has not yet been completed as a noun, since فيسخرون is conjoined to يلمزون. So al-Naḥḥās mentioned in al-Iʿrāb, and in my view it is a mistake on his part.

mekki-muskil:81-81.t:
His saying {خلاف رَسُول الله}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); it has also been said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). الخوالف are the women, and its singular is خالفة. فاعل is not pluralised as فواعل except in poetry or in a small amount of speech; they said فارس and فوارس, and هالك and هوالك. They have also said of a man خالفة and خالف when he is not noble.
And whoever reads the sīn with fatḥa in {دَائِرَة السوء}, its meaning is corruption and badness; whoever reads it with ḍamma, its meaning is defeat, affliction, harm and what is hateful. الدائرة is what encompasses a person so that he has no escape from it. It is annexed to السَّوء and السُّوء by way of emphasis and clarification, in the manner of His saying شمس النهار: even if the night were not mentioned the meaning would be known; likewise, even if السوء were not mentioned the meaning would be known from the word الدائرة alone.
«[Translator's note: the remarks on الخوالف and دائرة السوء concern 9:87 and 9:98.]»

mekki-muskil:101-101.t:
His saying {مَرَدُوا}: a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "and of the people of Medina are people who persisted" (قوما مردوا); the genitive phrase is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and لا تعلمهم is also a naʿt of the omitted [noun].
«[Translator's note: the text writes the implied mubtadaʾ as «قوما» in the accusative, as printed.]»

mekki-muskil:103-103.t:
His saying {تطهرهُمْ وتزكيهم}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the implied pronoun in خذ, which is the Prophet ﷺ, and the tāʾ at the beginning of both verbs is for address. It is also permissible that تطهرهم be a naʿt (adjective) of صدقة and تزكيهم a ḥāl from the implied pronoun in خذ; then the tāʾ in تطهرهم is for the feminine of الصدقة, not for address, and تزكيهم is for address.
And whoever reads {مرجون} with hamza takes it from أرجأت الأمر when you postponed it; whoever reads it without hamza takes it from hope (الرجاء). This is the view of al-Mubarrad. It has been said that it too is from postponement: one says أرجأت الأمر and أرجيته meaning "I postponed it" — two dialectal forms.
His saying {قد نبأنا الله من أخباركم}: نبأ has the meaning of أعلم ("inform"), and in principle it is transitive to three objects. It may be restricted to one, but it may not be restricted to two without the third. Likewise it is not permissible to assume that من in His saying من أخباركم is redundant, because if you assumed it to be redundant, نبأ would have become transitive to two objects without the third, and that is not permissible. It has only become transitive to one object, which is نا, and then it is made transitive by a preposition. If you implied a third object, it would be good to assume من redundant according to the doctrine of al-Akhfash, because he allowed من to be redundant in the affirmative; and the implied form would be "Allah has informed us of your news, explained in detail".
«[Translator's note: مرجون and قد نبأنا الله من أخباركم are from 9:106 and 9:94. The text reads «في الجواب», evidently for «في الإيجاب» ("in the affirmative"), and is translated accordingly.]»

mekki-muskil:107-107.t:
His saying {وَالَّذين اتَّخذُوا}: الذين is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is لا يزال بنيانهم.
His saying {ضِرَارًا وَكفرا وَتَفْرِيقًا} {وَإِرْصَادًا}: all of them are accusative as maṣdars (verbal nouns), and it is permissible that they be mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose).
And the hāʾ in بنيانه, in the reading of whoever reads [أسس] with ḍamma or fatḥa, refers back to whoever is the owner of the building. البنيان is the maṣdar of بنى; Abū Zayd reported بنيت بنيانا وبناء وبنية. It has also been said that البنيان is the plural of بنيانة, like تمرة and تمر.
«[Translator's note: لا يزال بنيانهم and بنيانه are from 9:110 and 9:109.]»

mekki-muskil:109-109.t:
His saying {جرف هار}: the original of هار is هائر; Abū Ḥātim said its original is هاور. Then on both views it was transposed (qalb), so the wāw or yāʾ came last, and the nunation caused it to be dropped, just as the wāw and yāʾ were dropped from غاز and رام; that is in the nominative and the genitive. Al-Kisāʾī reported تهور and تهير, and al-Akhfash reported هرت تهار, like خفت تخاف.
The grammarians allowed هار to be treated on the basis of the dropping without the dropped letter being assumed, because of the frequency of its use in transposed form, so that it becomes like a sound word: the rāʾ takes all the case endings, and the dropped letter is not restored in the accusative as is done with غاز and رام. Whoever holds this makes it on the pattern فَعَل, just as they said يوم راح and put it in the nominative, though it is transposed from رائح; but when their use of it in transposed form became frequent they made it فَعَلاً and declined it with all the case endings. It is also permissible according to them to treat it by the analogy, like غاز and رام, so its pattern is فاعل transposed to فالع, then made defective because of the heaviness of the vowel on the weak letter and the entry of nunation, just as they made defective their words قاض, رام and غاز in the nominative and the genitive, and treated them as sound in the accusative because of the lightness of the fatḥa.

mekki-muskil:111-111.t: His saying {وَعدا عَلَيْهِ حَقًا}: two emphasising maṣdars (verbal nouns).

mekki-muskil:112-112.t: His saying {التائبون}: nominative by implying a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are the repentant", or as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar (predicate) omitted; it has also been said that the khabar is His saying الآمرون and what follows it.

mekki-muskil:117-117.t:
His saying {كَاد يزِيغ قُلُوب}: كاد contains an implied pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-ḥadīth); therefore تزيغ follows كاد directly, and القلوب is nominative by تزيغ. It has been said that القلوب is nominative by كاد, and تزيغ is intended to be postponed, as they allowed that with كان in the like of His saying ما كان يصنع فرعون and in His saying وأنه كان يقول سفيهنا. Abū Ḥātim said: whoever reads يزيغ with yāʾ does not make القلوب nominative by كاد. It has been said that كاد contains its noun, which is the pronoun of the party, the group or the tribe, because the Companions of the Prophet, Allah bless him, were mentioned earlier; so القلوب is nominative by تزيغ, and the yāʾ and the tāʾ in تزيغ are equal, because making a plural masculine or feminine is permissible, according to the sense of "plural" and the sense of "group".
The implied pronoun was permitted in كاد, though it is not among those that enter upon a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), only because it must always be followed by a khabar, so it became like the verbs that enter upon a mubtadaʾ and khabar; hence implying its noun in it, and implying the pronoun of the matter in it, is permissible. The like of that is not permissible with عسى, because it may do without a khabar when أن occurs after it, and because its khabar can only be أن and what follows it. أن does not occur after كاد as its khabar except by poetic necessity, and likewise أن is not dropped after عسى except by poetic necessity.

mekki-muskil:121-121.t: His saying {وَاديا}: its plural is أودية. فاعل with [a plural on] أفعِلة has not come except in this one word alone.

mekki-muskil:128-128.t: His saying {عَزِيز عَلَيْهِ مَا عنتم}: ما is in the position of the nominative by عزيز, and عزيز is a naʿt (adjective) of رسول. It is permissible that ما be a mubtadaʾ (subject) and عزيز its khabar (predicate), with the clause a naʿt of رسول. And it is permissible that عزيز be a mubtadaʾ and ما an agent standing in place of the khabar, with the clause a naʿt of رسول.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿كيف وإن يظهروا عليكم لا يرقبوا فيكم إلا ولا ذمة﴾: كيف is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī); ﴿وإن﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl), and إن is conditional; يظهروا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) it; لا يرقبوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); فيكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يرقبوا; إلا [Translator's note: i.e. إلًّا, "bond of kinship"] is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ذمة is conjoined to it.
﴿يرضونكم بأفواههم وتأبى قلوبهم وأكثرهم فاسقون﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; بأفواههم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يرضونكم; تأبى قلوبهم is conjoined to it; أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and فاسقون is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿اشتروا بآيات الله ثمنا قليلا﴾: اشتروا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بآيات is a preposition and its genitive noun; ﴿الله﴾, the Name of Majesty, is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ثمنًا is the object of اشتروا, and قليلا is an adjective.
﴿فصدوا عن سبيله إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون﴾: ساء is a past verb, and ﴿ما﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. «ساءهم الذي كانوا يعملونه» (what they used to do grieved them), or «عملهم» (their deed) if you take ما as maṣdariyya. Or بئس [Translator's note: so in the source; ساء is evidently meant] is a frozen (jāmid) verb, one of the verbs of blame, running in the same way as بئس, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿لا يرقبون في مؤمن إلا ولا ذمة﴾: لا is negating; يرقبون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); في مؤمن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يرقبون; ﴿إلًّا﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and ولا ذمة is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to إلًّا.
﴿وأولئك هم المعتدون﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; أولئك is a demonstrative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); هم is a second mubtadaʾ, and المعتدون is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾, the nominal clause being the khabar of the demonstrative. Or هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and المعتدون is the khabar of أولئك.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿فإن تابوا وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and إن is conditional; تابوا is a past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); وأقاموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة: the two clauses are conjoined to تابوا.
﴿فإخوانكم في الدين﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); إخوانكم is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «فهم إخوانكم» (then they are your brothers); في الدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause ﴿فإن تابوا...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ونفصل الآيات لقوم يعلمون﴾: the wāw is parenthetical, and the clause is a parenthesis between the two conditionals, between His words ﴿فإن تابوا﴾ and His words ﴿وإن نكثوا﴾, to arouse and urge reflection on the rulings that Allah the Exalted has set out in detail. Or the wāw is resumptive and the clause after it is resumptive; on both views the clause has no grammatical position. لقوم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نفصل﴾, and the clause يعلمون is an adjective (naʿt).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وإن نكثوا أيمانهم من بعد عهدهم وطعنوا في دينكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من بعد عهدهم is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and طعنوا في دينكم is also conjoined.
﴿فقاتلوا أئمة الكفر إنهم لا أيمان لهم لعلهم ينتهون﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); قاتلوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and أئمة الكفر is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). إنهم: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun; لا is the lā of generic negation, and أيمان is its noun; ﴿لهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of it, and the clause is the khabar of إنهم. لعل is an abrogating particle, the hāʾ is its noun, and the clause ينتهون is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿ألا تقاتلون قوما نكثوا أيمانهم﴾: ألا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ); تقاتلون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and قومًا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause نكثوا أيمانهم is an adjective (ṣifa) of قومًا. Or the hamza is interrogative and لا is negating, the hamza entering upon it to affirm (taqrīr) the negation of fighting, and urging it from another angle.
﴿وهموا بإخراج الرسول﴾: conjoined to نكثوا; بإخراج is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) هموا.
﴿وهم بدءوكم أول مرة﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause بدءوكم is the khabar (predicate); أول مرة is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), attached to بدءوكم.
﴿أتخشونهم فالله أحق أن تخشوه إن كنتم مؤمنين﴾: the hamza is interrogative. فالله: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and الله is the mubtadaʾ, and أحق is the khabar; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن تخشوه﴾ is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from ﴿الله﴾, i.e. «خشية الله أحق» (fearing Allah is more worthy). إن is conditional, كنتم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and مؤمنين is the khabar of كنتم; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم﴾: قاتلوهم is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); يعذبهم is the answer to the command, made jussive (majzūm) by it.
﴿ويخزهم وينصركم عليهم ويشف صدور قوم مؤمنين﴾: verbs conjoined to يعذبهم.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ويذهب غيظ قلوبهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿يذهب غيظ﴾ is a verb and its object, and the fāʿil (agent) is a pronoun.
﴿ويتوب الله على من يشاء﴾: the wāw is resumptive; يتوب الله is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿على من﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يتوب; من is a relative noun in the position of genitive; يشاء is a verb and its fāʿil is a pronoun; the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿والله عليم حكيم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) in the nominative, and عليم حكيم are two khabars (predicates); the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿أم حسبتم أن تتركوا﴾: أم: a disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) conjunction meaning بل together with the interrogative hamza, the meaning being ﴿بل أحسبتم ...﴾; حسبتم is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); أن and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of حسبتم.
﴿ولما يعلم الله الذين جاهدوا منكم﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl); لما is a jussive particle conveying expectation, and يعلم is jussive (majzūm) by it; الله is the fāʿil, and الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause جاهدوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position, and منكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ولم يتخذوا من دون الله ولا رسوله ولا المؤمنين وليجة﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; يتخذوا is an imperfect, jussive by لم; من دون الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يتخذوا; ولا رسوله is conjoined to الله; وليجة is the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿والله خبير بما تعملون﴾: the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and خبير is the khabar (predicate); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خبير; the clause تعملون is the ṣila of the relative, with no grammatical position; the clause ﴿والله خبير...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ما كان للمشركين أن يعمروا مساجد الله﴾: ما is negating; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; للمشركين is the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان, and أن and what falls within its scope is its postponed noun.
﴿شاهدين على أنفسهم بالكفر﴾: شاهدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in يعمروا; على أنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) شاهدين, and likewise His words بالكفر.
﴿أولئك حبطت أعمالهم وفي النار هم خالدون﴾: أولئك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause حبطت أعمالهم is the khabar (predicate); في النار is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خالدون; هم is a mubtadaʾ, and خالدون is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿إنما يعمر مساجد الله من آمن بالله واليوم الآخر وأقام الصلاة وآتى الزكاة﴾: إنما is [إنّ] restrained [by] the restraining [ما] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); يعمر مساجد الله is an imperfect verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); مَن is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of يعمر; the clause آمن is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position, and what comes after it is conjoined to it.
﴿ولم يخش إلا الله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; يخش is jussive (majzūm) by لم, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to من آمن; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and the Name of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi.
﴿فعسى أولئك أن يكونوا من المهتدين﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa; عسى is a past verb, one of the verbs of hope; أولئك is the noun of عسى, and أن يكونوا is the khabar (predicate) of عسى; من المهتدين is the khabar of يكونوا.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿أجعلتم سقاية الحاج وعمارة المسجد الحرام كمن آمن بالله واليوم الآخر﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position. The hamza is for rebuking, disapproving interrogation; جعلتم سقاية الحاج is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عمارة المسجد الحرام is conjoined to سقاية الحاج. ﴿كمن﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿مَن﴾ is a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause آمن is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position. A muḍāf must be omitted either from the first or from the second so that the two things equated correspond, the implied form being: «أجعلتم أهل سقاية الحاج وعمارة المسجد الحرام كمن آمن» (have you made the people of the giving of drink to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque like one who believed), or: «أجعلتم السقاية والعمارة كإيمان من آمن» (have you made the giving of drink and the maintenance like the faith of one who believed), or «كعمل من آمن» (like the deed of one who believed).
﴿وجاهد في سبيل الله لا يستوون عند الله﴾: conjoined to آمن.
﴿والله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين﴾: a resumption confirming the nullification of the equality, i.e. the two parties are not equal; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause لا يهدي القوم الظالمين is the khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t: ﴿الذين آمنوا وهاجروا وجاهدوا في سبيل الله بأموالهم وأنفسهم أعظم درجة عند الله وأولئك هم الفائزون﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position. الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject); آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position, and what comes after it is conjoined to it; أعظم is the khabar (predicate), and درجة is a tamyīz (specification); عند الله, the adverb, is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿وأولئك هم الفائزون﴾ is a clause conjoined to الذين آمنوا.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿يبشرهم ربهم برحمة منه ورضوان وجنات﴾: يبشرهم ربهم is an imperfect verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent); برحمة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يبشرهم; منه is an adjective (ṣifa); ﴿ورضوان وجنات﴾ are conjoined to رحمة.
﴿لهم فيها نعيم مقيم﴾: لهم is a fronted khabar (predicate); فيها is a ḥāl (circumstantial); نعيم is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and مقيم is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿خالدين فيها أبدا﴾: خالدين is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara, circumstantial); فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خالدين; أبدًا is an adverb (ẓarf), also attached to خالدين.
﴿إن الله عنده أجر عظيم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the Name of Majesty is its noun; the adverb is a fronted khabar (predicate), أجر is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and عظيم is an adjective; the nominal clause is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تتخذوا آباءكم وإخوانكم أولياء﴾: يا is a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), a definite-intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative; ها is for alerting (tanbīh); الذين is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; آمنوا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position. لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil; آباءكم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), إخوانكم is conjoined to it, and أولياء is the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿إن استحبوا الكفر على الإيمان﴾: إن is conditional; استحبوا is a verb and its fāʿil, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); الكفر is the object of استحبوا; على الإيمان is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) استحبوا, which includes the meaning of اختاروا (they chose). The clause ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ومن يتولهم منكم فأولئك هم الظالمون﴾: the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional [noun], mubtadaʾ (subject); يتولهم is the protasis; منكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a pronoun that is a mubtadaʾ; الظالمون is the khabar (predicate) of أولئك or of هم, and the clause is the khabar of أولئك. The clause ﴿ومن يتولهم منكم...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:116-116.t:
﴿إن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض يحيي ويميت﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), the Name of Majesty is its noun (ism), «﴿له﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and «ملك السماوات والأرض» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «يحيي» is a second khabar of «﴿إن﴾», the first khabar being the clause «﴿له ملك السماوات﴾», and «يميت» is conjoined to «يحيي».
﴿وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, «ما» is negative, «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar, «من دون الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), «من» is a connective (ṣila) particle, «ولي» is a postponed mubtadaʾ by position, and «﴿ولا نصير﴾» is conjoined to «﴿من ولي﴾».

muyesser-irab:117-117.t:
﴿لقد تاب الله على النبي والمهاجرين والأنصار الذين اتبعوه في ساعة العسرة﴾: the lām is the answer to an omitted oath, «قد» is a particle of verification (taḥqīq), «تاب الله» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), «على النبي» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «﴿تاب﴾», «المهاجرين والأنصار» is conjoined to «النبي», «﴿الذين﴾» is a naʿt (adjective), the clause «اتبعوه» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position, and «في ساعة العسرة» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «﴿اتبعوه﴾».
﴿من بعد ما كاد يزيغ قلوب فريق منهم﴾: «من بعد» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), to express the severity [of the hardship] and its reaching the utmost limit; the noun of «كاد» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), the clause «يزيغ» is [its] khabar (predicate), «قلوب» is the fāʿil, «فريق» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and «منهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa).
﴿ثم تاب عليهم إنه بهم رءوف رحيم﴾: «ثم» is a conjunction expressing delay (tarākhī), «تاب» is conjoined to the first «تاب», «﴿عليهم﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «تاب»; in «﴿إنه﴾», «إن» is an abrogating particle and the hāʾ is its noun, «﴿بهم﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «رءوف», and «رءوف رحيم» are two khabars of «﴿إن﴾».

muyesser-irab:118-118.t:
﴿وعلى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا﴾: «﴿على الثلاثة﴾» is conjoined to what preceded, «الذين» is an adjective (ṣifa), the clause «خلفوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين», a clause with no grammatical position; «خلفوا» is in the form of the verb whose agent is not named (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. [left behind] from the campaign.
﴿حتى إذا ضاقت عليهم الأرض بما رحبت وضاقت عليهم أنفسهم﴾: «حتى» is a particle of extent (ghāya), «إذا» is an adverb of future time that includes the meaning of condition, the clause «ضاقت» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) to it, «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ضاقت», «الأرض» is the fāʿil (agent), and «بما رحبت» means «برحبها» ("with its vastness"), the bāʾ being a preposition of accompaniment and «ما» being maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun).
﴿وظنوا أن لا ملجأ من الله إلا إليه﴾: «ظنوا» is conjoined to «ضاقت», «أن» is lightened from the heavy [«أنّ»], its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause «﴿لا ملجأ...﴾» is its khabar (predicate); «لا» is the lā of generic negation, «ملجأ» is its noun, «من الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted khabar, «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), and «إليه» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «ملجأ».
﴿ثم تاب عليهم ليتوبوا إن الله هو التواب الرحيم﴾: «ثم» is a conjunction, «تاب» is a past verb, «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «﴿تاب﴾»; in «﴿ليتوبوا﴾» the lām is of causation (taʿlīl), or the lām of consequence (ʿāqiba), or of outcome (ṣayrūra), i.e. their consequence was repentance; «إن» is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), the Name of Majesty is its noun, «﴿هو﴾» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «التواب الرحيم» are two khabars of «﴿هو﴾», and the clause «هو التواب» is the khabar of «إن»; or «﴿هو﴾» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and «التواب الرحيم» are two khabars of «﴿إن﴾».

muyesser-irab:119-119.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: «﴿يا﴾» is a vocative particle; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative (naṣb); «ها» is for alerting (tanbīh), «الذين» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «﴿أي﴾», «آمنوا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين», a clause with no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source reads «يا حرف نداء، أي: منادى…», where «أي» is the parsed word «أيّ» (not the explanatory «أي» "i.e.").]
﴿اتقوا الله وكونوا مع الصادقين﴾: «اتقوا الله» is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «كونوا» is conjoined to «اتقوا», the wāw is the noun of «كان», and «مع الصادقين» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of «كونوا».

muyesser-irab:120-120.t:
﴿ما كان لأهل المدينة ومن حولهم من الأعراب أن يتخلفوا عن رسول الله﴾: «ما» is negative, «كان» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, «﴿لأهل المدينة﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of «كان», «مَن» is conjoined to «﴿أهل﴾», «﴿حولهم﴾» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, the ṣila clause having no grammatical position, «﴿من الأعراب﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), «أن» together with what falls within its scope is the postponed noun of «كان», and «عن رسول الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «﴿يتخلفوا﴾».
﴿ولا يرغبوا بأنفسهم عن نفسه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; «يرغبوا» is accusative (manṣūb) by conjunction, on the view that «﴿لا﴾» is negative, and jussive (majzūm) on the view that «﴿لا﴾» is prohibitive; «﴿بأنفسهم﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «﴿يرغبوا﴾», and «﴿عن نفسه﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. they must accompany him in every circumstance.
﴿ذلك بأنهم لا يصيبهم ظمأ ولا نصب ولا مخمصة في سبيل الله﴾: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «بأنهم» is the khabar, «لا يصيبهم ظمأ» is a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a fāʿil (agent); «ولا نصب ولا مخمصة» is conjoined to «﴿ظمأ﴾», and «﴿في سبيل الله﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the hāʾ, or an adjective (ṣifa) of «مخمصة».
﴿ولا يطئون موطئا يغيظ الكفار﴾: «﴿لا يطئون﴾» is conjoined to «﴿لا يصيبهم﴾», «﴿موطئا﴾» is a mafʿūl bihi, or an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause «يغيظ الكفار» is an adjective of «﴿موطئًا﴾».
﴿ولا ينالون من عدو نيلا﴾: conjoined to what preceded, and «﴿من عدو﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «﴿ينالون﴾».
﴿إلا كتب لهم به عمل صالح﴾: «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr), the clause «كتب» is in the place of an accusative as a ḥāl, the exception being emptied (mufarragh) from the most general of circumstances; «كتب» is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive), «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «﴿كتب﴾», and likewise «﴿به﴾», «عمل» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and «صالح» is a naʿt (adjective).
﴿إن الله لا يضيع أجر المحسنين﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), the Name of Majesty is its noun, and the clause «لا يضيع أجر المحسنين» is the khabar of «إن».

muyesser-irab:121-121.t:
﴿ولا ينفقون نفقة صغيرة ولا كبيرة﴾: conjoined to «﴿لا ينالون﴾», and «نفقة» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ولا يقطعون واديا إلا كتب لهم﴾: conjoined to what preceded.
﴿إلا كتب لهم﴾: the clause is resumptive, from the most general of circumstances, as preceded, with no grammatical position, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is omitted, i.e. «عمل صالح» ("a righteous deed"). [Translator's note: in the previous ayah the same construction was described as a ḥāl in the place of an accusative; here it is called resumptive with no grammatical position — translated as written.]
﴿ليجزيهم الله أحسن ما كانوا يعملون﴾: the lām is of causation (taʿlīl), «يجزي» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن» after the lām, the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied «أن» and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «﴿كتب﴾»; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi, «﴿الله﴾» is the fāʿil (agent), «﴿أحسن﴾» is the second mafʿūl bihi, or a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. «يجزيهم أحسن جزاء» ("He rewards them with the best reward"). «﴿ما﴾» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), «﴿كانوا﴾» is an incomplete, abrogating past verb (kāna and its sisters), the wāw is its noun, and the clause «﴿يعملون﴾» is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:122-122.t:
﴿وما كان المؤمنون لينفروا كافة﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, «ما» is negative, «كان» is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, «المؤمنون» is its noun; in «﴿لينفروا﴾» the lām is the lām of denial (juḥūd), i.e. for emphasising the negation, and «ينفروا» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن» after the lām of denial; the lām and what it governs are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of «كان», and «﴿كافة﴾» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿فلولا نفر من كل فرقة منهم طائفة ليتفقهوا في الدين﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (of eloquent inference), «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), i.e. «هلاّ» ("why not"), «نفر» is a past verb, «﴿من كل فرقة﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «﴿نفر﴾», «منهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective (ṣifa) of «﴿طائفة﴾»; in «﴿ليتفقهوا﴾» the lām is of causation (taʿlīl), «يتفقهوا» is accusative by an implied «أن», the maṣdar formed from «أن» and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «نفر», and «في الدين» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «﴿يتفقهوا﴾». [Translator's note: the source does not explicitly parse «طائفة»; it is the fāʿil of «نفر».]
﴿ولينذروا قومهم إذا رجعوا إليهم لعلهم يحذرون﴾: «﴿ولينذروا﴾» is conjoined to «﴿ليتفقهوا﴾», the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), «قومهم» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); in «﴿إذا رجعوا﴾» the clause «رجعوا» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) [to «إذا»], «﴿إليهم﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «رجعوا», «لعل» and its noun [follow], and the clause «يحذرون» is its khabar. [Translator's note: the source has «واسهما», evidently a misprint for «واسمها» ("and its noun").]

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿قل إن كان آباؤكم وأبناؤكم وإخوانكم وأزواجكم وعشيرتكم وأموال اقترفتموها وتجارة تخشون كسادها ومساكن ترضونها أحب إليكم من الله ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله﴾: إن is conditional; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb; آباؤكم is its noun, and what follows is conjoined to it; أحب is the khabar (predicate) of كان; إليكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial); من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أحب; ﴿ورسوله وجهاد في سبيله﴾ is conjoined to the Name of Majesty, i.e. [more beloved] than emigrating to the two of them.
﴿فتربصوا حتى يأتي الله بأمره والله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين﴾: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); تربصوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); حتى is a particle of limit and genitive; يأتي is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى, and أن with the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar in the genitive, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to تربصوا; الله is the fāʿil, and بأمره is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يأتي; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين﴾ is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿لقد نصركم الله في مواطن كثيرة﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath, قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); نصركم الله is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent); في مواطن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نصركم, and كثيرة is an adjective (ṣifa).
﴿ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يوم is an adverb (ẓarf) conjoined to His words ﴿في مواطن﴾, so it is attached to what the thing it is conjoined to is attached to, the implied form being «ونصركم يوم حنين» (and He helped you on the day of Ḥunayn). ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb for past time, accusative as a badal (substitute) from ﴿يوم حنين﴾; the clause ﴿أعجبتكم﴾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and كثرتكم is the fāʿil.
﴿فلم تغن عنكم شيئا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; تغن is an imperfect, jussive (majzūm) by لم; شيئًا stands in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or is a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وضاقت عليكم الأرض بما رحبت﴾: ضاقت is conjoined to what precedes; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ضاقت; الأرض is the fāʿil; the bāʾ is a preposition meaning مع (with), and ما is maṣdariyya, on the view that the preposition and its genitive noun are in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. «متلبسة برحبها» (together with its vastness), as when you say «دخلت عليه بثياب السفر» (I came in to him in travelling clothes), i.e. clad in them, meaning with travelling clothes.
﴿ثم وليتم مدبرين﴾: conjoined to what precedes; مدبرين is a ḥāl from the tāʾ in وليتم.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿ثم أنزل الله سكينته على رسوله وعلى المؤمنين﴾: ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; أنزل الله is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); سكينته is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); على رسوله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزل; على المؤمنين is conjoined to رسوله.
﴿وأنزل جنودا لم تروها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أنزل جنودًا: conjoined to what precedes; the clause لم تروها is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿جنودًا﴾.
﴿وعذب الذين كفروا وذلك جزاء الكافرين﴾: also conjoined; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and جزاء الكافرين is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t: ﴿ثم يتوب الله من بعد ذلك على من يشاء والله غفور رحيم﴾: conjoined to what precedes, joined with delay; من بعد ذلك is a ḥāl (circumstantial); على من يشاء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يتوب; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and غفور رحيم are its two khabars (predicates).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا: a vocative particle; أي is the one addressed (munādā), a definite-intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative; ها is for alerting (tanbīh); الذين is an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿أي﴾; آمنوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position.
﴿إنما المشركون نجس﴾: إنما is [إنّ] restrained [by] the restraining [ما] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); المشركون نجس are mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
﴿فلا يقربوا المسجد الحرام﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa; لا is prohibitive; يقربوا is an imperfect, jussive (majzūm) by it; the wāw is the fāʿil; المسجد is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and الحرام is an adjective.
﴿بعد عامهم هذا﴾: the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يقربوا; عامهم is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); هذا is a naʿt (adjective) of عامهم, or a badal (substitute) from it.
﴿وإن خفتم عيلة فسوف يغنيكم الله من فضله إن شاء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; خفتم is a verb and its fāʿil, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); عيلة is the mafʿūl bihi. فسوف: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa), and سوف is a particle of the future; يغنيكم الله is an imperfect verb, its mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); من فضله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يغنيكم; إن is conditional and شاء is its verb, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. «فسوف يغنيكم» (then He will enrich you).
﴿إن الله عليم حكيم﴾: إن is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is its noun, and عليم حكيم are its two khabars.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿قاتلوا الذين لا يؤمنون بالله ولا باليوم الآخر﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position. قاتلوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); الذين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause لا يؤمنون is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يؤمنون; ولا باليوم الآخر is conjoined to الله.
﴿ولا يحرمون ما حرم الله ورسوله﴾: conjoined to what precedes; ما is the object of يحرمون, and the clause حرم الله ورسوله is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿ولا يدينون دين الحق﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿دين﴾: the maṣdar (verbal noun) of يدينون, so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or a mafʿūl bihi with يدينون made to include the meaning of يعتقدون (they believe).
﴿من الذين أوتوا الكتاب﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يدينون, or from the first الذين together with what falls within its scope; the clause أوتوا الكتاب is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position, and الكتاب is the second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد﴾: حتى is a particle of limit and genitive; يعطوا is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى, and أن with the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar in the genitive, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to قاتلوا; الجزية is the mafʿūl bihi, and عن يدٍ is a ḥāl.
﴿وهم صاغرون﴾: a second ḥāl; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and صاغرون is the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿وقالت اليهود عزير ابن الله﴾: the wāw is resumptive; قالت اليهود is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿عزير﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ﴿ابن الله﴾ is the khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿وقالت اليهود...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿وقالت النصارى المسيح ابن الله﴾: a clause conjoined to the one before it; ﴿قالت النصارى﴾ is a verb and its fāʿil; ﴿المسيح﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, and ﴿ابن الله﴾ is the khabar; the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿ذلك قولهم بأفواههم﴾: ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, and قولهم is the khabar; ﴿بأفواههم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿يضاهئون قول الذين كفروا من قبل﴾: the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); قول is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذين is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position; من قبل is a ḥāl.
﴿قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون﴾: قاتلهم الله is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil; the clause is a supplication (duʿāʾiyya) with no grammatical position. أنى is an interrogative noun meaning كيف (how), in the position of accusative as a fronted ḥāl; يؤفكون is an imperfect verb in the passive (built for one whose agent is not named), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. how are they turned away from the truth.

muyesser-irab:123-123.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: «﴿يا﴾» is a vocative particle; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative (naṣb); «ها» is for alerting (tanbīh), «الذين» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «﴿أي﴾», «آمنوا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين», a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿قاتلوا الذين يلونكم من الكفار﴾: «قاتلوا» is an imperative verb and its fāʿil, «الذين» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the clause «يلونكم» is the ṣila of «الذين», a clause with no grammatical position, and «من الكفار» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿وليجدوا فيكم غلظة واعلموا أن الله مع المتقين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the lām of command, «يجدوا» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command, the wāw is the fāʿil, «فيكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «﴿يجدوا﴾», «غلظة» is a mafʿūl bihi, «اعلموا» is conjoined to the preceding command, and «أن» together with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of «اعلموا»; «أن» is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), the Name of Majesty is its noun, and «﴿مع المتقين﴾» is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to its omitted khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:124-124.t:
﴿وإذا ما أنزلت سورة﴾: the wāw is resumptive, «إذا» is an adverb of future time that includes the meaning of condition, «ما» is connective (ṣila), the clause «أنزلت» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) to it, and «سورة» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿فمنهم من يقول أيكم زادته هذه إيمانا﴾: the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa, linking the apodosis), «﴿منهم﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and «﴿مَن﴾» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); it is a relative noun, or a complete indefinite (nakira tāmma) qualified by the clause «يقول», i.e. «فريق يقول» ("a party who says"); the clause «يقول» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «﴿مَن﴾», with no grammatical position; «أيكم» is a mubtadaʾ, the clause «زادته» is [its] khabar, the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «﴿هذه﴾» is the fāʿil (agent), and «إيمانًا» is a second mafʿūl bihi; the clause «﴿وإذا ما أنزلت...﴾» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فأما الذين آمنوا فزادتهم إيمانا وهم يستبشرون﴾: the fāʾ is of ramification (tafrīʿiyya), «﴿أما﴾» is a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl), «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ, the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila of «الذين», a clause with no grammatical position, the fāʾ is connective, «زادتهم» is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of «﴿الذين﴾», and «إيمانًا» is a second mafʿūl bihi or a tamyīz (specification).

muyesser-irab:125-125.t:
﴿وأما الذين في قلوبهم مرض فزادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم﴾: «أما» is conjoined to «﴿أما﴾» in the previous ayah, «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «في قلوبهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), «مرض» is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين», with no grammatical position; in «﴿فزادتهم﴾» the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), the clause «زادتهم» is the khabar of «الذين», «رجسًا» is a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «إلى رجسهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa), i.e. «مضمومًا إلى رجسهم» ("added to their filth").
﴿وماتوا وهم كافرون﴾: conjoined to «زادتهم»; the wāw is circumstantial (of ḥāl), and the clause «﴿هم كافرون﴾», made of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause.

muyesser-irab:126-126.t:
﴿أولا يرون أنهم يفتنون في كل عام مرة أو مرتين﴾: the hamza is for interrogation of disapproval and rebuke, the wāw is a conjunction joining to something implied, «يرون» is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), «أن» together with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of the verb of mental perception (ruʾya qalbiyya), the clause «يفتنون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن», «في كل عام» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «﴿يفتنون﴾», «مرة» is a stand-in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is its number, «أو» is a conjunction, and «﴿مرتين﴾» is conjoined to «﴿مرة﴾». [Translator's note: the source writes «خبر إن»; the particle in the ayah is «أنّ».]
﴿ثم لا يتوبون ولا هم يذكرون﴾: «ثم» is a conjunction of delay (tarākhī), the clause «لا يتوبون» is conjoined to «يفتنون», the wāw is a conjunction, «﴿هم﴾» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «يذكرون» is [its] khabar.

muyesser-irab:127-127.t:
﴿وإذا ما أنزلت سورة نظر بعضهم إلى بعض﴾: conjoined to what preceded; the clause «نظر بعضهم» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «﴿إذا﴾», with no grammatical position, and «﴿إلى بعض﴾» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «﴿نظر﴾».
﴿هل يراكم من أحد﴾: the clause is in the position of an accusative, the speech-content (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. «قائلين» ("saying"), and the clause of saying is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); «يراكم» is an imperfect verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), «من» is a connective (ṣila) particle, and «أحد» is the fāʿil (agent) by position.
﴿ثم انصرفوا صرف الله قلوبهم بأنهم قوم لا يفقهون﴾: «﴿ثم انصرفوا﴾» is conjoined to «﴿نظر بعضهم﴾»; the clause «﴿صرف الله قلوبهم﴾» may validly be informative and circumstantial (ḥāliyya), or performative and supplicatory, in which case it has no grammatical position; «﴿بأنهم﴾» is attached to «صرف», the bāʾ being causal, «﴿أن﴾» is an abrogating particle, the hāʾ is its noun, and the clause «﴿لا يفقهون﴾» is its khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:128-128.t:
