The majority [read] «جباهُهم» with clear pronunciation (iẓhār), and Abū ʿAmr in some of his transmission routes read it with assimilation (idghām), just as he assimilated {سَلَكَكُمْ} [al-Muddaththir: 42] and {مَّنَاسِكَكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 200]. Like جباههم is «وجوههم», in which clear pronunciation is the well-known [reading].
His words: {هذا مَا كَنَزْتُمْ لأَنْفُسِكُمْ}: governed by an omitted verb of saying, i.e. that will be said to them on the day it is heated. His words {مَا كُنتُمْ تَكْنِزُونَ}: i.e. the recompense of what you used to [hoard], because what is hoarded is not tasted. «ما» may mean "that which", the returning pronoun being omitted, or it may be maṣdariyya. It was also read «تَكْنُزون» with ḍamma on the middle radical of the imperfect; they are two dialects: one says كَنَزَ يَكْنِز and كَنَزَ يَكْنُز.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِنَّ عِدَّةَ}: al-ʿidda is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning number. «عند الله» is in the accusative by it, i.e. in His ruling. «اثنا عشر» is the khabar (predicate) of inna. Hubayra from Ḥafṣ read — and it is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar — «اثنا عْشَرَ» with sukūn on the ʿayn while retaining the alif before it. It was found objectionable in that it combines two vowelless letters not according to their [permitted] conditions, like their saying «التقت حَلْقتا البِطان» with the alif of «حَلْقتا» retained. Ṭalḥa read with sukūn on the shīn, as though he treated عشر in the masculine like عشرة in the feminine.
«شَهْراً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and it is emphatic, because that was already understood from the first [word]; it is like your saying «عندي من الدنانير عشرون ديناراً». The plural differs in His words «عدَّة الشهور» and in His words {الحج أَشْهُرٌ} [al-Baqara: 197], because this is a plural of multitude and that is a plural of paucity.
His words: {فِي كِتَابِ الله}: it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «اثنا عشر». It may [also, as was said,] be a badal (substitute) of the adverbial before it; but this is not permissible, or is weak, because it entails giving a predicate about the relative [i.e. the maṣdar ʿidda] before its ṣila is complete, since this preposition phrase is attached to it by way of substitution. And even supposing that this is valid technically, how can it be valid in meaning? Nor may {فِي كِتَابِ الله} be attached to «عدة», lest it entail separating the maṣdar from what it governs by its khabar. The analogy of whoever allowed its substitution for the adverbial is that he should allow this; and al-Ḥawfī explicitly allowed it.
His words: {يَوْمَ خَلَقَ}: it may be attached to «كتاب», on the view that the maṣdar is meant by it and not a concrete thing. It may be attached to the [notion of] existence (al-istiqrār) in the preposition phrase {فِي كِتَابِ الله}, the book then being a concrete thing, not a maṣdar. Al-Ḥawfī allowed it to be attached to «عدة», which is rejected by what has preceded.
His words: {مِنْهَآ أَرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ}: three views are possible for this clause. First: it is an adjective of «اثنا عشر». Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in the [notion of] existence. Third: it is resumptive. The pronoun in «منها» refers back to {اثنا عَشَرَ شَهْراً}, because it is the nearest thing mentioned, not to «الشهور». The pronoun in «فيهنَّ» also refers back to «الاثنا عشر». Al-Farrāʾ and Qatāda said: it refers back to the four sacred [months], and this is better for two reasons. First: it is the nearest thing mentioned. Second: it is established that treating a plural of paucity of non-rational beings like a group of females is better than treating it with the singular feminine pronoun, and the plural of multitude the reverse: «الأجذاع انكسَرْن» and «الجذوع انكسرت»; the reverse is also permissible.
His words: {كَآفَّةً}: accusative as a ḥāl, either of the fāʿil (agent) or of the object. It has preceded that «كافَّة» is used only in the accusative as a ḥāl, that al- does not enter it, and that it is neither dualised nor pluralised; likewise the second «كافة».

semin-durr:37-37.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِنَّمَا النسياء}: there are two views on «النسِيْء». First: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern فَعِيل from أَنْسَأ, i.e. "he postponed", like النذير from أَنْذَر and النكير from أَنْكر. This is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words, for he said: "Al-nasīʾ is postponing the sanctity of a month to another month." In that case predicating «وزيادة» of it is clear and needs no supposition. Al-Ṭabarī said: "Al-nasīʾ with hamza means increase." I say: because it is a postponement in time, increase follows from it.
Second: it is a فَعِيل in the sense of مَفْعول (passive participle), from نَسَأه, i.e. he postponed it, so it is منسوء; then مفعول was converted into فعيل, just as مفعول was converted into فعيل [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably a reference to parallel words such as قتيل from مقتول]. Abū Ḥātim and al-Jawharī inclined to this. Al-Fārisī rejected this view on the grounds that the meaning would be: "the postponed [thing] is only an increase", the postponed thing being the month, and the month cannot be an increase in unbelief. Some answered this by supposing the omission of a muḍāf, either from the first, i.e. "the postponing of what is postponed is only an increase in unbelief", or from the second, i.e. "what is postponed is only a thing of increase".
The majority read «النَّسيء» with a hamza after the yāʾ. Warsh from Nāfiʿ read «النَّسِيّ», changing the hamza into yāʾ and assimilating the [preceding] yāʾ into it; this was also related from Abū Jaʿfar, al-Zuhrī and Ḥumayd, just as they lightened «برية» and «خطية». Al-Sulamī, Ṭalḥa, al-Ashhab and Shibl read «النَّسْء» with sukūn on the sīn. Mujāhid, al-Sulamī and Ṭalḥa also read «النَّسُوء» on the pattern فَعُول with fatḥa on the first radical, which is postponement; فَعول is rare among maṣdars, and a few small words of it have preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. The derivation of this root has preceded in al-Baqara. Here it denotes postponing some months after others. He said:
2483 - ألَسْنا الناسئينَ على مَعَدٍّ ... شهورَ الحِلِّ نجعلُها حَراما
(Are we not the ones who postpone the months for Maʿadd, making the lawful months sacred?)
Another said:
2484 - نَسَؤُوا الشّهور بها وكانوا أهلَها ... مِنْ قبلِكم والعزُّ لم يتحوَّلِ
(They postponed the months in it, and they were its people before you, while might had not shifted.)
His words: {يُضَلُّ بِهِ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «يُضَلُّ» in the passive, and the rest in the active [يَضِلُّ], with the relative noun as its fāʿil (agent). Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Qatāda, Yaʿqūb and ʿAmr ibn Maymūn read «يُضِلُّ», active, from أضل. There are two views on the fāʿil. First: the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, i.e. Allah leads astray those who disbelieved. Second: the fāʿil is «الذين كفروا», and on this view the object is omitted, i.e. those who disbelieved lead astray their followers. Abū Rajāʾ read «يَضَلُّ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ḍād; it is from ضَلِلْت with kasra on the lām, أضَلُّ with fatḥa on it; the original form is أَضْلَلُ, and the fatḥa of the lām was transferred to the ḍād for the sake of assimilation. Al-Nakhaʿī, and al-Ḥasan in the transmission of Maḥbūb, read «نُضِلُّ» with ḍamma on the nūn of majesty, «الذين» being the object; this strengthens [the view] that the fāʿil is the pronoun of Allah in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd.
His words: {يُحِلُّونَهُ}: two views. First: the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) of the going astray. Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His words: {لِّيُوَاطِئُواْ}: there are two views on this lām. [First:] it is attached to «يُحَرِّفونه» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «يُحَرِّمُونَهُ»]. This is what the doctrine of the Basrans requires, for they give government to the second of two competing [governors]. Second: it is attached to «يُحِلُّونه»; this is what the doctrine of the Kufans requires, for they give government to the first because it comes first. The saying of whoever said that it is attached to both verbs together means only in meaning, not in wording.
Abū Jaʿfar read «ليوطِيُوا» with kasra on the ṭāʾ and ḍamma on a pure yāʾ. The correct [form] is that it ought to be read with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ and the yāʾ dropped, because when he changed the hamza into yāʾ, the ḍamma on it was found heavy and was dropped; then two vowelless letters met, so the yāʾ was dropped and the ṭāʾ given ḍamma to match the wāw.
Al-muwāṭaʾa is agreement and coming together. One says: تواطَؤُوا على كذا, i.e. they came together on it, as if each one treads (yaṭaʾu) where the other treads. From it is His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ الليل هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْأً} [al-Muzzammil: 6], also read وِطاءً; it will come, if Allah wills.
Al-Zuhrī read «ليواطِيُّوا» with a doubled yāʾ. That is how they described his reading, and it is problematic, so much so that someone said: "If he did not mean by it a strong articulation of the yāʾ and freeing it from the hamza, without doubling, I do not know its justification." It is as he said.
His words: «زُيِّنَ»: the majority read «زُيِّن» in the passive, the omitted fāʿil being Satan. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it in the active, [the fāʿil] being Satan too, and «سوء» its object.

semin-durr:38-38.t:
The words of the Exalted: {اثاقلتم}: its original form is تثاقلتم. When assimilation was intended, the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the tāʾ is meant] was made vowelless and a connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in, as preceded at {فادارأتم} [al-Baqara: 72], whose original form is تدارأتم. Al-Aʿmash read «تثاقلتم» in this original form. «ما» in His words «مالكم» is interrogative, with a sense of disapproval in it. It was said: its [i.e. of «قيل»] omitted fāʿil (agent) is the Messenger.
«اثَّاقلتم» is past in wording and imperfect in meaning, i.e. they are being sluggish; it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it governs the adverbial, i.e. "what is the matter with you, being sluggish at the time of the saying?" Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "اثَّاقلتم is a past verb in the sense of the imperfect, i.e. what is the matter with you that you are sluggish; it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. what [good] is there for you in sluggishness; or in the position of the genitive according to the opinion of al-Khalīl. It was also said: it is in the position of a ḥāl." The Shaykh said: "This is not good, because it entails the omission of «أَنْ», since a maṣdar is only formed from a maṣdar particle and the verb, and omitting «أَنْ» in such a case is very rare, or a poetic necessity. And if the implied form is 'in sluggishness', it cannot govern «إذا», because what is governed by the relative maṣdar does not precede it; so what governs «إذا» in the accusative, and what 'in sluggishness' is attached to, is what «لكم», occurring as the khabar (predicate) of «ما», is attached to."
It was also read «أَثَّاقَلْتم» with the interrogative whose meaning is disapproval. In that case it may not govern «إذا», because what follows an interrogative particle does not govern what precedes it; so the governor of this adverbial is either the [notion of] existence implied in «لكم», or something implied that the wording indicates, the implied form being: "what do you do when it is said to you?". Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this. What appears [best] is to suppose: "what is the matter with you that you are sluggish when it is said", so that it is indicated both by the wording and by the meaning.
His words: {إِلَى الأرض}: it implies the meaning of inclining and clinging. His words «من الآخرة»: the statements of the grammatical analysts and commentators concur that «مِنْ» means "instead of", as in His words {لَجَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ مَّلاَئِكَةً} [al-Zukhruf: 60], i.e. instead of you. Like it are the words of the other [poet]:
2485 - جاريةٌ لم تَأْكُلِ المُرَقَّقا ... ولم تَذُقْ من البُقول الفُسْتُقا
(A girl who has not eaten thin bread, nor tasted pistachios instead of vegetables.)
and the words of the other:
2486 - فليت لنا مِنْ ماءِ زمزمَ شَرْبةً ... مُبَرَّدَةً باتَتْ على طَهَيانِ
(Would that we had, instead of the water of Zamzam, a cooled draught that spent the night on [Mount] Ṭahayān.)
However, most grammarians do not affirm this meaning for it and interpret whatever suggests it; the implied form here is: "you have held fast [away] from the Hereafter, content with the life", and likewise the rest of them. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«من الآخرة» is in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. in place of the Hereafter"; so he supposed the attachment to be specific, though he may have intended to explain the meaning.
His words: {فِي الآخرة}: attached to something omitted in terms of meaning, its implied form being: "the enjoyment of the life of this world, counted in the Hereafter, is only…"; «محسوباً» is thus a ḥāl of «متاع». Al-Ḥawfī said: "It is attached to «قليل», which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject)." He said: "It is permissible for the adverbial to precede its governor that is joined with «إلا», because adverbials are governed by mere traces of verbs. Had you said «ما زيدٌ عمراً إلا يَضْرب», it would not be permissible."

semin-durr:40-40.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِلاَّ تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ}: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of this condition is omitted because His words «فقد نصره» indicate it; the implied form is: "If you do not help him, He will help him." Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned two views on it, one of them being what has preceded. The second, he said: "He made help obligatory for him and made him helped at that time, so he will not be forsaken after it." The Shaykh said: "From this the apodosis of the condition does not appear, because making help obligatory for him is something that preceded, and the past does not follow upon the future; so what appears [correct] is the first view."
His words: {ثَانِيَ اثنين}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of «أخرجه». The meaning of the annexation in this kind of construction has preceded at His words {ثَالِثُ ثَلاَثَةٍ} [al-Māʾida: 73]. A group read «ثاني اثنين» with sukūn on the yāʾ. Abū al-Fatḥ said: "Abū ʿAmr reported it." Its justification is that he made the yāʾ vowelless, likening it to the alif; some restrict this to poetic necessity.
His words: {إِذْ هُمَا فِي الغار}: a badal (substitute) of the first «إذ», so what governs it is «فقد نَصَره». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Whoever denies that what governs the badal is what governs the thing substituted for supposes another governor, i.e. He helped him «إذ هما في الغار»."
«الغار» is a hollow in a mountain; it is pluralised as غِيران, like تاج and تِيْجان, قاع and قِيعان. Al-ghār is also a sweet-smelling plant, al-ghār is also a group, and al-ghārān are the belly and the private parts. The alif of al-ghār is from wāw.
His words: {إِذْ يَقُولُ}: a second badal of the first «إذ». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«إذ هما في الغار» and «إذ يقول» are two adverbials of «ثاني اثنين»." The pronoun in «عليه» refers back to Abū Bakr, because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ always had tranquillity upon him. The discussion of {السكينة} [al-Baqara: 248] has preceded. The pronoun in «أيَّده» is for the Prophet ﷺ. Mujāhid read «وأَيَدَه» without doubling. «لم تَرَوْها» is a naʿt (adjective) of «جنود».
His words: {وَكَلِمَةُ الله هِيَ العليا}: the majority read «كلمة» in the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). «هي» may be a second mubtadaʾ, with «العُلْيا» its khabar (predicate) and the clause the khabar of the first; or «هي» may be a separating pronoun (faṣl) and «العليا» the khabar. It was also read «وكلمةَ الله» in the accusative, coordinated with the two objects of جَعَلَ, i.e. "and He made the word of Allah the highest". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak for three reasons. First: putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, since the proper way is to say وكَلِمَتُه. Second: it implies that the word of Allah was the lowest and then became the highest, which is not so. Third: emphasising such a thing with «هي» is far-fetched, since analogy requires «إياها»." I say: as for the first, there is no weakness in it, because the Qur'an is full of this kind, and it is among the best [usages], because there is magnification and exaltation in it. As for the second, what he mentioned does not follow, namely that the thing made into [something] was in the specific opposite state; rather, the "making" indicates the passing of that thing from some state to this state. As for the third, «هي» is not emphasis at all; «هي» is only a separating pronoun as it stands. How could it be emphasis, when the grammarians have stated explicitly that a pronoun does not emphasise an overt noun?

semin-durr:41-41.t: {خِفَافاً وَثِقَالاً} is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «انفروا».

semin-durr:42-42.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لَوْ كَانَ عَرَضاً}: the noun (ism) of kāna is a pronoun referring back to what the context indicates, i.e. "had what you called them to been…". ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Aʿraj read «بَعِدَت» with kasra on the middle radical. ʿĪsā also read «الشِّقَّة» with kasra on the shīn. Abū Ḥātim said: "Both are the dialect of Tamīm."
Al-shuqqa is the land which is traversed (yushaqqu) with difficulty; it is derived from al-shiqq or al-mashaqqa (hardship).
His words: {بالله}: attached to «سَيَحْلِفُون». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«بالله» is attached to «سَيَحْلِفُون», or it is part of their speech, the [verb of] saying being intended in both views; i.e. they will swear — meaning those who stayed behind, when you return, making excuses — saying: 'By Allah, had we been able…'; or: and they will swear by Allah, saying: 'Had we been able…'. And His words «لَخَرَجْنا» fill the place of both the answer of the oath and [that of] «لو»." The Shaykh said: "His saying that «لخَرَجْنا» fills the place of both the answer of the oath and «لو» is not good. Rather, the grammarians have two doctrines on such a case. One: «لَخَرَجْنا» is the answer of the oath, and the answer of «لو» is omitted, according to the rule for the combination of oath and condition, since the oath precedes the condition; this is the choice of Abū al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUṣfūr. The other: «لَخَرَجْنا» is the answer of «لو», and «لو» with its answer is the answer of the oath; this is the choice of Ibn Mālik. As for «لَخَرَجْنا» filling the place of both, I know of no one who held that. His words may be interpreted as meaning that, since the answer of «لو» was omitted and the answer of the oath indicated it, it was treated as if it filled the place of both the answer of the oath and the answer of لو."
Al-Aʿmash and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «لوُ اسْتَطَعْنا» with ḍamma on the wāw, as though they fled from the kasra on the wāw, even though it is the base; they likened the wāw of «لو» to the wāw of the pronoun, just as they likened the wāw of the pronoun to the wāw of «لو» when they gave it kasra, as in {اشتروا الضلالة} [al-Baqara: 16], because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. Al-Ḥasan read «اشْتَرَوَا الضلالة» and «لوَ استطعنا» with fatḥa on the wāw, for lightness.
His words: {يُهْلِكُونَ}: there are three views on this clause. First: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «سَيَحْلِفُون», i.e. they will swear, destroying themselves. Second: it is a badal (substitute) of the clause before it, «سَيَحْلِفون». Third: it is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «لَخَرَجْنا». Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these three views, saying: "«يُهْلِكون» is either a badal of «سيحلفون» or a ḥāl in the sense of 'destroying'. The meaning is that they cast themselves into destruction by their false swearing. It may be a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «خَرَجْنا», i.e. we would have gone out even if we destroyed ourselves. It came in the third-person form because He is giving information about them. Do you not see that if it were said: 'they will swear by Allah, had they been able they would have gone out', it would be sound? One says: حَلَفَ بالله ليفعلن and لأفعلن; the third person follows the rule of reporting, and the first person follows that of quotation."
The Shaykh said: "As for «يُهْلِكون» being a badal of «سَيَحْلِفون», it is far-fetched, because destroying is neither synonymous with swearing nor a kind of it, and a verb is substituted for a verb only if it is synonymous with it or a kind of it." I say: the badal is valid in the sense of a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because swearing is a cause of destruction and so includes it; the effect was substituted for its cause because the cause includes it. It has many parallels, among them his words:
2487 - إنَّ عليَّ اللَّهَ أن تُبايعا ... تُؤْخَذَ كَرْهاً أو تجيءَ طائعاً
(I owe it to Allah that you shall give allegiance: be taken by force or come willingly.)
«تُؤْخَذ» is a badal of «تبايع», a badal of inclusion in the sense mentioned, and neither is a kind of the other. Then the Shaykh said: "As for its being a ḥāl of His words «لخرجنا», [what appears is that it is not permissible, because His words «لخَرَجْنا»] contain the pronoun of the speaker, so what is predicated of it can only be with the pronoun of the speaker. Were it a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «لخَرَجنا», the construction would be: نُهْلك أنفسنا, i.e. destroying ourselves. As for his drawing an analogy with «حَلَفَ زيد ليفعلن» and «لأفعلنَّ», it is not correct, because if he treats it according to the third-person pronoun, he does not go out of it to the pronoun of the speaker. Were you to say «حَلَفَ زيد ليفعلن وأنا قائم», with «وأنا قائم» as a ḥāl of the pronoun of «ليفعلن», it would not be permissible; and likewise its reverse, as in «حَلَفَ زيدٌ لأفعلن يقوم», meaning 'standing', would not be permissible. As for his saying 'it came in the third-person form because He is giving information about them', it is a fallacy: He is not giving information about them by His words {لَوِ استطعنا لَخَرَجْنَا}; rather He is quoting the wording of their speech. Then he said: 'Do you not see that if it were said: had they been able they would have gone out, it would be sound…' to the end: that is correct speech, but the Exalted did not say it as information about them; rather it is quotation, and the ḥāl is part of their quoted speech, so it may not differ from the one it qualifies, since they share the governor. Were you to say «قال زيد خرجت يضرب خالداً», meaning 'I went out striking Khālid', it would not be permissible; and were you to say «قالت هند: خرج زيد اضربْ خالداً», meaning 'Zayd went out striking Khālid', it would not be permissible." End of quotation.
Fourth: it is a resumptive clause; Allah informed about them with it.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ}: «لِمَ» and «لهم» are both attached to أَذِنْتَ. That is permissible because the meanings of the two lāms differ: the first is causal and the second is for conveying [to the addressee]. The alif of the interrogative ما was dropped because it is in the genitive. Fronting the first preposition phrase is obligatory because it governs something that has the right to the head of the sentence. What the permission relates to is omitted. It may be staying behind, i.e. "why did you permit them to stay behind?", which the context indicates, from their excusing themselves for lagging behind him, upon him be peace. Or it may be going out, i.e. "why did you permit them to go out?", because their going out involves harm, such as discouraging [others] and the like, as {لَوْ خَرَجُواْ فِيكُم مَّا زَادُوكُمْ إِلاَّ خَبَالاً} [al-Tawba: 47] indicates.
His words: {حتى يَتَبَيَّنَ}: «حتى» may express the limit, or it may be causal. On both suppositions it is a preposition, meaning either "until" or [that of] the lām, with «أَنْ» implied after it putting the verb in the accusative; and it is attached to something omitted. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its implied form is: why did you not defer them until it became clear, or so that it might become clear. His words {لِمَ أَذِنتَ لَهُمْ} indicate the omitted part. «حتى» may not be attached to «أَذِنْتَ», because that would require that he gave them permission up to this limit or for the sake of clarification, and he would not be reproached for that." Al-Ḥawfī said: "«حتى» is a limit for what the interrogative implies, i.e. he ought not to have given them permission until the excuse became clear to him." I say: there is some impropriety in this wording.

semin-durr:44-44.t: The words of the Exalted: {أَن يُجَاهِدُواْ}: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: it is what the asking for permission relates to, i.e. they do not ask your permission concerning striving; rather they go ahead with it without hesitation. The second: what the asking for permission relates to is omitted, and «أن يُجاهدوا» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), its implied form being: "the believers do not ask your permission to go out or to stay behind out of dislike of striving; rather, when you command them with something, they hasten to it."

semin-durr:46-46.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لأَعَدُّواْ لَهُ عُدَّةً}: the generality read «عُدّة» with ḍamma on the ʿayn and the tāʾ of the feminine; it is the provisions, the mount and everything the traveller needs.
Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān and his son Muʿāwiya read «عُدَّهُ» likewise, except that in place of the tāʾ of the feminine he put the hāʾ of the third-person pronoun, referring back to the going out. There was disagreement on how to account for it. It was said: its origin is like the majority reading with the tāʾ of the feminine, but they drop it in annexation, like the tanwīn. Al-Farrāʾ counted among this His words, the Exalted: {وَإِقَامَ الصلاة} [al-Nūr: 37], and from it are the words of Zuhayr:
2488 - إنَّ الخَلِيْطَ أجَدُّوا البَيْنَ فانْجَرَدُوا ... وأَخْلَفُوك عِدَ الأمرِ الذي وَعدُوا
(The companions resolved on parting and went off quickly, and broke with you the promise of the matter they had promised.)
He means: عِدَّة الأمر. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "When he annexed it, he made the pronoun stand in for the tāʾ and dropped it; that is because العُدّ without tāʾ, and without supposing it, is something that comes out on the face [Translator's note: i.e. a pimple]." Abū Ḥātim said: "It is the plural of عُدَّة, like بُرّ, plural of بُرّة, and دُرّ, plural of دُرَّة; the proper form for it would be عُدَد, but that does not agree with the script of the muṣḥaf."
Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Abān, read «عِدَّهُ» with kasra on the ʿayn, annexed to the pronoun hāʾ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In my view it is a noun for what is prepared, like الذِّبْح and القِتْل." It was also read «عِدَّة» with kasra on the ʿayn and the tāʾ of the feminine, the meaning being a quantity of provisions and weapons, derived from al-ʿadad (number).
His words: {ولكن كَرِهَ الله}: the restriction (istidrāk) here requires reflection; that is why al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the position of the particle of restriction? I say: since His words {وَلَوْ أَرَادُواْ الخروج} convey the negation of their going out and of their preparing for the campaign, it was said: but Allah disliked [their setting out]; as if it were said: they did not go out, but they held back from going out because of [Allah's] dislike of their setting out; just as [you say: Zayd did not] treat me well, but he treated me badly." End of quotation. He means that the apparent sense of the verse requires that what follows «لكن» agrees with what precedes it, while it is established about it that it occurs only between two contraries, two contradictories, or two different things — with a disagreement over this last — so he needed the answer mentioned.
The Shaykh said: "The verse is not a parallel to this example," meaning: Zayd did not treat me well but he treated me badly, "because in the example «لكن» occurs between [two contraries, whereas in the verse «لكن» occurs between] two things that agree in meaning." I say: by "two contradictories" they mean negation and affirmation in wording, even if they meet in meaning, and that is not counted as agreement.
Al-tathbīṭ is hindering. One says: ثَبَّطْتُ زيداً, i.e. I hindered him from what he wanted; from their saying: ناقة ثَبِطَة, i.e. slow in pace. What is meant by His words «اقعدوا» is leaving [them] alone; it is a metonymy for their sluggishness, and [indicates] that they made themselves like women, or children, the chronically ill and those with excuses. Sitting [literally] is not meant, as in his words:
2489 - دَعِ المكارِم لا تَقْصِدْ لبُغْيَتها ... واقعُدْ فإنَّك أنت الطاعِمُ الكاسي
(Leave noble deeds, do not set out to seek them, and sit [at home], for you are the one who is fed and clothed.)

semin-durr:47-47.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لَوْ خَرَجُواْ فِيكُم}: i.e. in your army and in your company. It was said: «في» means "with", i.e. with you. The explanation of «الخبال» has preceded in Āl ʿImrān.
His words: {إِلاَّ خَبَالاً}: they allowed it to be a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil) which is emptied (mufarragh), because «زاد» takes two objects. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "What is excepted from is not mentioned, so the exception is from the most general of the general, which is 'thing'; so it is a connected exception, because al-khabāl (corruption) is a part of the most general of the general; as though it were said: they would not have increased you in anything but corruption." They also allowed it to be a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), the meaning being: they would not have increased you in strength or might, but in corruption. This fits the view of whoever said that there was no corruption in the army of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; so said the Shaykh. This is questionable, because if there was no corruption in the army at all, how could something be excepted that did not exist and whose existence was not imagined?
His words: {خِلاَلَكُمْ}: accusative as an adverbial. Al-khilāl is the plural of خَلَل, which is the gap between two things; it is used figuratively for abstract things, so one says: "there is a flaw (khalal) in this matter".
Al-īḍāʿ is hastening. One says: أَوْضَعَ البعيرُ, i.e. it hastened in its pace. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
2490 - أرانا مُوضِعينَ لأَِمْرِ غيبٍ ... ونُسْحَرُ بالطعامِ والشراب
(I see us hastening toward a hidden matter, while we are beguiled by food and drink.)
Another said:
2491 - يا لَيْتَني فيها جَذَعْ ... أَخُبُّ فيها وأَضَعْ
(Would that I were a young man in it, trotting and hastening in it!)
The object of «أوضعوا» is omitted, i.e. they hastened their mounts, because the rider is faster than the walker. One says: وَضَعَتْ الناقةُ تَضَعُ when it hastens, and أوضعتها I [made it hasten]. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read {ما زادَكم إلا خَبالاً}, i.e. their going out would not have increased you [except in corruption]. Mujāhid and Muḥammad ibn Zayd read «ولأَوْفَضوا», which is also hastening, from His words, the Exalted: {إلى نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ} [al-Maʿārij: 43]. Ibn al-Zubayr read «وَلأَرْفَضُوا» with rāʾ, fāʾ and the dotted ḍād, from رَفَضَ, i.e. also hastened [Translator's note: so in the source; the verses cited below, and the closing remark, concern رَقَصَ (with qāf and ṣād) "to move quickly", and the reading is usually reported as «ولأرقصوا»]. Ḥassān said:
2492 - بزجاجةٍ رَقَصَتْ بما في جَوْفِها ... رَقْصِ القَلوصِ براكبٍ مستعجِلِ
(With a glass that danced with what was inside it, like the young she-camel's quick pace under a hurrying rider.)
And he said:
2493 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... والراقصاتِ إلى مِنَىً فالغَبْغَبِ
(… and by the [camels] hastening to Minā and then to al-Ghabghab.)
One says: رَفَضَ في مِشْيته رَفْضاً ورَفَضاناً.
His words: {يَبْغُونَكُمُ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «أَوْضَعوا», i.e. they would have hastened among you, seeking, i.e. seeking discord for you.
His words: {وَفِيكُمْ سَمَّاعُونَ لَهُمْ}: this clause may be a ḥāl of the object of «يَبْغُونكم» or of its fāʿil; that is permissible because the clause contains the pronouns of both. It may also be resumptive, the meaning being that among you are some who listen to them and give ear to their speech. Or what is meant may be: among you are spies of theirs who listen to news from you for them. On the first [meaning] the lām is for strengthening (taqwiya), because the governor is secondary [i.e. an intensive participle]; on the second it is causal, i.e. for their sake.
{ولا أَوْضَعُوا خلالكم} was written in the muṣḥaf with an alif after «لا». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The fatḥa used to be written as an alif before the Arabic script, and the Arabic script was invented shortly before the revelation of the Qur'an; a trace of that remained in people's habits, so they wrote the form of the hamza as an alif and its fatḥa as another alif. Similar is {أَوْ لا أَذْبَحَنَّهُ} [al-Naml: 21]" — he means with regard to the addition of an alif after «لا». It is not permissible to read according to this, and whoever reads it [so] deliberately commits unbelief.

semin-durr:48-48.t: Maslama ibn Muḥārib read «وقَلَبوا» without doubling. His words «وهم كارهون» are a ḥāl (circumstantial), the link being the wāw.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مَّن يَقُولُ ائذن}: like His words {يَاصَالِحُ ائتنا} [al-Aʿrāf: 77], in that the hamza may be pronounced fully or changed into wāw because of the ḍamma before it, even though it is separated [as part of] another word. This hamza is the first radical of the word, and before it there was a connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) that dropped out in continuous speech. Abū Jaʿfar said: "When the wāw or the fāʾ enters upon «ائذن», it is spelled alif, dhāl, nūn, without yāʾ; or [when] «ثم» [enters], it is spelled alif, yāʾ, dhāl, nūn. The difference is that one may pause on «ثم» and it is separable, unlike those two." I say: he means that when the wāw or fāʾ of coordination enters this word, their connection with it becomes strong, so the connective hamza dropped in continuous speech is not taken into account and no form is written for it; so it is written «فَأْذَنْ، وَأْذَنْ», this alif being the form of the hamza that is the first radical of the word. When «ثم» enters upon it, it is written thus: {ثُمَّ ائتوا}; they took account of the connective hamza and wrote a form for it. I say: it is as though this rule he mentioned with «ثم» is specific to this word; otherwise, for other words whose first radical is hamza, the form of the connective hamza is dropped in writing, so the imperative from al-ityān with «ثم» is written thus: «ثم أْتُوا»; and the analogy with «ثمَّ ائْذَنْ» would have been «ثم ائتوا». This is questionable.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Ismāʿīl al-Makkī, in what Ibn Mujāhid related from him, read «ولا تُفْتِنِّي» with ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from the four-letter أفتنه. Abū Ḥātim said: "It is the dialect of Tamīm." It was said: أفتنه means "he brought him into it [i.e. temptation]". The poet combined the two dialects, saying:
2494 - لئن فَتَنَتْني فهي بالأمس أفتنتْ ... سعيداً فأمسى قد قلا كلَّ مسلم
(If she has tempted me, well, yesterday she tempted Saʿīd, and he came to loathe every Muslim.)
What the permission relates to is staying behind, i.e. "permit me to stay behind and lag back from [facing] the enemy, and do not tempt me by my going out with you."

semin-durr:51-51.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لَّن يُصِيبَنَآ}: ʿAmr ibn Shaqīq said: "I heard Aʿyun, the judge of al-Rayy, read «لن يُصيبَنَّا» with a doubled nūn." Abū Ḥātim said: "That is not permissible, because the nūn does not come with «لن». Had it been [the reading] of Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif, it would have been permissible, because it is with «هل»; Allah the Exalted said: {هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُ مَا يَغِيظُ} [al-Ḥajj: 15]." I say: Abū Ḥātim means that the imperfect may be emphasised after an interrogative particle, and Ibn Muṣarrif reads «هل» instead of «لن»; it is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd.
An excuse was offered for this reading: it treated «لن» like the negative «لم» and «لا», after which the negated verb may be emphasised. As for «لا», the verification of the discussion on it preceded in al-Anfāl. As for «لم», that has been heard, and they recited:
2495 - يَحْسَبُه الجاهل ما لم يَعْلما ... شيخاً على كرسيِّه مُعَمَّمَا
(The ignorant, as long as he does not know, takes it for an old man on his chair wearing a turban.)
He meant «يَعْلَمَنْ», and changed the light [nūn] into alif after a fatḥa, like the tanwīn.
The judge and Ṭalḥa also read «هل يُصَيِّبُنا» with a doubled yāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its justification is that it is يُفَيْعِل, not يُفَعِّل, because it is from the wāw-roots, given their saying الصواب, صاب يصوب, and مصاوب as a plural of مصيبة; so the يُفَعِّل [form] from it would properly be يُصَوِّب — do you not see their saying صَوَّب رأيه? — unless it is from the dialect of those who say صاب السهمُ يَصيب, as in his words:
2496 - أَسْهُمِيَ الصائِبات والصُّيُبْ
(My arrows, those that hit and the hitting ones.)"
He means that its original form is صَوْيِب; the wāw and the yāʾ came together, the first of them being vowelless, so the wāw was changed into yāʾ and assimilated into it, just as preceded for you in تحيَّز, whose original form is تَحَيْوَز. But if we take it from the dialect of those who say صاب السهم يَصيب, it is from the yāʾ-roots, and its pattern in this dialect is فَعَّل.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِلاَّ إِحْدَى}: the object of the waiting, so it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). Ibn Muḥayṣin read «إلا احدى» with the alif of «احدى» connected, treating the disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) like the connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl). It is like the words of the poet:
2497 - إنْ لم أُقاتِلْ فالبسوني بُرْقُعا
(If I do not fight, then dress me in a veil.)
and the words of the other:
2498 - يابا المغيرة رُبَّ أَمْرٍ مُعْضِلٍ ... فَرَّجْتُه بالمكر مِنِّي والدَّهَا
(O Abū al-Mughīra, many a perplexing matter I have resolved by my cunning and shrewdness.)
His words {أَن يُصِيبَكُمُ} are the object of the waiting.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
The words of the Exalted: {طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً}: two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. willingly or unwillingly. The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «كُرْهاً» with ḍamma; the verification of that has preceded in al-Nisāʾ.
The Shaykh said here: "Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Waththāb read «كُرْهاً» with ḍamma on the kāf." This gives the impression that it was not read among the Seven. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a command in the sense of a statement, like His words {فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ الرحمن مَدّاً} [Maryam: 75]. Its meaning is: it will not be accepted from you, whether you spend willingly or unwillingly. Similar are His words, the Exalted: {استغفر لَهُمْ أَوْ لاَ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ} [al-Tawba: 80], and his words — he means Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
2499 - أسِيْئي بنا أو أَحْسِني لا مَلُومَةٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Treat us badly or treat us well, [you are] not blamed …)
i.e. Allah will not forgive them whether you ask forgiveness or not, and we do not blame you whether you treat us well or badly. In its meaning are the words of the speaker:
2500 - أخوك الذي إنْ قُمْتَ بالسيفِ عامداً ... لتضربَهُ لم يَسْتَغِشَّك في الودِّ
(Your [true] brother is the one who, if you rose with the sword intending to strike him, would not suspect your affection of deceit.)"
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is a command containing a recompense [i.e. a conditional sense]; this holds in every command accompanied by a recompense. The implied form is: if you spend, it will not be accepted from you. But when the command is devoid of an answer, implication of a condition does not accompany it." The Shaykh said: "What impairs this account is that if the command has the sense of a condition, the answer would be [treated like] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition; on this view the construction would have to be «لن يُتقبل» with the fāʾ, because «لن» does not occur as the apodosis of a condition except with the fāʾ, and likewise what implies its meaning. Do you not see its making the answer jussive in such as: اقصد زيداً يُحْسِنْ إليك?" I say: Abū Muḥammad [Ibn ʿAṭiyya] only meant to explain the meaning; otherwise, he is not ignorant of such obvious matters. Moreover, it does not follow, because what is implied need not be given the ruling of the overt thing in every respect.
His words: {إِنَّكُمْ} and what follows function as a statement of cause.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَن تُقْبَلَ}: there are two views on it. First: it is the second object of «منع», either by supposing the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "from being accepted", or because the verb reaches it by itself, since you say: منعتُ زيداً حَقَّه and مِنْ حقه. Second: it is a badal (substitute) of «هم» in مَنْعِهم; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, as though he meant a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). There is no need for it.
There are two views on the fāʿil (agent) of «منع». The first, which is the apparent one: it is {إِلاَّ أَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُواْ}, i.e. nothing prevented them from the acceptance of their spending but their unbelief. The second: it is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, i.e. Allah did not prevent them, «إلا أنهم» then being accusative by the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "because they disbelieved".
The two brothers read «أن يُقْبَلَ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, and the rest with the upper-dotted tāʾ; both are clear, because the femininity is figurative. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read like the two brothers, except that he made النفقة singular. Al-Aʿraj read «تُقْبل» with the upper-dotted tāʾ and «نفقتُهم» in the singular. Al-Sulamī read «يَقبل» in the active, [the fāʿil] being Allah the Exalted. It was also read «نَقْبل» with the nūn of majesty, and «نفقتهم» in the singular.
His words: {إِلاَّ وَهُمْ كسالى} and {إِلاَّ وَهُمْ كَارِهُونَ}: both clauses are a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil before them.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
The words of the Exalted: {الحياة الدنيا}: there are two views on it. First: it is attached to «تعجبك», His words {إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ الله لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ بِهَا} being a parenthetical clause, the implied form being: "so let them not please you in the life [of this world]". The preposition phrase may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أموالهم». Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Suddī and Ibn Qutayba inclined to this; they said: in the speech there is fronting and postponing, and the meaning is: "so let not their wealth nor their children please you in the life of this world; Allah only intends to punish them by them in the Hereafter." The Shaykh said: "However, as for restricting the forbidden admiration that arises from their wealth and children, it is known that it can only be in the life of this world, so that remains like an additional emphasis; unlike the punishment, which may be in this world as it may be in the Hereafter. Moreover, our colleagues restrict fronting and postponing to poetic necessity." I say: how can it be said, despite the explicit statement of those I mentioned, "our colleagues restrict that to poetic necessity"? Besides, it has nothing to do with the fronting and postponing that occurs in poetic necessity; it is only a parenthesis, and of a parenthesis one does not say "fronting and postponing" in the technical sense restricted to poetic necessity. Their naming it so — I mean Ibn ʿAbbās and those with him, may Allah be pleased with them — they only intend by it the parenthesis indicated, not what the people of the craft restrict to poetic necessity.
Second: «في الحياة» is attached to the punishment, what is meant by worldly punishment being the misfortunes and calamities of this world, or the burdensome obligations imposed on them, for which they hope for no reward — Ibn Zayd said this — or the zakāts imposed on them — al-Ḥasan said this. On this view the pronoun in «بها» refers back to the wealth only, while on the first it refers back to the children and the wealth.

semin-durr:57-57.t:
The words of the Exalted: {مَلْجَئاً أَوْ مَغَارَاتٍ}: al-maljaʾ is the fortress; it was said: the place of escape; and it was said: the place of safekeeping. It is a مَفْعَل from لجأ إليه يلجأ, i.e. he withdrew [to it]. One says: ألجأته إلى كذا, i.e. I compelled him to it, so he took refuge (iltajaʾa). Al-maljaʾ is suitable for the maṣdar, the time and the place; what is apparent here is the place. Al-maghārāt is the plural of مغارة, a مَفْعَلة from غار يغور (to sink in), so it is like al-ghār (cave) in meaning. It was said: al-maghāra is a burrow in the ground, like the tunnel of the jerboa; and al-ghār is a hollow in a mountain.
The majority read «مغارات» with fatḥa on the mīm. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf read «مُغارات» with ḍamma; it is from أغار. أغار may be intransitive — the Arabs say أغار meaning غار, i.e. he entered — or transitive: you say أَغَرْتُ زيداً, i.e. I made him enter the cave. On this view it is from the transitive أغار, with the object omitted, i.e. places in which they make themselves enter, i.e. hide themselves.
Al-muddakhal is a مُفْتَعَل from al-dukhūl (entering); it is a form of intensification in this meaning. The original is مُدْتَخل, then the dāl was assimilated into the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form, like ادَّان from al-dayn. Qatāda, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Aʿmash read «مُدَّخَّلاً» with doubling of both the dāl and the khāʾ. Its justification is that the original is مُتَدَخَّلاً, from the doubled تَدخَّل; when the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl, the word became مُدَّخَّلاً, like مُدَّيَّن from تَدَيَّن. Al-Ḥasan also, Maslama ibn Muḥārib, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Ibn Kathīr in one transmission read «مَدْخَلاً» with fatḥa on the mīm, sukūn on the dāl and a light fatḥa on the khāʾ, from دخل. Al-Ḥasan in the transmission of Maḥbūb read likewise, except that he gave the mīm ḍamma, making it from أدخل.
This is among the most brilliant of knowledge: He first mentioned the most general thing, namely a refuge of whatever kind; then He mentioned the caves in which one hides in the highest places and in the mountains; then the places in which one hides in the low places, namely the burrows, which He expressed by al-muddakhal.
Al-Zajjāj said: "It is valid for al-maghārāt to be from their saying حَبْل مُغار, i.e. firmly twisted; then that is used figuratively for a firm, settled matter. On this view the interpretation is: if they found help, or well-directed, interconnected matters that would protect them from you." He also made al-muddakhal [mean] a people whose company they would enter.
Ubayy read «مُنْدَخَلاً» with nūn after the mīm, from اندخل. He said:
2501 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا يدي في حَمِيتِ السَّمْنِ تَنْدَخِلُ
(… nor does my hand go into the skin of clarified butter.)
Abū Ḥātim denied this reading from him and said: "It is only with tāʾ." I say: he is excused, because انفعل is intransitive and does not take an object, so how could a passive participle be formed from it?
Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī read «لَوَالَوا», i.e. they gave allegiance and hastened; likewise Ibn Abī ʿUbayda ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Nawfal related it from his father from his grandfather, who was a Companion — from al-muwālāt (alliance). This is among the cases in which فَعَّل and فاعَل have one meaning, as in ضَعَّفْتُه and ضاعَفْتُه. Saʿīd ibn Muslim said: "I think it is «لَوَأَلُوا», with a hamza bearing fatḥa after the wāw, from وَأَلَ, i.e. he took refuge." Al-Zamakhsharī transmitted this reading and explained it as taking refuge, as preceded.
Al-jumūḥ is bolting away swiftly; from it is فرس جَموح, when the bridle does not hold it back. He said:
2502 - جَمُوحاً مَرُوحاً وإحضارُها ... كمَعْمَعَةِ السَّعَفِ المُؤْقَدِ
(Bolting, lively, and her gallop is like the crackling of burning palm-fronds.)
Another said:
2503 - إذا جَمَحَتْ نساؤكُمُ إليه ... أَشَظَّ كأنه مَسَدٌ مُغَارُ
(When your women rush to him, he stiffens as though he were a firmly twisted rope.)
Another said:
2504 - وقد جَمَحْتُ جِماحاً في دمائِهمُ ... حتى رأيتُ ذوي أحسابِهم جَهَزوا
(I rushed headlong into their blood until I saw their men of noble lineage finished off.)
Anas ibn Mālik and al-Aʿmash read «يَجْمِزُون». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "[It means] they trot in their walking." It was said: يَجْمِزُون, يَجْمَحون and يشتدُّون have one meaning. In the ḥadīth: "When the stones struck him painfully, he ran off (jamaza)." Ruʾba said:
2505 - إمَّا تَرَيْني اليومَ أمَّ حَمْزِ ... قارَبْتُ بين عَنَقي وجَمْزي
(If you see me today, O Umm Ḥamz, [you see that] I have brought my stride and my trot close together.)
This is its origin in the language.
His words: {إِلَيْهِ}: the pronoun refers back to the refuge or to the muddakhal, because the coordination is with «أو»; it may also refer back to «المَغَارات» by interpreting it as a masculine.
His words: {مَّن يَلْمِزُكَ}: the generality read «يلمِزك» with kasra on the mīm, from لَمَزه يَلْمِزه, i.e. he found fault with him; its origin is signalling with the eye and the like. Al-Azharī said: "Its origin is pushing: لَمَزْته means I pushed him." Al-Layth said: "It is winking in the face; from it is هُمَزَةٌ لُمَزَة, i.e. one who does these two acts much."
Yaʿqūb, Ḥammād ibn Salama from Ibn Kathīr, al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ read it with ḍamma on it [the mīm], and it was also related from Abū ʿAmr; they are two dialects in the imperfect. Al-Aʿmash read «يُلْمِزُك», from the four-letter ألمز. Ḥammād ibn Salama related «يُلامِزُك», on the form of mufāʿala from one party, like سافرَ and عاقَب.
The discussion of «إذا» of surprise has preceded many times. As for what governs it: Abū al-Baqāʾ said «يَسْخَطون», because he said that it is an adverb of place; this is questionable, as preceded in its parallel.

semin-durr:59-59.t: The words of the Exalted: {وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ رَضُوْاْ}: what is apparent is that the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, its implied form being: "it would have been better for them". It was said: its apodosis is «وقالوا», the wāw being redundant (zāʾida); this is the doctrine of the Kufans. His words «سيُؤْتينا» and «إنَّا إلى الله راغبون»: these two clauses are like an explanation of their saying "Allah is sufficient for us"; that is why they were not [Translator's note: the source has «يم», a misprint for «لم»] conjoined, because they are like one thing; the strength of the connection prevented coordination.

semin-durr:60-60.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَرِيضَةً}: there are two views on its accusative. First: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the sense, because the meaning of «إنما الصدقات للفقراء» amounts to: Allah has prescribed that. Second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الفقراء»; al-Kirmānī and Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, meaning: of the pronoun latent in the preposition phrase because it occurs as a khabar (predicate), i.e. the alms are for them, being an obligation, i.e. obligatory. In that case «فريضة» may be in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūla), the tāʾ having entered only because it is treated like nouns, like النَّطيحة; or it may be a maṣdar occurring in the place of a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why did He turn from the lām to «في» in the last four? I say: to indicate that they are more firmly established in deserving to receive alms than those mentioned before, because «في» is for containment; so He drew attention to the fact that they are worthy of having alms placed in them and of being made a likely place and a receptacle for it." Then he said: "The repetition of «في» in His words {وَفِي سَبِيلِ الله وابن السبيل} gives these two an extra preference over the slaves and the debtors."
It was transmitted from Sībawayh that «فريضة» is accusative by its implied verb, i.e. Allah prescribed that as an obligation. It was transmitted from al-Farrāʾ that it is accusative by way of "cutting off" (al-qaṭʿ).
It was also read «فريضةٌ» in the nominative, on [the implied form]: "that is an obligation".
The origin of al-ghurm is the binding of something burdensome; from it, passionate love was called gharām, and it is used to express destruction in His words, the Exalted: {إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً} [al-Furqān: 65]. Paying a fine (gharāma) of wealth involves great hardship.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ لَّكُمْ}: «أُذُن» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "say: he is an ear of good". The majority read «خيرٍ» in the genitive by annexation. Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «أُذنٌ» with tanwīn and «خيرٌ» in the nominative. There are two views on it. First: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «أُذُن». Second: it is a khabar after a khabar. «خير» may be an adjective without [the sense of] preference, i.e. "an ear possessing good for you", or it may express preference in its basic sense, i.e. "more good for you". The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» allowed «أذن» to be a mubtadaʾ and «خير» its khabar; beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible here because it is qualified by implication, i.e. "an ear that does not take you to task is better for you than an ear that takes you to task".
One says: رَجُلٌ أُذُنٌ, i.e. [a man who] listens to everything that is said. There are two interpretations of it. First: he was named by the organ because it is the instrument of hearing, which is the principal thing intended of him, like their calling the scout "an eye". It was said: what is meant by the ear here is the organ, in which case it involves the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "possessor of an ear". Second: أُذُن is an adjective on the pattern فُعُل, like أُنُف and شُلُل; one says أَذِن يَأْذَن, so he is أُذُن. He said:
2506 - وقد صِرْتَ أُذْناً للوُشاة سَميعةً ... ينالُون مِنْ عِرْضي ولو شئتَ ما نالوا
(You have become an ear for the slanderers, listening keenly; they attack my honour, and had you wished, they would not have.)
His words: {وَرَحْمَةٌ}: the majority read «ورحمة» in the nominative, coordinated with «أذن ورحمة» among those who read «رحمة» in the nominative [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is that it is coordinated with «أذن»]. Some said: it is conjoined to «يؤمن», because «يؤمن» is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of «أذن», the implied form being: "an ear that believes, and a mercy". Ḥamza and al-Aʿmash read «ورحمةٍ» in the genitive, coordinated with «خير», which is in the genitive through the annexation of «أذن» to it; on this reading the clause is parenthetical between the two conjoined words, the implied form being: "an ear of good and of mercy". Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ورحمةً» in the accusative, as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), what it explains being omitted, i.e. "he listens to you out of mercy towards you"; it was omitted because His words {قُلْ أُذُنُ خَيْرٍ} indicate it.
The bāʾ and the lām in «يؤمن بالله» and «ويؤمن للمؤمنين» are both transitivising; the discussion of them has preceded at the beginning of this topic. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He intended belief in Allah, which is the opposite of unbelief, so He made it transitive with the bāʾ; and He intended listening to the believers and accepting what they say, so He made it transitive with the lām. Do you not see His words {وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا وَلَوْ كُنَّا صَادِقِينَ} [Yūsuf: 17]? How far it is from the bāʾ! Similar are {فَمَآ آمَنَ لموسى} [Yūnus: 83], {أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ واتبعك الأرذلون} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 111] and {آمَنتُمْ لَهُ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 49]." Ibn Qutayba said: "Both are redundant (zāʾida), and the meaning is: he believes Allah and believes the believers." This is a rejected view; what shows that they are not redundant is the difference between the redundant particles: had an independent meaning not been intended, He would not have differentiated between the two particles. Al-Mubarrad said: "It is attached to a maṣdar implied from the verb, as though He said: and his faith for the believers." It was said: one says آمنتُ لك meaning "I believed you", and from it is {وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُؤْمِنٍ لَّنَا}. In my view this lām implies «ما», so the meaning is: and he believes the believers in what they tell him. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The lām in «للمؤمنين» is redundant; it entered to distinguish between «يؤمن» meaning 'believes [someone]' and يؤمن meaning 'establishes faith'."

semin-durr:62-62.t:
The words of the Exalted: {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ}: He made the pronoun in «يُرْضوه» singular, even though the rule in coordination with the wāw is agreement, for several reasons. First: the pleasure of Allah and of His Messenger is one thing — whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed [Allah], {إِنَّ الذين يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ الله} [al-Fatḥ: 10] — so He made the two pronouns one pronoun to draw attention to that. Second: the pronoun refers back to the two in the singular form by interpreting [it as] "what has been mentioned", like the words of Ruʾba:
2507 - فيها خطوطٌ مِنْ سوادٍ وبَلَقْ ... كأنه في الجلد تَوْلِيْعُ البَهَقْ
(In it are streaks of black and piebald white, as though it were, on the skin, the blotching of leucoderma.)
i.e. as though that which has been mentioned. The explanation of this has preceded for you at the beginning of al-Baqara. Third: al-Mubarrad said: "In the speech there is fronting and postponing, its implied form being: and Allah is more deserving that they please Him, and His Messenger." I say: this is according to the opinion of those who claim the omission from the second. Fourth, which is the doctrine of Sībawayh: He omitted the khabar (predicate) of the first and retained the khabar of the second. This is better than its reverse, which is the view of al-Mubarrad, because it avoids separating the mubtadaʾ (subject) from its khabar [Translator's note: the source has «المبتدأ أو خبره», a misprint for «المبتدأ وخبره»], and also because it involves predicating a thing of what is nearest to it; moreover, it is the only possible [analysis] in the words of the poet:
2508 - نحن بما عندنا وأنت بما ... عندكَ راضٍ والرأيُ مختلفُ
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, and opinion differs.)
i.e. "we are content (rāḍūn)"; «راضون» was omitted because the khabar of the second indicates it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The doctrine of Sībawayh is that they are two clauses, the first having been omitted because the second indicates it." The Shaykh said: "If the pronoun in «أنهما» refers back to each of the two clauses, how can he say 'the first was omitted', when the first was not omitted, only its khabar? And if it refers back to the khabar, namely {أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ}, it is a clause only if one holds that «أن يُرْضُوه» is a mubtadaʾ with «أحقُّ» as its khabar placed before it; and this view is not necessary, since the khabar may be a single word, the implied form being: أحقُّ بأَنْ تُرْضوه." I say: Abū Muḥammad [Ibn ʿAṭiyya] only intended the first analysis, which is the well-known one among the grammatical analysts: they make «أحق» a fronted khabar and «أن يرضوه» a postponed mubtadaʾ, [i.e.] "and Allah and His Messenger — pleasing Him is more deserving". The detailed treatment of this preceded recently at His words {فالله أَحَقُّ أَن تَخْشَوْهُ} [al-Tawba: 13].
{إِن كَانُواْ مُؤْمِنِينَ} is a condition whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted or placed before it.

semin-durr:63-63.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَلَمْ يعلموا}: the majority read «يَعْلموا» with the yāʾ of the absent [third person], referring back to the hypocrites. Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj read «تَعْلموا» with the tāʾ of address. It was said: it is an iltifāt (shift of person) from absence to address, if the hypocrites are meant. It was said: the address is to the Prophet, upon him be peace, and the plural form was used to honour him, as in his words:
2509 - وإن شِئْتِ حرَّمْتُ النساءَ سواكم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And if you wish, I will forbid myself all women other than you [pl.] …)
And it was said: the address is to the believers. With these three suppositions the meaning of the interrogative differs: on the first, the interrogative is for rebuke and reproach; on the second, it expresses wonder at their state; on the third, it is for affirmation (taqrīr).
Knowing (al-ʿilm) here may be in its basic sense, so that «أَنْ» fills the place of two objects according to Sībawayh, and the place of one of them, the other being omitted, according to al-Akhfash; or it may be in the sense of recognising, so that «أنَّ» fills the place of one object. «مَنْ» is conditional, and {فَأَنَّ لَهُ نَارَ} is its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «أنَّ» was given fatḥa after the fāʾ for what is known from al-Anʿām. The conditional clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the first «أنَّ».
This is a clear account, yet a group turned away from this clear one to other views. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«فأنَّ له» may be conjoined to «أنه», on the view that the apodosis of «مَنْ» is omitted, its implied form being: Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger will perish, and that for him…" Al-Jarmī and al-Mubarrad said: the second «أنَّ» is repeated for emphasis, as though the implied form were: "then for him is the Fire of Hell", and «أنَّ» was repeated for emphasis. Abū al-Baqāʾ likened it to His words, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ عَمِلُواْ السواء} [al-Naḥl: 119], then He said: {إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِن بَعْدِهَا}. He said: "On this view the fāʾ is [the fāʾ of] the apodosis of the condition."
The Shaykh rebutted al-Zamakhsharī's view on the grounds that they stated explicitly that when the apodosis of a condition is omitted, the verb of the condition must be past, or imperfect joined with «لم»; while on his view the apodosis is omitted and the verb of the condition is an imperfect not joined with «لم». "Moreover, we find the speech complete without what he supposed."
It was transmitted from Sībawayh that he said: "The second is a badal (substitute) of the first." This is not authentic from Sībawayh, for it is weak or impossible. Abū al-Baqāʾ judged it weak for two reasons. "First: the fāʾ prevents that, and declaring it redundant is weak. Second: making it a badal entails the loss of the apodosis of «مَنْ» from the speech." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is objected to on the grounds that nothing is substituted for a thing until it is complete, and the first [أنّ] here has not yet received its khabar, since the apodosis of the condition has not yet come, and that clause is the khabar. Moreover, the fāʾ resists the badal; [moreover,] it has another meaning than the badal, so the badal is awkward."
Some said: "It must be on the supposition of the lām, i.e. 'then because for him is the Fire of Hell'; on this view something must be implied to complete the apodosis of the condition, its implied form being: then his opposition is because for him is the Fire of Hell."
All these are needless contrivances. The best is what preceded, what he [Translator's note: so in the source, «فالأولى ما تقدم ما ذكره»; the antecedent of "he" is unclear] mentioned: namely, that {فَأَنَّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ} is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar is omitted; and you ought to suppose it placed before it, as al-Zamakhsharī and others did, i.e. "then it is true that for him is the Fire of Hell". Someone else supposed it placed after it, i.e. "then that for him is the Fire of Hell is necessary"; so al-Akhfash supposed it. They rebutted him on the grounds that one does not begin with it; but this is not binding on him, for he permits beginning with «أنَّ» with fatḥa without fronting a khabar, while others do not permit beginning with it except on condition that «أمَّا» precedes, as in «أمَّا أنك ذاهبٌ فعندي», or on condition that the khabar precedes, as in «عندي أنَّك مُنْطَلق». It was also said: «فأنَّ له» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then what is necessary is that for him…". This clause after the fāʾ, together with the fāʾ, is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition.
Abū ʿAmr, in what Abū ʿUbayda related, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī ʿAbla [Translator's note: the source has «وابن لأبي عبلة», a misprint] read «فإنَّ» with kasra; it is a good, strong reading. It has preceded that some of the Seven read [with it] in al-Anʿām, and its justification preceded there.
Al-muḥādda is opposition, obstinacy, transgressing the limit and enmity. It was said: it is derived from al-ḥadd, the edge of the iron weapon with which one fights. It was said: from al-ḥadd meaning side, as though he is on a side other than his companion's side, like their saying شاقَّه, i.e. he was on a side (shiqq) other than his companion's side, and عاداه, i.e. he was on a bank (ʿudwa) other than his bank.
Some preferred the reading with kasra because it does not require supposing anything implied; and his words:
2510 - فَمَنْ يكُ سائلاً عني فإني ... وجِرْوَةَ لا تُعارُ ولا تُباعُ
(Whoever asks about me: I and Jirwa [my mare] — she is neither lent nor sold.)
were only transmitted with kasra. This is not binding, for it came according to one of the two permissible [forms]. «خالداً» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

semin-durr:64-64.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَن تُنَزَّلَ}: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed in the accusative by «يحذر», for «يَحْذَر» is transitive by itself, because of His words, the Exalted: {وَيُحَذِّرْكُمُ الله نَفْسَهُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 30]; were it not transitive to one object originally, the doubling would not have given it a second object. What Sībawayh recited also indicates it:
2511 - حَذِرٌ أُموراً لا تَضيرُ وآمِنٌ ... ما ليسَ مُنْجيَه من الأَقْدارِ
(Wary of things that do no harm, and feeling safe from what will not save him from the decrees of fate.)
There is discussion about the verse: it was said to be fabricated, which is false; I set out its story carefully in «Sharḥ al-Tashīl». Al-Mubarrad said: "حَذِر is not transitive," saying: "because it is one of the states of the soul, like فَزِع." This does not follow, for among the states of the soul we have what is transitive, such as خاف and خشِي. So «تُنَزَّل», according to al-Mubarrad, is by the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "of [the] sending down". His words «تُنَبِّئهم» are in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «سورة».

semin-durr:65-65.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أبالله}: attached to His words «تستهزئون», and «تستهزئون» is the khabar (predicate) of kāna. It is evidence for the fronting of the khabar of kāna before it, because fronting what is governed indicates [the possibility of] fronting the governor; what is governed by the khabar has been placed before «كان», so fronting it [the khabar] should be permissible a fortiori. There is a point of discussion here: Ibn Mālik impugned this evidence with His words, the Exalted: {فَأَمَّا اليتيم فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ وَأَمَّا السآئل فَلاَ تَنْهَرْ} [al-Ḍuḥā: 9-10]. He said: "اليتيم and السائل have been placed before the prohibitive «لا», and what governs them is what comes after it; yet what follows the prohibitive «لا» may not be placed before it, since it is made jussive by it. So what is governed has been fronted where the governor may not be fronted." He mentioned that in connection with their adducing, for the permissibility of fronting the khabar of laysa, His words: {أَلاَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفاً عَنْهُمْ} [Hūd: 8].
Al-iʿtidhār is disavowing a sin. Its origin is from تعذَّرت المنازل, i.e. the dwellings became effaced and their traces were wiped out. Ibn Aḥmar said:
2512 - قد كنتَ تعرف آياتٍ فقد جعلَتْ ... أطلالُ إلفِك بالوَعْساء تعتذِرُ
(You used to know [its] signs, but the ruins of your beloved's abode in the sandy ground have begun to be effaced.)
So the one who apologises tries to wipe out his sin. It was said: its origin is from al-ʿadhr, which is cutting; from it is al-ʿudhra (virginity), because it is severed by defloration. Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: "They say: اعتذرت [المياه, i.e. the waters were cut off; and it is as though the one who apologises tries] to cut off blame from himself."

semin-durr:66-66.t:
The words of the Exalted: {إِن نَّعْفُ}: ʿĀṣim read «نَعْفُ» with the nūn of majesty, and «نُعَذِّب» likewise, with «طائفةً» in the accusative as an object; it is the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Zayd ibn ʿAlī. The rest read «يُعفَ» in both places [Translator's note: so in the source; the second verb is «تُعَذَّبْ»] with the lower-dotted yāʾ, in the passive, with «طائفةٌ» in the nominative as standing in place of the fāʿil (agent). What stands in place of the fāʿil in the first verb is the preposition phrase after it. Al-Jaḥdarī read «إن يَعْفُ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ in both, in the active, [the fāʿil] being the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, with «طائفة» in the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Mujāhid read «تَعْفُ» with the upper-dotted tāʾ in both, in the active, [the fāʿil] being the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, with «طائفةً» in the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. Mujāhid [also] read «تُعفَ» with the upper-dotted tāʾ in both, in the passive, with «طائفة» in the nominative because it stands in place of the fāʿil. [Translator's note: so in the source; Mujāhid is credited with two different readings.]
There are two views on what stands in place of the fāʿil in the first verb. First: it is the pronoun of the sins, i.e. "if these sins are pardoned". Second: it is the preposition phrase, the verb having been made feminine only according to the sense. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The proper way is the masculine, because what it is predicated of is the adverbial, as you say «سِيْرَ بالدابة» and do not say «سِيْرت بالدابة»; but he went by the meaning, as though it were said: 'if a party is shown mercy', so he made it feminine for that reason. It is unusual."

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying, the Exalted: {يَأْمُرُونَ}: This clause has no grammatical position, because it is explicative of His saying {بَعْضُهُمْ مِّن بَعْضٍ}; and likewise what is conjoined to «يَأْمرون».

semin-durr:68-68.t: His saying, the Exalted: {خَالِدِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the first object of the promise, and it is a anticipated (muqaddara) ḥāl, because this state did not coincide with the promise. As for His saying «هي حَسْبُهم», this clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. And His saying «هي حسبهم»: this resumptive clause has no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source repeats this last remark.]

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قَوْمِ نُوحٍ}: a badal (substitute) for the relative noun before it. It may be a badal of the whole for the whole, if what is meant by «الذين» is only what is mentioned after it; and it may be a partial badal of the whole, if what is meant by it is more general than that.
And «المُؤْتَفكات» means "those overturned". One says: أَفَكْتُه فانتفك, that is, "I overturned it and it was overturned". The root indicates turning and changing about, and from it comes {يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 9], that is, "is turned away". The pronoun in «أَتَتْهم» may refer back to those mentioned earlier, and some restricted it to «المؤتفكات».

semin-durr:71-71.t: His saying, the Exalted: { [بَعْضُهُمْ] أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ}: whereas He said of the hypocrites {مِّن بَعْضٍ} [al-Tawba: 67], since there is no wilāya (mutual allegiance) among the hypocrites. As for His saying «يَأْمُرون», it is as in its counterpart above. The sīn in «سيرحمهم الله» is for the future, since what is meant is a particular mercy, namely what He has kept in store for them in the Hereafter. al-Zamakhsharī claimed that it indicates the certainty of the mercy and the reinforcement of the threat and the warning, as in: سأنتقم منك ("I shall take vengeance on you").

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {خَالِدِينَ}: an anticipated ḥāl, as stated above. And «العَدْن» means residing. One says: عَدَنَ بالمكان يَعْدِن عَدْناً, that is, "he settled and became established"; from it comes «المَعْدِن» (the mine), for the place where jewels are fixed. One also says عَدَن عُدُوناً, so it has two verbal nouns. This is the original sense of this word in the language; in exegesis they have mentioned many meanings for it. al-Aʿshā said, in the sense of residing:
2516 - وإن يَسْتضيفوا إلى حِلْمِهِ ... يُضافُوا إلى راجِحٍ قد عَدَنْ
(If they seek hospitality with his forbearance, they will be hosted by one steadfast, who has settled.)
that is, "he has become fixed and settled"; and from it «عَدَن» is the name of a city in Yemen, because of the many who reside in it.
His saying: {وَرِضْوَانٌ مِّنَ الله أَكْبَرُ}: the indefiniteness (of «رضوان») conveys a causal sense, that is: the least bit of good pleasure is greater than all that preceded of the gardens and their dwellings. [Translator's note: the source says «التكثير» ("making plentiful"); this is likely a slip for «التنكير» (indefiniteness), which is how it is rendered here.]

semin-durr:73-73.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ}: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If it is asked: how is the wāw good here, when the fāʾ would be more fitting in this place? There are three answers. The first: the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial), and the estimate is: 'Do that while they deserve Hell', and that state is the state of their disbelief and hypocrisy. The second: the wāw is brought as a signal that an omitted verb is intended, its implied form being: 'and know that their abode is Hell'. The third: the speech has been carried according to the meaning, the meaning being that there has been gathered for them the punishment of this world, through jihad and harshness, and the punishment of the Hereafter, by making Hell their abode." But none of all this is needed; rather, this is a resumptive clause.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ أَنْ أَغْنَاهُمُ}: There are two possibilities in it. The first: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), that is: "they disliked and found fault with nothing except Allah's enriching them". It is of the type of their saying: ما لي عندك ذنبٌ إلا أَنْ أَحْسَنْت إليك ("I have no offence with you except that I did you good"), that is: "if there is any offence, it is this"; so it is mockery of them, as in the saying:
2517 - ولا عيبَ فينا غيرُ عِرْقٍ لمعشرٍ ... كرامٍ وأنَّا لا نَخُطُّ على النمل
(There is no fault in us except a lineage of noble folk, and that we do not write upon ants.)
and the saying of another:
2518 - ما نقِموا من بني أميةَ إلا ... أنهمْ يَحْلُمون إنْ غَضِبوا
وأنهم سادةُ الملوكِ ولا ... يَصْلحُ إلا عليهم العَرَبُ
(They resented nothing in the Banū Umayya except that they are forbearing when angered, and that they are the masters of kings, and the Arabs are fit to be ruled only by them.)
The second: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and on this the direct object is omitted, its implied form being: "and they did not resent faith in them except because of Allah's enriching them". The discussion of نَقِم has already preceded.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّنْ عَاهَدَ الله}: it contains the sense of an oath, therefore it was answered with His saying «لنصَّدَّقَنَّ»; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted because this answer indicates it, and you already know the rule on that. The lām is the preparatory lām (lām al-tawṭiʾa). Combining the oath with the preparatory lām is not precluded. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "There are two possibilities in it. One: its implied form is 'so he said: if He gives us...'. The second: that «عاهد» is in the sense of «قال» ('he said'), for a covenant is a statement." But there is no need for what he mentioned.
His saying: {لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ وَلَنَكُونَنَّ}: the majority read both with the heavy nūn, and al-Aʿmash with the light one.

semin-durr:77-77.t: The majority read «يَكذبون» with the light form (without shadda), and Abū Rajāʾ with the heavy form (with shadda).

semin-durr:78-78.t: The majority read «يَعْلموا» with the yāʾ (third person). ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Ḥasan and al-Sulamī read it with the address (tāʾ, second person), as an iltifāt (shift of address) directed to the believers rather than the hypocrites.

semin-durr:80-80.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), like your saying: «ضربتُه عشرين ضربةً» ("I struck him twenty strikes"); it is for the number of his times. As for His saying {استغفر لَهُمْ أَوْ لاَ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ}, the discussion of this has already preceded shortly after His saying {قُلْ أَنفِقُواْ طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً لَّن يُتَقَبَّلَ مِنكُمْ} [al-Tawba: 53], and that it is the counterpart of the saying:
2519 - أَسِيْئي بنا أو أَحْسِني لا مَلومةٌ ... لدينا ولا مَقْلِيَّةٌ إنْ تَقَلَّتِ
(Treat us ill or treat us well: you are not blamed with us, nor hated, if you hate.)

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كالذين مِن قَبْلِكُمْ}: There are several possibilities in it. The first: this kāf is in the position of the nominative, its implied form being "they are like those who…", so it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). The second: that it is in the position of the accusative. al-Zajjāj said: "The meaning is: He promised you a promise like that of those before you; so it is attached to «وَعَدَ»." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is shaky." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It may be attached to «يَسْتهزئون»", and in this there is great remoteness.
His saying: {كَانُواْ أَشَدَّ} is an explanation of their likeness to them and an illustration of their action. al-Farrāʾ made its position accusative by an implied verb, saying: "The comparison is from the side of the action, that is: you did as those before you did", so the kāf is in the position of the accusative. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and in the speech a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) is omitted, its implied form being 'a promise like the promise of those who…'." al-Zamakhsharī mentioned the nominative possibility given above and the possibility I put first from al-Farrāʾ, and likened it to the saying of al-Namir ibn Tawlab:
2513 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كاليوم مَطْلوباً ولا طَلَبا
(…like today, [I have never seen] one sought, nor one seeking.)
with the implied "I have not seen".
His saying: {كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ الَّذِينَ}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "an enjoyment like the enjoyment of those who…".
His saying: {كالذي خاضوا}: the kāf is like the one before it. There are several possibilities regarding «الذي». The first: that the meaning is "and you plunged a plunging like the plunging of those who plunged", the nūn being dropped for lightness, or the singular put in the place of the plural. The verification of this was given at the beginning of al-Baqara. So the described maṣdar and the muḍāf to the relative noun are omitted, and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) of the relative is implied as "خاضوه", the original being "خاضوا فيه", because it is made transitive by «في»; then latitude was allowed in it, the preposition was dropped, the pronoun became attached to the verb, and so its omission became permissible. Without this gradation the omission would not be permissible, for you know from what has passed that whenever the ʿāʾid is governed by a preposition, the condition for permitting its omission is that the relative noun be governed by the like of that preposition, and that the thing to which it is attached be the same, along with other conditions I mentioned earlier.
The second: that «الذي» is an adjective of a singular that conveys a plural, that is: "and you plunged a plunging like the plunging of the company who plunged", or "the group who plunged". The discussion of the ʿāʾid is as before.
The third: that «الذي» is a description of the maṣdar, and the estimate is: "and you plunged a plunging like the plunging that they plunged". On this the ʿāʾid is accusative without the mediation of a preposition. This possibility ought to be the preferred one, since there is no objection in it.
