The fourth: that «الذي» occurs as a maṣdar-forming particle, and the estimate is "and you plunged a plunging like their plunging"; and likewise:
2514 - فَثَبَّتَ اللَّهُ ما آتاك مِنْ حسنٍ ... في المُرْسلين ونَصْراً كالذي نُصِروا
(May Allah make firm what He gave you of goodness among the messengers, and a victory like the one they were given.)
that is, "like their victory". And the saying of another:
2515 - يا أمَّ عمروٍ جزاكِ اللَّهُ مغفرةً ... رُدِّي عليَّ فؤادي كالذي كانا
(O Umm ʿAmr, may Allah reward you with forgiveness: return my heart to me as it was.)
that is, "like its being". It has already been mentioned that this is the school of al-Farrāʾ and Yūnus, and the Basrans' interpretation of this has also preceded. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the benefit of His saying {فاستمتعوا بِخَلاقِهِمْ كَمَا} when His saying {كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ} suffices without it, as «كالذي خاضوا» dispenses with saying 'and they plunged, so you plunged like those who plunged'? I say: its benefit is to censure the first group for enjoying what they were given and for their contentment with it instead of looking to the outcome and seeking success in the Hereafter, and to make the matter of enjoyment seem base and the one content with it abhorrent, and then to liken the state of those addressed to theirs. As for «وخُضْتُمْ كالذي خاضوا», it is conjoined to what precedes it, and is predicated of that, being independent through its predication to it of that introduction." He means that it dispenses with the construction being: "and they plunged, so you plunged like those who plunged".
In His saying {كَمَا اسْتَمْتَعَ الَّذِينَ} there is the placing of the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, for a subtle point: the original was «فاستمتعتم فخَلاقكم كما استمتعوا بخلاقِهم», but He brought them out in the form of the overt noun to disparage them, like His saying {لاَ تَعْبُدِ الشيطان إِنَّ الشيطان كَانَ للرحمن عَصِيّاً} [Maryam: 44], and like His saying before this {المنافقون والمنافقات بَعْضُهُمْ مِّن بَعْضٍ} and then {إِنَّ المنافقين هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ} [al-Tawba: 67]. Just as placing the overt noun in the place of the pronoun indicates magnification and exaltation, by it one also indicates the opposite, which is disparagement.

semin-durr:79-79.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يَلْمِزُونَ}: There are several possibilities in it. The first: that it is nominative through an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are those who…". The second: that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «من المؤمنين» a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المطَّوِّعين», and «في الصدقات» attached to «يَلْمِزون». And {وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَجِدُونَ} is conjoined to «المطَّوِّعين», that is: they find fault with the wealthy and the poor.
Makkī said: "«والذين» is genitive, conjoined to «المؤمنين»; and its being conjoined to «المطَّوِّعين» is not good, because the noun is not yet complete, since «فيسخرون» is conjoined to «يَلْمِزُون»." So al-Naḥḥās mentioned it in his «Iʿrāb», and in my view it is a slip on his part. I say: the matter is as he stated, for «المطَّوِّعين» is complete without needing anything else.
His saying {فَيَسْخَرُونَ} is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), and the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is the clause of His saying {سَخِرَ الله مِنْهُمْ}. This is the clearest iʿrāb said here. It was also said: {وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَجِدُونَ} is conjoined to «الذين يَلْمزون»; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it. This is not permissible, because it would necessitate predicating of them His saying {سَخِرَ الله مِنْهُمْ}, and this could only be if those who do not find were hypocrites; but if they were believers, how could Allah mock them? It was also said: {وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَجِدُونَ} is conjoined to the believers; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. The Shaykh said: "It is very remote." I say: the reason for its remoteness is that it suggests that those who do not find are not believers, because the basis of conjunction is to indicate difference; so it is as if it were said: "they find fault with the volunteers from these two classes: the believers and those who do not find", which would make those who do not find volunteers who are not believers.
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «في الصدقات» is attached to «يَلْمِزون» and not to «المطَّوِّعين», lest a stranger intervene between them. This refutation is open to question, since His saying «من المؤمنين» is a ḥāl, and a ḥāl is not a stranger. What does show the refutation is that «يطَّوَّع» is made transitive only by «بـ», not by «في», and «في» being in the sense of «بـ» is contrary to the basic rule.
It was also said: {فَيَسْخَرُونَ} is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the fāʾ enters because of the sense of condition the mubtadaʾ contains. In this possibility there is remoteness, in that it comes close to the khabar being identical in meaning with the mubtadaʾ, for whoever finds fault with someone and winks at him knows that he is mocking him; so it would be like their saying: «سيد الجارية مالكها» ("the master of the girl is her owner").
The third: that its position is accusative by ishtighāl (an occupying verb), with an implied verb which {سَخِرَ الله مِنْهُمْ} explains by way of meaning, like: "He censured those who find fault; Allah mocked them." The fourth: that it is accusative as an expression of vilification (shatm). The fifth: that it is genitive as a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in «سِرَّهم ونجواهم».
It was also read «يُلْمزون» with a ḍamma on the mīm, and it has already been mentioned that it is a dialect form.
His saying {سَخِرَ الله} may be a plain statement, and it may be a supplication. The majority read «جُهدهم» with a ḍamma on the jīm. Ibn Hurmuz and a group read «جَهْدهم» with a fatḥa. It was said they are two dialect forms with one meaning. It was also said: the fatḥa form is hardship and the ḍamma form is capacity, as al-Qutabī said. It was also said: the ḍamma form is a small thing one lives on, and the fatḥa form is work.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ}: attached to «فرح». It is suitable for the maṣdar of «قعد», for its time and for its place; what is meant here is the maṣdar, that is: by their sitting and their staying in Medina.
His saying: {خِلاَفَ}: There are three possibilities in it. The first: that it is accusative as a maṣdar with an implied verb which «مَقْعدهم» indicates, because it is in the sense of «تخلَّفوا», that is: "they stayed behind in opposition to the Messenger of Allah". The second: that «خلاف» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and its governor is either «فرح» or «مَقْعد», that is: they rejoiced because of their opposing the Messenger of Allah, in that he went on to jihad and they stayed behind from it; or by their sitting because of opposing him. To this al-Ṭabarī, al-Zajjāj and Muʾarrij went, and it is supported by the reading of whoever read «خُلْف» with a ḍamma on the khāʾ and a sukūn on the lām. The third: that it is accusative as a circumstance of place/time (ẓarf), that is: after the Messenger of Allah. One says: «أقام زيد خلاف القوم», that is, "he stayed behind after their departure", and «خلاف» is used as a ẓarf. The poet said:
2520 - عَقَبَ الربيعُ خِلافَهُمْ فكأنما ... بَسَطَ الشَّواطِبُ بينهن حصيرا
(The spring followed after them, as though the palm-leaf splitters had spread a mat among them.)
and another said:
2521 - فقلْ للذي يَبْقى خِلاَفَ الذي مضى ... تَهَيَّأْ لأخرى مِثلها وكأنْ قَدِ
(So say to the one who remains after the one who has gone: prepare for another like it, as if it had already come.)
To this Abū ʿUbayda, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Akhfash went, and it is supported by the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Ḥaywa and ʿAmr ibn Maymūn «خَلْفَ» with a fatḥa on the khāʾ and a sukūn on the lām.

semin-durr:83-83.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِن رَّجَعَكَ}: «رجع» is used transitively, as in this noble verse, and its maṣdar is «الرَّجْع», as in {والسمآء ذَاتِ الرجع} [al-Ṭāriq: 11]; and it is used intransitively, like {وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجِعُونَ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 35] in the reading of whoever built it with the agent as subject, and its maṣdar is «الرجوع», like «الدخول».
His saying: {أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ}: this has already preceded. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is a ẓarf." The Shaykh said: "He means a ẓarf of time, and it is remote", because the apparent sense is that it is accusative as a maṣdar; and in the exegesis it is "the first expedition the Messenger of Allah went out on", so the meaning is "the first time of going out". al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «مرة» is an indefinite noun put in the place of «المرات» ('times') from the superlative, then why is the superlative noun annexed to it mentioned, when it indicates one of the times? I say: the more frequent of the two usages is «هند أكبرُ النساء وهي أكبرُهن» ('Hind is the eldest of the women, and she is the eldest of them'); then your saying «هي كبرى امرأة» you will hardly come across, but rather «هي أكبر امرأة وأول مرة وآخر مرة»."
His saying: {مَعَ الخالفين}: this ẓarf may be attached to «اقعدوا», and it may be attached to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl from the agent of «اقعدوا». «الخالِف» is the one who stays behind after the people. It was also said: «الخالف» is the corrupt, from «خَلَفَ», that is, "became corrupt", and from it «خُلوف فم الصائم» (the odour of the fasting person's mouth). What is meant by them is the women, the children and the incapable men, and therefore its plural form is permissible by predominance (taghlīb). Qatāda said: "The Khālifūn are the women", which is rejected because of the plural form. ʿIkrima and Mālik ibn Dīnār read «مع الخَلِفين», shortened from «الخالِفين», like his saying:
2523 - مثل النَّقَا لَبَّده بَرْدُ الظِّلَلْ
(Like a sand dune packed down by the coolness of the shade.)
and his saying:
2524 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
عَرِدا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . بَرِدا
(…firm… cold.)
he means «الظلال» (shades), and «عارِداً» and «بارداً».

semin-durr:84-84.t: His saying, the Exalted: {مِّنْهُم}: an adjective of «أحد», and likewise the clause of His saying «مات». «منهم» may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مات», that is: "he died while being one of them, characterised by the attribute of hypocrisy", like their saying «أنت مني» ("you are from me"), meaning "on my way". And «أبداً» is a ẓarf governed by the prohibition.

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تُعْجِبْكَ أَمْوَالُهُمْ}: It was said: this is a reinforcement of the preceding verse. al-Fārisī said: "It is not a reinforcement, because that one concerns one group and this one another, and the wording of the two differs. Here it is «ولا» with the wāw, for the fitness of conjoining a prohibition to a prohibition before it in His saying «ولا تُصَلِّ، ولا تَقُمْ، ولا تُعْجبك», so the wāw is fitting; while there it is with the fāʾ, for the fitness of following on from His saying «ولا يُنْفِقون إلا وهم كارهون», that is, 'for spending', so they are impressed by the abundance of wealth and children, and He forbade him to be impressed with the fāʾ of sequence. Here it is «وأولادهم» without «لا», because it is a prohibition of being impressed by the two together, while there it has the addition of «لا», because it is a prohibition regarding each one by one; so the two combined indicate the prohibition regarding them both together and separately. Here it is «أنْ يُعَذِّبهم» and there «ليُعَذِّبهم»; so He brought the lām there to signal predominance, and the object of the intending is omitted, that is: 'Allah only intends to test them with wealth and children'; and He brought «أن» here because the target of the intending is the punishing, that is: 'Allah only intends to punish them'. So the object to which the intending is attached differs in the two verses. This is the apparent sense, though it is possible that the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and that «أَنْ» is on the omission of a causal lām. There it is «في الحياة الدنيا», and here «الحياة» is dropped, to alert to the baseness of this world and that it does not deserve to be called life, especially as it is mentioned after the mention of the death of the hypocrites, so it was fitting that it not be called life."

semin-durr:86-86.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذَآ أُنزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ}: «إذا» by its original placement does not require repetition, even if some people understood that from it here. This has already preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara, and I recited on it:
2525 - إذا وجدْتُ أوارَ الحُبِّ في كَبِدي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When I find the heat of love in my liver… [verse incomplete in the source])
and that this is understood only from contextual indications, not from what «إذا» was placed to convey.
His saying: {أَنْ آمِنُواْ}: there are two possibilities. The first: that it is explicative (tafsīriyya), because what precedes it is in the sense of speech, though not its letters. The second: that it is a maṣdar-forming particle with an omitted preposition, that is: «بأنْ آمنوا». In His saying «اسْتَأْذَنَكَ» there is an iltifāt (shift) from the third person to the second person, because the word «رسوله» preceded; had it followed the basic pattern it would have been said «استأذنه».

semin-durr:87-87.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَعَ الخوالف}: «الخَوَالِفُ» is the plural of «خالفة», from a description of women, and this is a description of censure, as in the saying of Zuhayr:
2526 - وما أَدْري وسوف إخالُ أَدْري ... أقومٌ آلُ حِصْنٍ أم نساءُ
فإنْ تكنِ النساءُ مُخَبَّآتٍ ... فَحُقَّ لكل مُحْصَنَةٍ هِداءُ
(I do not know, and I shall presently think I know: are the family of Ḥiṣn men or women? If women are to be kept hidden away, then every guarded woman deserves to be given a gift of a bride.)
and another said:
2527 - كُتِبَ القَتْلُ والقتالُ علينا ... وعلى الغانيات جَرُّ الذيولِ
(Killing and fighting have been decreed upon us, and upon the beautiful women the trailing of skirts.)
al-Naḥḥās said: "«الخوالِف» may be from a description of men, in the sense that it is the plural of «خالفة». One says «رجل خالِفَة», that is, 'there is no good in him'; so on this it would be a plural for males according to its wording." Some said: it is the plural of «خالف»; one says «رجلٌ خالفٌ», that is, "no good in him". But this is rejected, for «فواعل» is not a plural of «فاعل» as a description of a rational being, except what is irregular such as «فوارس» and «نواكس» and «هوالك».

semin-durr:88-88.t:
And «الخَيْرات» is the plural of «خَيْرة» on the pattern faʿla with a sukūn on the ʿayn; it is the best-liked of everything, and its use came to predominate for women, and from it comes His saying, the Exalted: {خَيْرَاتٌ حِسَانٌ}, and the poet's saying:
2528 - ولقد طَعَنْتُ مَجامِع الرَّبَلاتِ ... رَبَلاتِ هندٍ خَيْرةِ الملَكاتِ
(I have pierced the places where the plump flesh gathers, the plump flesh of Hind, the best of the queens.)

semin-durr:90-90.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {المعذرون}: It has been read in many ways. Among them is the reading of the majority: a fatḥa on the ʿayn and shadda on the dhāl. This reading admits two possibilities: that its pattern is faʿʿala, with doubling, and the meaning of the doubling in it is taking pains (takalluf); the meaning being that he imagined that he has an excuse, while he has no excuse. The second: that its pattern is iftaʿala, the original being «اعتذرَ»; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl by converting the tāʾ of iftiʿāl into a dhāl, and its vowel was moved to the silent letter before it, which is the ʿayn. The reading of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr «المعتذرون» on the original form indicates this. To this al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ, Abū ʿUbayda, Abū Ḥātim and al-Zajjāj went.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Aʿraj, Abū Ṣāliḥ and ʿĪsā ibn Hilāl read, and it is also the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Yaʿqūb and al-Kisāʾī, «المُعْذِرون» with a sukūn on the ʿayn and a kasra on the dhāl, light, from «أَعْذَر يُعْذِر» like «أكرم يكرم».
Maslama read «المُعَّذَّرون» with shadda on the ʿayn and the dhāl, from «تعذَّر» in the sense of «اعتذر». Abū Ḥātim said: "He meant «المتعذرون», but the tāʾ is not assimilated into the ʿayn because of the distance of their points of articulation, so it is a mistake by him or against him."
His saying: {لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُمْ}: attached to «جاء»; the agent is omitted and the prepositional phrase is put in its place because it is known, that is: "so that the Messenger may give them leave". The majority read «كَذَبوا» light, that is, "they lied in their faith". al-Ḥasan in the well-known report from him, Ubayy and Ismāʿīl read «كذَّبوا» with shadda, that is, "they did not believe what the Messenger brought from his Lord, nor did they comply with His command".

semin-durr:91-91.t:
Abū Ḥaywa read «نصحوا اللَّهَ» without a lām, and it has already been mentioned that «نَصَح» is made transitive by itself and by the lām.
His saying {مِن سَبِيلٍ}: an agent of the prepositional phrase, because it relies on a negation; it may also be a mubtadaʾ with the preceding prepositional phrase as its khabar. On both views «مِنْ» is redundant in it, that is: «ما على المحسنين سبيل».
Some said: in this verse there is a kind of badīʿ (rhetorical embellishment) called «التمليح» (tamlīḥ), which is: that you allude, in the gist of your speech, to a famous story, a current proverb or a rare verse without mentioning it; and from it is the saying:
2529 - اليومَ خمرٌ ويبدو بعده خَبَرٌ ... والدهرُ مِنْ بين إنعامٍ وإبْآسِ
(Today is wine, and after it news will appear; time moves between bestowing favour and bringing misery.)
He alludes to the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays when the news of the killing of his father reached him: «اليومَ خمرٌ وغداً أمره» ("Today is wine, and tomorrow is its matter"). And the saying of another:
2530 - فواللَّهِ ما أدري أأحلامُ نائمٍ ... أَلَمَّت بنا أم كان في الركب يوشَعُ
(By Allah, I do not know whether it was a sleeper's dreams that visited us, or whether Joshua was in the riding party.)
It alludes to the story of Joshua, peace be upon him, and his making the sun stop. And the saying of another:
2531 - لعَمْروٌ مع الرَّمْضاءِ والنارُ تَلْتَظِي ... أرقُّ وأحفى منكَ في ساعة الكَرْبِ
(ʿAmr, even with the scorching ground and the blazing fire, is gentler and more solicitous than you in the hour of distress.)
It alludes to the famous verse:
2532 - المستجيرُ بعمروٍ عند كُرْبته ... كالمستجير مِنَ الرَّمْضاءِ بالنار
(One who seeks the protection of ʿAmr in his distress is like one who flees the scorching ground into the fire.)
It is as if this saying, «ما على المحسنين من سبيل», had something of its meaning become widespread among the people, so He alluded to it without mentioning its wording. When the Shaykh mentioned tamlīḥ he did not qualify it with "without mentioning it", yet it is indispensable, because if he mentions it by its wording it is iqtibās (quotation) and taḍmīn (incorporation).

semin-durr:92-92.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ عَلَى الذين}: There are several possibilities in it. The first: that it is conjoined to «الضعفاء», that is: "there is no blame on the weak, nor on those who, when they came to you…", so they enter into the khabar of «ليس», the predicate being reported about them, attached to its subject «حَرَج». The second: that it is conjoined to «المحسنين», so they enter into what is predicated of His saying «من سبيل»; for «مِنْ سبيل» may be a mubtadaʾ, and may be the subject of the Hijazi «ما», and «مِنْ» is redundant in both cases. The third: that {وَلاَ عَلَى الذين} is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "nor, on those who, when they came to you, up to the end of the ṣila, is there any blame or way", and it is omitted because the speech indicates it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said it, and there is no need for it, because it is an estimate that can be dispensed with, since he has estimated something that this present expression stands in for, in wording and meaning. This relative noun may be included in His saying {وَلاَ عَلَى الذين لاَ يَجِدُونَ مَا يُنفِقُونَ}, and they were mentioned by way of denying blame from them; and they may not be included, if these were people who found what to spend but did not find a mount.
Maʿqil ibn Hārūn read «لنَحْملهم» with the nūn of majesty. There is a difficulty in it, since what the construction required was: "I said, I do not find that on which Allah may carry you."
His saying «قلت»: there are four possibilities in it. The first: that it is the apodosis of the conditional «إذا», and «إذا» with its apodosis is in the position of a ṣila, the ṣila being a conditional clause. On this, His saying «تَوَلَّوا» is an answer to an implied question, as if someone had said: "What was their state when they were answered with this answer?" and it was answered with His saying «تولَّوا». The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the kāf of «أَتَوْك», that is: "when they came to you while you were saying: I do not find that on which to carry you"; and «قد» is implied according to those who require that in a past verb occurring as ḥāl, like His saying {أَوْ جَآءُوكُمْ حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 90] in one of its possibilities, as its verification has preceded. To this al-Zamakhsharī inclined. The third: that it is conjoined to the condition, so it is in the position of the genitive through the annexation of the ẓarf to it by way of coordination, with the conjunction omitted, the implied form being «وقلت». You have already had discussion of this question and of what people cited as evidence on it. To this al-Jurjānī went, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya followed him, except that he estimated the conjunction as a fāʾ, that is «فقلت». The fourth: that it is resumptive. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: is it permissible for His saying «قلت لا أجدُ» to be resumptive like it", meaning like {رَضُواْ بِأَن يَكُونُواْ مَعَ الخوالف}, as if it were said: 'When they came to you for you to carry them, they turned away', and then it was said: 'What is the matter with them, that they turned away weeping?' [and it was said], 'You said: I do not find that on which to carry you', except that it is placed between the condition and the result like a parenthesis. I say: yes, and it is good." End of quotation.
The Shaykh said: "It is neither permissible nor good in the speech of the Arabs, so how in the speech of Allah? It is an understanding of a non-Arab." I say: I do not know the reason for his prohibiting it and not finding it good, given its clarity and obviousness in wording and meaning. That is because their turning away stands as it is, so the tears are not consequent merely on their coming to him, peace be upon him, for him to carry them, but on his saying to them {لاَ أَجِدُ مَآ أَحْمِلُكُمْ}; and if that is so, his saying that to them is a cause of their weeping, so it is good to make His saying {قُلْتَ: لاَ أَجِدُ مَآ أَحْمِلُكُمْ} an answer to whoever asks about the reason for their turning away while their eyes overflow with tears, which is the meaning Abū l-Qāsim intended. On these three possibilities which I put forward for «قلت», its apodosis is His saying «تولَّوا», and His saying «لتحملَهم» is the reason for «أَتَوْك». And His saying «لا أجد» is the one that takes one object, because it is from «الوُجْد». And «ما» may be a relative or a described (indefinite) noun.
His saying: {وَّأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «تَوَلَّوا». al-Zamakhsharī said: «تفيضُ من الدمع» is like your saying «تفيض دمعاً» ("overflowing tears"). This has been treated fully in al-Māʾida at His saying {ترى أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدمع} [al-Tawba: 83] [Translator's note: the source says al-Māʾida but cites al-Tawba 9:83; kept as written], where he made «من الدمع» a tamyīz (specification) and «مِنْ» redundant, and the refutation of him in that was given there, so turn to it.
His saying: {حَزَناً}: there are three possibilities for its accusative. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and its governor is «تفيض», as the Shaykh said. It cannot be said that the agent here differs, since the overflowing is attributed to the eyes and the grief proceeds from the owners of the eyes, and when the agent differs the noun must be governed by a preposition; for we say: grief is attributed to the eyes too, figuratively. One says: عين حزينةٌ وسخينة ("a sad eye", "a hot eye"), and عين مسرورةٌ وقريرة ("a delighted eye", "a cool eye") for the opposite. It may also be that its governor is «تَوَلَّوا», and then the agents of the reason and the effect are really the same. The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is: "they turned away sad", or "their eyes overflow sad", on the figurative sense mentioned. The third: that it is a maṣdar with an implied governor of its own wording, that is: "they grieve a grief", as Abū l-Baqāʾ said. And this clause he estimated as governing this maṣdar is itself in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl: either from the agent of «تَوَلَّوا» or from the agent of «تفيض».
His saying: {أَلاَّ يَجِدُواْ}: there are two possibilities in it. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and its governor is «حَزَناً» if we parse it as an object of purpose or a ḥāl; but if we parse it as a maṣdar, then no, because a maṣdar does not govern when it is a reinforcement of its governor. On the view that «حَزَناً» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, «أن لا يَجِدوا» is the reason of the reason, meaning that he gave the overflow of tears the reason of grief, and gave the grief the reason of not finding anything to spend. This is clear, and you have already had its counterpart in His saying {جَزَآءً بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَالاً مِّنَ الله} [al-Māʾida: 38]. The second: that it is attached to «تفيض». The Shaykh said: "Abū l-Baqāʾ said: 'It may be attached to «تفيض»'." Then the Shaykh said: "That is not permissible on his parsing of «حزناً» as an object of purpose governed by «تفيض», since a governor does not call for two objects of purpose except by conjunction or substitution."

semin-durr:93-93.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {رَضُواْ}: there are two possibilities in it. The first: that it is resumptive, as if someone had said: "What is the matter with them, that they asked leave to sit when they are able to fight?" and it was answered with His saying «رَضُوا بأن يكونوا مع الخوالِفِ». To this al-Zamakhsharī inclined. The second: that it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with «قد» implied in His saying [«رَضُوا»].
His saying: {وَطُبَعَ}: conjoined to «رضُوا», to alert that the cause of their staying behind is their contentment with their sitting and Allah's sealing of their hearts.
His saying {إِنَّمَا السبيل على}: He brought «على» although it can be connected with «إلى», for a difference they mentioned: «على» indicates superiority and the weakness of the defence of the one it is applied to, as in «لي سبيل عليك» and «لا سبيلَ لي عليك», unlike «إلى». So when you say «لا سبيل عليك», it is different from your saying «لا سبيلَ إليك». And among the cases where «إلى» comes with it is his saying:
2533 - ألا ليت شِعْري هل إلى أمِّ سالمٍ ... سبيلٌ فأمَّا الصبرُ عنها فلا صبرا
(Would that I knew whether there is a way to Umm Sālim; as for patience away from her, there is none.)
and his saying:
2534 - هل من سبيلٍ إلى خَمْرٍ فأشربَها ... أم من سبيل إلى نَصْرِ بن حَجَّاجِ
(Is there a way to wine, that I may drink it, or a way to Naṣr ibn Ḥajjāj?)

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قَدْ نَبَّأَنَا الله مِنْ أَخْبَارِكُمْ}: there are two possibilities in it. The first: that «نبَّأ» is the one governing two objects, the first being the «نا» and the second His saying «مِنْ أخباركم». On this «مِنْ» has two possibilities. One: that it is not redundant, and the estimate is: "Allah has informed us of some reports of your reports", or "a portion of your reports", so it is in reality an adjective of the omitted object. The other: that «مِنْ» is redundant according to al-Akhfash, because he sets no condition for it; the estimate being: "Allah has informed us of your reports".
The second of the two possibilities from the first pair: that it governs three objects, like «أعلم»; so the first and second are as stated, and the third is omitted for brevity because it is known, the estimate being: "Allah has informed us, of your reports, that it is a lie", or the like. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It may govern three, and the other two are omitted, the estimate being 'reports of your reports, established'; «من أخباركم» alerts to the omitted element, and «مِنْ» is not redundant, since if it were redundant it would be the second object and the third object omitted, which is an error because whenever the second object is mentioned in this chapter, mentioning the third is required. It was also said: «مِنْ» is in the sense of «عن»." I say: his statement that omitting the third is an error — if he means omission by suppression (ḥadhf iqtiṣār), it is conceded; if he means omission for brevity (ḥadhf ikhtiṣār), it is denied. The positions of the scholars on this question have already come to you.

semin-durr:95-95.t: His saying, the Exalted: {جَزَاءً}: it may be accusative as a maṣdar with an implied verb of its own wording, that is: «يُجْزَوْنَ جزاء»; and it may be accusative by the content of the preceding clause, because their taking refuge in Hell is in the sense of requital. It may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi.

semin-durr:97-97.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الأعراب}: a plural form, and it is not the plural of «عرب», as Sībawayh said; this is so as not to make the plural more specific than the singular, since «العرب» is this particular people whether they dwell in the desert or in the towns, whereas «الأعراب» is applied only to those who dwell in the desert. You have had this at the beginning of this work at His saying, the Exalted, {رَبِّ العالمين} [al-Fātiḥa: 1]. For this difference, the relative adjective is formed from «الأعراب» on its wording, so one says «أعرابيّ», and it is pluralised as «أعاريب».
His saying: {وَأَجْدَرُ}, that is, more fitting and more apt. One says: هو جديرٌ وأجدر وحقيق وأحقّ وقمين وأَوْلى وخليق بكذا, all in one meaning. al-Layth said: "جَدَر يَجْدُر جَدارةً, so he is جديرٌ", and it is feminised, dualised and pluralised. The poet said:
2535 - بِخَيْلٍ عليها جِنَّةٌ عَبْقَرِيَّةٌ ... جديرون يوماً أن يَنَالوا وَيَسْتَعْلوا
(With horsemen upon whom is a ʿabqarī jinn-like spirit, worthy one day of attaining and rising high.)
al-Rāghib drew attention to the origin of the derivation of this root, that it is from «الجِدار» (the wall), saying: "«الجديرُ» is the limit, because the matter ends at it as a thing ends at the wall." What appears is that its derivation is from «الجَدْر», which is the root of the tree, so it is as if it were firm, like the firmness of the root, in your saying «جدير بكذا».
His saying: {أَلاَّ يَعْلَمُواْ}, that is, «بأن لا يعلموا»; the preposition was omitted, so the well-known disagreement arose between al-Khalīl and al-Kisāʾī on the one side, and Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ on the other.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن يَتَّخِذُ مَا يُنفِقُ مَغْرَماً}: «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ, and it is either a relative noun or a described (indefinite) noun. «مَغْرَماً» is a second object, because «اتخذ» here is in the sense of «صَيَّر» ("made"). «المَغْرَمُ» is loss, derived from «الغَرام», which is destruction, because it is an evil; and from it {إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَاماً} [al-Furqān: 65]. It was also said: its origin is clinging, and from it comes «الغَريمُ» (the creditor), for his clinging to the one from whom he demands.
His saying: {وَيَتَرَبَّصُ}: conjoined to «يَتَّخِذ», so it is either part of the ṣila or an adjective. «التربُّصُ» is waiting. «الدوائر» is the plural of «دائرة», which is what surrounds a person of calamity and misfortune, conceived from the circle which surrounds a thing without escape from it. Its original is «داوِرَة» because it is from «دار يدور», that is, "surrounded". The meaning of «تربُّص الدوائر» is waiting for calamities. He said:
2536 - تَرَبَّصْ بها رَيْبَ المَنون لعلها ... تُطَلَّقُ يوماً أو يموتُ حليلُها
(Wait out with her the vicissitudes of fate; perhaps she will be divorced one day, or her husband will die.)
His saying: {عَلَيْهِمْ دَآئِرَةُ السوء}: this clause is parenthetical between the clauses of this account, and is a supplication against the Bedouins mentioned earlier. Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read here «السُّوء», and likewise the second in al-Fatḥ, with a ḍamma; the rest read with a fatḥa. As for the first in al-Fatḥ, which is «ظنَّ السَّوْء», the seven agreed on its fatḥa. As for the fatḥa form, it was said that it is a maṣdar. al-Farrāʾ said: "One says سُؤْتُه سُوْءاً ومَساءةً وسَوائِية ومَسَائِية, and with the ḍamma it is the noun." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is harm, and it is a maṣdar in reality." I say: he means that in origin it is like the fatḥa form in being a maṣdar, and then it was applied to every harm and evil. Makkī said: "Whoever puts a fatḥa on the sīn, its meaning is corruption and badness, and whoever puts a ḍamma, its meaning is defeat, affliction and harm." The apparent sense is that the two are nouns for what was mentioned, and it is possible that they are in origin a maṣdar and then applied to what was mentioned. Others said: the ḍamma form is punishment and harm, and the fatḥa form is censure; do you not see that they agreed on the fatḥa in {ظَنَّ السوء} [al-Fatḥ: 6] and in His saying {مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ امرأ سَوْءٍ} [Maryam: 28], and mention of punishment is not fitting in these two places.
al-Zamakhsharī said, and did well: "The ḍamma form is punishment, and the fatḥa form is censure of the 'circle', as in your saying «رجلُ سَوْء» as the opposite of «رجل عدل», because whoever the circle turns upon censures it." He means that it is of the type of annexing a described noun to its adjective, so it was in origin described by the maṣdar for emphasis and then annexed to its description, as in His saying, the Exalted, {مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ امرأ سَوْءٍ} [Maryam: 28]. The Shaykh said: "It has been reported with the ḍamma", and recited:
2537 - وكنت كذئبِ السُّوء لمَّا رأى دماً ... بصاحبه يوماً أحال على الدَّم
(You were like the evil wolf which, seeing blood on its companion one day, turned upon the blood.)
Concerning «الدائرة» there are two views, the clearer of which is that it is an adjective on the pattern fāʿila like «قائمة». al-Fārisī said: "It may be a maṣdar like «العافية»."
His saying: {بِكُمُ الدوائر}: there are two possibilities in it. The clearer is that the bāʾ is attached to the verb before it. The second: that it is a ḥāl from «الدوائر», as Abū l-Baqāʾ said, which is not clear; and on this it is attached to an omitted element, as has been established several times.

semin-durr:99-99.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قُرُبَاتٍ}: a second object of «يتخذ», as stated for «مَغْرَما». The seven readers did not differ over the ḍamma on the rāʾ of «قُرُبات», although they differ over the rāʾ of «قربة», as will come. It may be a plural of «قُرُبة» with a ḍamma, as in the reading of Warsh from Nāfiʿ, and it may be a plural of the form with a sukūn, the ḍamma being given only as assimilation to «غرفات»; and notice of this rule and its conditions has preceded at His saying, the Exalted, {فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ} [verse 17] at the beginning of al-Baqara.
His saying: {عِندَ الله}: there are three possibilities for this ẓarf. The clearest: that it is attached to «يَتَّخذ». The second: that it is a ẓarf of «قربات», as Abū l-Baqāʾ said, which is not so. The third: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of «قربات».
His saying: {وَصَلَوَاتِ الرسول}: two possibilities. The clearer: that it is conjoined to «قربات», which is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words, for he said: "The meaning is that what he spends is a cause of obtaining nearness with Allah «وصلوات الرسول», because he used to pray for those who give charity with good, as in his saying, 'O Allah, bless the family of Abū Awfā.'" The second, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed and Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned no other: that it is conjoined to «ما ينفق», that is: "and he takes, through righteous deeds and the blessings of the Messenger, a means of nearness."
His saying: {ألا إِنَّهَا قُرْبَةٌ}: the pronoun in «إنها» was said to refer to «صلوات», and it was also said to refer to the expenditures understood from «يُنفقون».
Warsh read «قُرُبَة» with a ḍamma on the rāʾ, and the rest with a sukūn; it was said they are two dialect forms. It was also said: the original is the sukūn and the ḍamma is assimilation, and there has already been a disagreement among the morphologists on this: is it permissible to make fuʿl heavy to fuʿul? Some made «عُسُراً» and «يُسُراً» with a ḍamma on the sīn branches of the sukūn forms. It was also said: the original is «قُرُبة» with a ḍamma, and the sukūn is for lightness, which accords more with the usage of the Arabs, since their basis is fleeing from heaviness to lightness.
In the resumption of this clause and its being headed by the two particles of alerting and verification, which signal the firmness and establishment of the matter, there is a testimony from Allah to the soundness of what he believed about his spending. al-Zamakhsharī said the sense of this, and said: "And likewise «سيُدْخلهم», and what is in the sīn of the verification of the promise."

semin-durr:100-100.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والسابقون}: two possibilities. The clearer: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and for its khabar there are three possibilities. One, which is the apparent one: that it is the supplicatory clause of His saying «رضي الله عنهم». The second: that the khabar is His saying «الأوَّلون», the meaning being: "the foremost, that is in emigration, [they] are the first of the people of this religion", or "the foremost to Paradise are the first of the people of emigration". The third: that the khabar is His saying {مِنَ المهاجرين والأنصار}, the meaning in it being the notification that the foremost of this community are from the Emigrants and the Helpers; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned that, and in the last two possibilities there is affectation.
The second of the two possibilities for «السابقين»: that it is conjoined to {مَن يُؤْمِنُ بالله}, that is: "and among them are the foremost". In it there is remoteness.
The majority have genitive «الأنصار», conjoined to the Emigrants, meaning that the foremost are from these two classes. A large group of distinguished figures read — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Qatāda, al-Ḥasan, Sallām, Saʿīd ibn Abī Saʿīd, ʿĪsā al-Kūfī, Ṭalḥa and Yaʿqūb — «والأنصارُ» in the nominative. There are two possibilities in it. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «رضيَ الله عنهم». The other: conjoined to «السابقون». What there is in it has preceded, so it takes its ruling.
His saying: {بِإِحْسَانٍ}: attached to an omitted element, because it is a ḥāl from the agent of «اتَّبعوهم». ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, held that the wāw is omitted from «والذين اتبعوهم», and said that the relative noun is an adjective of what precedes it, until Zayd ibn Thābit told him that it is with the wāw. He said: "Bring me Ubayy." They brought him, and he said to him: "The confirmation of that is in the Book of Allah, at the beginning of al-Jumuʿa: {وَآخَرِينَ مِنْهُمْ لَمَّا يَلْحَقُواْ بِهِمْ} [verse 3], in the middle of al-Ḥashr: {والذين جَآءُوا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ} [verse 10], and at the end of al-Anfāl: {والذين آمَنُواْ مِن بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُواْ} [verse 75]." It is reported that he heard a man reading it with the wāw and said: "Who taught you to read?" He said: "Ubayy." He summoned him, and he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught it to me, while you were selling mimosa pods at al-Baqīʿ." He said: "You have spoken truly; and if you wish, say: we were present while you were absent, we gave support while you gave none, we sheltered while you drove away." From there ʿUmar said: "I used to think that we had been raised to a height that no one after us would reach."
Ibn Kathīr read {تجري من تحتها} with the preposition «مِنْ», and it is written so in the Meccan codices. The rest read «تحتها» without it, and it is not written in their codices. Most of what the Qur'an has agrees with the reading of Ibn Kathīr here: {تجري مِنْ تحتها} in more than one place.

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكُمْ}: a fronted khabar. «منافقون» is the mubtadaʾ, and «مَنْ» may be a relative or a described (indefinite) noun, the ẓarf being a ṣila or an adjective.
His saying: {مِّنَ الأعراب} is to clarify the kind. His saying: {وَمِنْ أَهْلِ المدينة} may be conjoined to «مَنْ» governed by «مِنْ», so the two genitives share in predicating of the mubtadaʾ «منافقون», as if it were said: "the hypocrites are from a people around you and from the people of Medina"; on this it is a conjunction of single terms, since it conjoins a khabar to a khabar, and on this His saying «مَرَدُوا» is resumptive and has no position. It may also be that the speech is complete at His saying «منافقون», and His saying {وَمِنْ أَهْلِ المدينة} is a fronted khabar, the mubtadaʾ after it being omitted with its adjective standing in its place. Omitting the described noun and putting its adjective in its place, when it is a clause, is regular with the partitive «مِنْ», as has been verified, as in «منا ظَعَن ومنا أقام» ("among us is one who departed and among us is one who stayed"); and the estimate is: "and among the people of Medina are a people or folk who persisted"; on this it is a conjunction of clauses. On the first possibility, «مَرَدُوا» may be an adjective of «منافقون», separated from its adjective by His saying {وَمِنْ أَهْلِ المدينة}. The estimate is: "among those around you and among the people of Medina are hypocrites who have persisted." al-Zajjāj said that, and al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Baqāʾ followed him. The Shaykh considered it remote because of the separation by the conjoined element between the adjective and what it describes, saying: "So it becomes like «في الدار زيدٌ وفي القصرِ العاقلُ»", meaning you separate Zayd and «العاقل» with your saying «وفي القصر». al-Zamakhsharī likened the omission of the described mubtadaʾ in the second possibility, with its adjective standing in for it, to the saying:
2538 - أنا ابنُ جلا. . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I am the son of Jalā…)
The Shaykh said: "If he means in the general omission of the described noun, it is fine; but if he likened it to it in its particularity, it is not fine, because omitting the described noun with «مِنْ» is regular, while «أنا ابن جلا» is a poetic licence like the saying:
2539 - يَرْمِي بكفَّيْ كان مِنْ أَرْمَى البشَرْ ..."
(He throws with the two hands of one who was among the best archers of mankind…)
I say: the verse referred to is his saying:
2540 - أنا ابن جَلا وطَلاَّعُ الثَّنايا ... متى أَضَعِ العِمامةَ تعرفونِي
(I am the son of the one who unveils and who climbs the mountain passes; when I take off my turban you will know me.)
The grammarians have several interpretations of this verse. One is what preceded. Another: that this clause is quoted, because the man was named by it, for «جلا» contains an agent pronoun, and then he was named by it and it was quoted, as they said «شاب قَرْناها» and «ذرى حَبَّا», and his saying:
2541 - نُبِّئْتُ أخوالي بني يزيدُ ... ظُلْماً علينا لهمُ فَدِيدُ
(I was told my maternal uncles, the Banū Yazīd, [wrongfully against us they have a clamour].)
The third, which is the school of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar: that it is a verb empty of a pronoun, and it is not given tanwīn because according to him it is a diptote, being barred by the pattern of the verb in common; so if one were named with «ضرب» or «قتل» they would be barred. As for the mere pattern without transfer from a verb, it is not barred at all, like «جَمَل» and «جَبَل». [Translator's note: the source text of this paragraph seems slightly corrupt; translated as written.]
«مَرَدوا» means "they became expert and practised". The discussion of this root has preceded in al-Nisāʾ at His saying {شَيْطَاناً مَّرِيداً} [verse 117].
His saying: {لاَ تَعْلَمُهُمْ}: this clause is also in the position of the nominative, an adjective of «منافقون»; it may also be resumptive. «العلم» here may be in its basic sense and so governs two objects, that is: "you do not know them to be hypocrites", the second being omitted because the earlier mention of the hypocrites indicates it, and because hypocrisy is among the attributes of the heart which cannot be observed. Or it may be the sense of recognition (ʿirfāniyya) and so governs one object, as Abū l-Baqāʾ said. As for «نحن نعلمهم», it cannot be except in its basic sense, for a discussion I mentioned to you in al-Anfāl, even though al-Fārisī in his «Īḍāḥ» explicitly ascribed recognition to Him, the Exalted, which is objectionable for what you have learned.
His saying: {مَّرَّتَيْنِ}: the discussion of the accusative of «مرة» has preceded, that it is in two ways: either as a maṣdar or as a ẓarf, and so likewise this. This dual may mean doubling of the one (that is, two times), which is what most say, and they differ in explaining the two; or it may be that the true dual is not meant but rather multiplication, as in His saying, the Exalted, {فارجِعِ البَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ} [al-Mulk: 4], that is, many times, by the proof of His saying «ينقلبْ إليك البصرْ خاسئاً وهو حسير», that is, repelled and weary, and that does not befall it except after many repetitions; and like it «لَبَّيْك وسَعْدَيْك وحنانَيْكَ».
ʿAbbās reported from Abū ʿAmr: «سنعذِّبْهم» with a sukūn on the bāʾ, which is his habit of lightening successive vowels, as in «ينصركم» and its like, though the case of «ينصركم» is better for the sukūn, as the rāʾ is a letter of repetition, so it is as if two ḍammas succeed each other, unlike other cases. The verification of this has preceded. The Shaykh said: "In the codex of Anas: «سيعذبهم» with the yāʾ." It has already been mentioned that the codices were devoid of dots and vocalisation marks, so how could this be said?

semin-durr:102-102.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَآخَرُونَ}: conjoined to «منافقون», that is: "and among those around you are others", or "and among the people of Medina are others". It may be a mubtadaʾ with «اعترفوا» as its adjective and its khabar His saying «خلطوا».
His saying: {وَآخَرَ}: conjoined to «عملاً». al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: each of the two has been made 'mixed', so what is it mixed with? I say: each is mixed and mixed-with, because the meaning is that each of the two was mixed with the other, as in your saying «خَلَطْتُ الماء واللبن» ('I mixed the water and the milk'), meaning: I mixed each of the two with its companion. In it is something that is not in your saying «خَلَطْتُ الماءَ باللبن» ('I mixed the water with the milk'), because there you made the water the mixed and the milk the mixed-with. When you say it with the wāw, you make water and milk both mixed and mixed-with, as if you had said: I mixed the water with the milk and the milk with the water." Then he said: "It may be from their saying «بِعْتُ الشاء: شاةً ودرهماً» ('I sold the sheep: a sheep and a dirham'), in the sense of 'a sheep for a dirham'." I say: he does not mean that the wāw is in the sense of the bāʾ; this is only an explanation of meaning. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If it were with the bāʾ, it would be permissible to say: «خلطْتُ الحِنْطة والشعير» and «خلطت الحنطةَ بالشعير»."
His saying: {عسى الله}: this clause may be resumptive, and it may be in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «آخرون», in which case His saying «خلطوا» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with «قد» implied with it, that is: «قد خلطوا». So it is summarised for «آخرون» that it is conjoined to «منافقون», or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «خلطوا», or the clause of hope.

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ}: two possibilities. One: that it is attached to «خُذْ», and «مِنْ» is partitive. The other: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is a ḥāl from «صدقة», since in origin it is an adjective of it, and when it was fronted it became accusative as a ḥāl.
His saying: {تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ}: the tāʾ in «تُطَهِّرهم» may be the address to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and may be third person, the agent being the pronoun for the charity. On the first, the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «خذ». It may also be an adjective of «صدقةً», in which case an ʿāʾid must be omitted, its implied form being «تطهِّرهم بها»; and «بها» is omitted because what follows indicates it. On the second, the clause is an adjective of «صدقة» only. As for «وتُزَكّيهم», the tāʾ in it is for the address only, because of «بها», since the pronoun refers to the charity, so it is impossible for the pronoun of «تزكِّيهم» to refer to the charity; on this the clause is a ḥāl from the agent of «خُذْ», on our saying that «تُطَهِّرهم» is a ḥāl from it and that the tāʾ in it is the address. It may also be an adjective if we say that «تطهِّرهم» is an adjective and its ʿāʾid is omitted.
Makkī allowed «تُطَهِّرهم» to be an adjective of «صدقة» with the tāʾ as third person, and «تُزَكِّيهم» a ḥāl from the agent of «خُذْ» with the tāʾ as address. They rejected it against him, because the wāw is a conjunction, that is: "a purifying charity and one that purifies by it"; whereas had it been without the wāw it would be permissible. I say: the reason for its invalidity is clear, for the wāw makes the two partners in wording and meaning, so if «وتزكيهم» were conjoined to «تُطَهِّرهم» it would necessarily be an adjective like the one it is conjoined to, since the two cannot differ; but that is permissible if «تزكِّيهم» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ and the wāw is of ḥāl, the implied form being «وأنت تزكِّيهم». In it there is weakness because of the rarity of its counterpart in their speech.
It is summarised from that that the two clauses may be two ḥāls from the agent of «خُذْ» with the tāʾ as address; or two adjectives of «صدقة» with the tāʾ as third person, with the ʿāʾid omitted from the first; or «تطهِّرهم» a ḥāl or adjective and «تزكِّيهم» a ḥāl as Makkī allowed; or «تزكِّيهم» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ with the wāw of ḥāl.
al-Ḥasan read «تُطْهِرهم» light, from «أطهر», making it transitive by the hamza.
His saying: {إِنَّ صلاوتك}: the two Brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ḥafṣ read «إنَّ صلاتَكَ», and in Hūd «أصلاتك تأمُرك», in the singular; the rest read «إنَّ صلواتك» and «أصلواتُك» in the plural in both; both are clear, except that «الصلاة» here is supplication, and there it is worship.
«السَّكَنُ» is tranquillity. He said:
2542 - يا جارةَ الحيِّ ألاَّ كنتِ لي سَكَناً ... إذ ليس بعضٌ من الجيران أَسْكَنني
(O neighbour of the tribe, would that you were a source of tranquillity for me, since some of the neighbours do not give me tranquillity.)
So faʿal is in the sense of mafʿūl, like «القَبْض» in the sense of «المقبوض», and the meaning is: "they find tranquillity in it". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Therefore he did not feminise it." But the apparent sense is that here it is in the sense of fāʿil, because of His saying «لهم»; and if it were as he said, the construction would be «سكنٌ إليها», that is, "something rested in"; so it is clear that the meaning is "a source of tranquillity for them".

semin-durr:104-104.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {هُوَ يَقْبَلُ}: «هو» is a mubtadaʾ, «يَقْبَلُ» is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «أنَّ», and «أنَّ» with what is in its scope stands in the place of the two objects, or in the place of the first. It is not permissible for «هو» to be a separating pronoun (faṣl), because what follows it does not create any suspicion of being an adjective; and this has been verified earlier.
al-Ḥasan read, and the Shaykh said: in the codex of Ubayy: «ألم تعلموا» with the address (second person plural). There are several possibilities in it: one: that it is an address to those who stayed behind, who said: "What is this distinction which these were given?" The [second]: that it is an iltifāt without an implied saying, and the ones meant are the repentant. The [third]: that it is on an implied saying, that is: "Say to them, Muḥammad: Do you not know?"
His saying: {عَنْ عِبَادِهِ}: attached to «يَقْبَل». It was made transitive with «عن»; it was said: because the meaning of «مِنْ» and the meaning of «عن» are close. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Often this one and that one are used interchangeably in one place, as in «لا صدقةَ إلا عن غني ومِنْ غني» ('there is no charity except from a wealthy person') and «فعل ذلك فلانٌ مِنْ أَشَره وبَطَره، وعن أَشَره وبَطَره» ('so-and-so did that out of his arrogance and insolence')." It was also said: the word «عن» signals some distance; you say «جلس عن يمين الأمير» ('he sat to the right of the emir'), that is, with a kind of distance. The apparent sense is that «عن» here is for passing beyond (mujāwaza) in its basic sense, and the meaning is: "He passes over His servants by accepting their repentance"; so when you say «أخذت العلم عن زيد» its meaning is passing, and when you say «منه» its meaning is the beginning of the limit.
His saying: {هُوَ التواب}: it may be a faṣl and it may be a mubtadaʾ, unlike what precedes it.

semin-durr:106-106.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مُرْجَوْنَ}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «مُرْجَؤُون» with a hamza with a ḍamma followed by a silent wāw. The rest read «مُرْجَوْن» without that hamza, which is like their reading in al-Aḥzāb «تُرْجِىء» with the hamza, the rest without it. They are two dialect forms: one says أَرْجَأْتُه and أَرْجَيْتُه like أَعْطيته. It is possible that they are two original forms in themselves, and that the yāʾ is a substitute for the hamza, since the realisation of the hamza is well-known to be frequent, as in قَرَأْت and قَرَيْتُ, توضَّأْت and توضَّيْت.
His saying: {إِمَّا يُعَذِّبُهُمْ}: this clause may be in the position of the nominative as a khabar, and «مُرْجَوْن» on this would be an adjective of the mubtadaʾ; or it may be a khabar after a khabar, or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, that is: "they are postponed: either punished or pardoned." «إمَّا» here is for doubt with respect to the addressee, or for vagueness with respect to the fact that He left it vague to the addressees.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والذين اتخذوا}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «الذين اتخذوا» without a wāw, and the rest with the conjunctive wāw. As for the reading of Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir, it is for agreement with their codices, for the wāw is omitted in the codices of Medina and Syria, while it is present in the codices of others. «الذين», on the reading of whoever omitted the wāw before it, has several possibilities. One: that it is a badal (substitute) for «آخرون» before it. In it there is some doubt, because these who took a mosque for harm cannot be said to be "deferred to the command of Allah", because it is reported in the exegesis that they were among the chief hypocrites such as Abū ʿĀmir the monk.
The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and about its khabar there are then several views. One: that it is «أفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بنيانَه», with the ʿāʾid omitted, its implied form being «بنيانَه منهم». The second: that it is «لا يزال بنيانُهم», as al-Naḥḥās and al-Ḥawfī said, and in it there is remoteness because of the length of the separation. The third: that it is «لا تقمْ فيه», as al-Kisāʾī said. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is workable with an implied element, either at the beginning of the verse or at its end, with the estimate: 'do not stand in their mosque'." The fourth: that the khabar is omitted, its implied form being «معذَّبون» or the like, as al-Mahdawī said.
The third possibility: that it is accusative by ikhtiṣāṣ (specification). This possibility will also come in the reading with the wāw.
As for the reading with the wāw, it has what has preceded, except that the badal from «آخرون» is barred because of the conjunction. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: «والذين اتخذوا», what is its position in iʿrāb? I say: its position is the accusative by ikhtiṣāṣ, as in His saying, the Exalted, {والمقيمين الصلاة} [al-Nisāʾ: 162]. It was also said: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its meaning being 'among those we have described are those who took…', as in His saying {والسارق والسارقة} [al-Māʾida: 38]." I say: he means according to the school of Sībawayh, whose estimate is "in what is recited to you is the thief", omitting the khabar and keeping the mubtadaʾ, like this verse.
His saying: {ضِرَاراً}: there are three possibilities in it. One: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, that is: "to harm their brothers". Second: that it is a second object of «اتَّخذ», as Abū l-Baqāʾ said. Third: that it is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl from the agent of «اتخذوا», that is: "they took it while harming their brothers"; and it may be accusative as a maṣdar, that is: "they harm others by it a harming", and the attachments of these maṣdars are omitted, that is: «ضِراراً لإِخوانهم وكفراً بالله».
His saying: {مِن قَبْلُ}: there are two possibilities in it. One, which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned alone: that it is attached to His saying «اتخذوا», that is: "they took a mosque before these became hypocrites". The second: that it is attached to «حارب», that is: "he fought before the taking of this mosque".
His saying: {وَلَيَحْلِفَنَّ إِنْ أَرَدْنَا}: «لَيَحْلِفُنَّ» is the answer of an implied oath, that is: «والله ليحلِفُنَّ». And His saying «إن أَرَدْنا» is the answer to His saying «ليحلِفُنَّ», so the answer to the implied oath is an oath-verb answered by His saying «إنْ أَرَدْنا». «إنْ» is negative, which is why «إلا» occurs after it. «الحسنى» is an adjective of an omitted described noun, that is: «إلا الخصلة الحسنى» or «إلا الإِرادةَ الحسنى». al-Zamakhsharī said: "We intended by building this mosque nothing but the best aim, or nothing but the desire for the best, which is prayer." The Shaykh said: "It is as if in his saying «إلا الخصلة الحُسْنى» he made it an object, and in his saying «أو لإِرادة الحسنى» he made it a reason, as though he had given «أراد» the sense of «قصد», that is: 'they intended by building it nothing at all except the desire for the best'." He said: "This is an affected possibility."

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَّمَسْجِدٌ}: two possibilities. One: that it is the lām of ibtidāʾ (commencement). The second: that it is the answer to an implied oath. On both estimates «لَمَسْجِدٌ» is a mubtadaʾ, «أُسِّس» is in the position of the nominative as its adjective, and «أحقُّ» is its khabar; and the deputy agent is the pronoun of the mosque with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "its building was founded".
«مِنْ أولِ» is attached to it, and the Kufans used it as evidence that «مِنْ» can be for the beginning of a limit in time; they also used as evidence the saying:
2543 - مِنَ الصبحِ حتى تَطْلُعَ الشمسُ لا ترى ... من القوم إلا خارجيّاً مُسَوَّما
(From dawn until the sun rises you see of the people only a marked rider outstripping.)
and the saying:
2544 - تُخُيِّرْن مِنْ أزمانِ يومِ حَليمةٍ ... إلى اليوم قد جُرِّبْن كلَّ التجاربِ
(They were chosen from the times of the Day of Ḥalīma until today; they have been tried in every trial.)
The Basrans interpreted it with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "from the founding of the first day", "from the rising of dawn", "from the coming of the times of the Day". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "This is weak, because the estimated founding is not a place such that «مِنْ» would be for the beginning of its limit. What shows the permissibility of that is His saying {لِلَّهِ الأمر مِن قَبْلُ وَمِن بَعْدُ} [al-Rūm: 4], and it is frequent in the Qur'an and elsewhere." I say: the Basrans only fled from its being for the beginning of the limit in time, and there is nothing in this expression requiring that it be only for the beginning of the limit in place such that it would be refuted against them by what was mentioned; the disagreement on this question is strong, and Abū ʿAlī has a long discussion on it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "I find it good to dispense with an estimate, and for «مِنْ» to govern the word «أول» as genitive, because it is in the sense of beginning, as if he said: 'from the start of the days'; and this which I have chosen has been related to me from one of the imams of grammar."
His saying: {أَحَقُّ} is not for comparison but in the sense of «حقيق» ("worthy"), since there is no comparison between the two mosques; «أن تقوم» is «بأن تقوم», and the tāʾ is the address to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and «فيه» is attached to it.
His saying: {فِيهِ رِجَالٌ}: «فيه» may be an adjective of «مسجد» with «رجال» as agent, and it may be a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «فيه» with «رجال» as its agent too; these two are better in that describing with a single word is the basic rule, and the prepositional phrase is close to a single word. «فيه» may also be a fronted khabar and «رجال» a postponed mubtadaʾ. In this clause there are also three possibilities: one, adjective; two, ḥāl, as preceded; three, resumptive.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd read «فيهِ» with a kasra on the hāʾ and the second «فيهُ» with a ḍamma, which is the original, combining the two dialects, and also removing the suspicion of emphasis and the suspicion that «رجالاً» is nominative by «تقوم».
His saying: {يُحِبُّونَ}: an adjective of «رجال», and «أن [يتطهروا]» is the direct object. Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif and al-Aʿmash read «يَطَّهَّرُوا» with assimilation, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib «المتطهِّرين» with the unassimilated form, the opposite of the readings of the majority in the two words.

semin-durr:109-109.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَانَهُ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «أُسِّس» as passive, with «بنيانُه» nominative, as it stands in for the agent. The rest read «أَسَّس» as active, «بنيانه» being the direct object and the agent the pronoun of «مَنْ». ʿUmāra ibn ʿĀʾidh read the first as passive and the second as active, with «بنيانُه» nominative in the first and accusative in the second for the reason stated. Naṣr ibn ʿAlī and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read «أُسُسُ بنيانِه». Abū Ḥaywa and the two Naṣrs also read «أَساسُ بنيانِه», the plural of «أُسّ». It was reported from Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim also «أَسُّ» with a fatḥa on the hamza and a doubled sīn with ḍamma. «إساس» with a kasra was also read; these are plurals annexed to «البنيان». «أساس» with a fatḥa on the hamza and «أُسّ» with a ḍamma on the hamza and doubled sīn were also read, and they are two singulars annexed to «البنيان». The author of the book «al-Lawāmiḥ» transmitted in it «أَسَسُ» light with ḍamma on the sīn, and «بنيانِه» genitive; «أَسَسٌ» is the maṣdar of «أسَّ يؤسُّه أَسَسَاً وأسَّاً». These are ten readings.
«الأُسُّ» and «الأَساس» are the foundation on which a thing is built; one says «كان ذلك على أُسِّ الدهر» like their saying «على وجه الدهر» ("from the earliest time"); and one says «أَسَّ» with doubling, that is, "made a foundation for it", and «آسَسَ» on the pattern fāʿala.
«البُنْيان» has two views. One: that it is a maṣdar like «الغفران» and «الشكران», applied to the object like «الخَلْق» in the sense of «المخلوق». The second: that it is a plural whose singular is «بُنْيانة». The poet said:
2545 - كبُنْيانةِ القاريِّ مَوْضِعُ رَحْلِها ... وآثارُ نَسْعَيْها مِنَ الدَّقِّ أَبْلَقُ
(Like the building of the Qārī, the place of her saddle, and the marks of her girth straps from the pounding are piebald.)
They mean that it is a generic noun like «قمح» and «قمحة».
His saying: {على تقوى}: two possibilities. One: that it is attached to «أَسَّس» itself, so it is its object in meaning. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «أَسَّسَ», that is: "intending piety by his building", as Abū l-Baqāʾ estimated it.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «تقوىً» with tanwīn. Sībawayh reported this reading, and people did not approve it because its alif is for feminine, so there is no reason for tanwīn; people have explained it as the alif being for ilḥāq (the alif of annexation to a pattern). Ibn Jinnī said: "By analogy its alif is for ilḥāq like «أَرْطى»."
His saying: {خَيْرٌ}: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The comparison here is according to their own belief. «أم» is the connected one, the second «من» is conjoined to the first «مِنْ», and «أَسَّس بنيانه» is like the first.
His saying: {على شَفَا جُرُفٍ}: like His saying «على تقوى» in its two possibilities. «الشَّفا» preceded in Āl ʿImrān. Ḥamza, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «جُرْفٍ» with a sukūn on the rāʾ, the rest with a ḍamma; it was said they are two dialect forms. It was also said: the sukūn form is a branch of the ḍamma form, like «عُنْق» for «عُنُق» and «طُنْب» for «طُنُب». It was also said the reverse, like «عُسُر» and «يُسُر». «الجُرُف» is the well that has not been lined.
It was also said: it is the hollow and what the torrent sweeps away of the valleys, as Abū ʿUbayda said. It was also said: it is the place that the water eats away and so sweeps away, that is, carries off. And «رَجُلٌ جِرَاف» means a man of much sexual intercourse, as if he sweeps away in that act, as al-Rāghib said.
His saying: {هَارٍ}: an adjective of «جُرُفٍ». There are three views on it. One, the well-known: that it is metathesised, by moving its lām before its ʿayn; its original being «هاوِرٌ» or «هايِرٌ» with wāw and yāʾ, because both forms were heard in it. They said: هار يَهُور فانْهارَ, and هار يَهير. And تَهَوَّر البناء and تَهَيَّر. The lām, which is the rāʾ, was moved before the ʿayn, which is the wāw or yāʾ, so it became like «غازٍ» and «رامٍ», and was subject to the weak-letter reduction like theirs; so its pattern after metathesis is fāliʿ, and after deletion it is fālin.
The second: that its ʿayn was dropped without cause, that is, with no requirement, and on this it takes the iʿrāb endings on its lām, so one says: هذا هارٌ, ورأيت هاراً, ومررت بهارٍ; its pattern is also fāl.
The third: that there is no metathesis and no deletion, and that its original is «هَوِر» or «هَيِر» on the pattern «كَتِف»; the weak letter was vowelled with a fatḥa before it, so it was changed to alif, becoming like their saying «كبشٌ صافٌ» (that is «صَوِف») or «يومٌ راحٌ» (that is «رَوِح»). On this it is also vowelled with the iʿrāb, like the one before it, as you say هذا باب, ورأيت باباً, ومررت ببابٍ. This is the most balanced of the views, as it is spared the claim of metathesis and deletion, which are contrary to the basic rule, were it not that it is not well-known among the morphologists. The meaning of «هار» is falling, collapsing, crumbling.
His saying: {فانهار}: its agent is either the pronoun of «البنيان», in which case the hāʾ in «به» is the pronoun of the founder-builder, that is: "the building of the builder fell on the edge of a crumbling bank"; or the pronoun of «الجُرُف», that is: "the edge fell" or "the bank fell", with the hāʾ in «به» for the building. It may also be for the builder-founder; and it is better that the agent be the pronoun of the bank, because its collapse necessarily entails the edge and the building together, while their collapse, or the collapse of one of them, does not necessarily entail its collapse. The bāʾ in «به» may be the one that makes transitive, and may be the one of accompaniment. You have already had a disagreement at the beginning of this work: that the transitive bāʾ, according to some, entails accompaniment. When it is said to be of accompaniment here, it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, that is: "it collapsed accompanying him".

semin-durr:110-110.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بُنْيَانُهُمُ}: it may be a maṣdar as it is, that is: "this action issuing from them continues"; and it may be that the thing built is meant, in which case one is forced to omit a muḍāf, that is: "the building of their building", because what is built is not doubt, and the omission is estimated from the second, that is: "what they built continues to be a cause of doubt". His saying «الذي بَنَوا» is an emphasis, to ward off the suspicion of whoever might suspect that they did not really build and only planned matters, from their saying «كم أبني وتهدمُ» ("how much I build and you demolish"), and on this is his saying:
2546 - متى يبلغُ البُنيانُ يوماً تمامَه ... إذا كنت تَبْنِيه وغيرك يَهْدِم
(When will the building ever reach completion, if you build it while another demolishes?)
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن تَقَطَّعَ}: the excepted-from is omitted and the estimate is: "their building will not cease to be a doubt at any time except the time of the cutting up of their hearts", or "in every state except the state of its cutting up". Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read «تَقَطَّع» with a fatḥa on the tāʾ, the original being «تتقطع» with two tāʾs, one of which was dropped. The rest read «تُقَطَّع» with a ḍamma, passive, imperfect of «قَطَّع» with doubling. Ubayy read «تَقْطَع» light, from «قطع». al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Qatāda and Yaʿqūb read «إلى أن» with the preposition «إلى», and Abū Ḥaywa likewise. This is a reading clear in meaning, except that Abū Ḥaywa read «تُقَطِّع» with a ḍamma on the tāʾ, a fatḥa on the qāf and a doubled kasra on the ṭāʾ, the agent being the pronoun of the Messenger; «قلوبَهم» is accusative as the object, and the meaning is that he kills them and gets full hold of them. It was also said: the agent is the pronoun of the doubt, that is: "until the doubt cuts their hearts." In the codex of ʿAbd Allāh it is «ولو قُطِّعَتْ», and his companions read it so, which differs from the script of the people's codices.

semin-durr:111-111.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ}: attached to «اشترى». The bāʾ enters here upon the thing given up, in accordance with its basic usage, and Abū l-Baqāʾ called it the bāʾ of exchange, like their saying bāʾ al-ʿiwaḍ. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb read «بالجنة».
His saying «يُقاتِلُون»: it may be resumptive and may be a ḥāl. al-Zamakhsharī said: «يقاتلون» has the sense of a command, like His saying, the Exalted, {وَتُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ الله بِأَمْوَالِكُمْ وَأَنفُسِكُمْ} [al-Ṣaff: 11]. I say: on this the resumptive reading is necessary, because a request cannot be a ḥāl. The disagreement over «فيَقتلون ويُقتلون» has preceded in Āl ʿImrān.
His saying: {وَعْداً}: accusative as a reinforcing maṣdar of the content of the clause, because the meaning of «اشترى» is that He promised them that, so it is the counterpart of «هذا ابني حقاً» ("this is my son, truly"). It may also be a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl, and in it is weakness. «حقاً» is its adjective, and «عليه» is a ḥāl from «حقاً», because in origin it is an adjective of it, had it been postponed.
His saying: {فِي التوراة}: two possibilities. One: that it is attached to «اشترى», and on this every community was commanded to fight and promised Paradise for it. The second: that it is attached to an omitted element because it is an adjective of the promise, that is: "a promise mentioned and found in the Torah", and on this the promise of Paradise for this community is mentioned in the revealed Books of Allah. al-Zamakhsharī said in the course of his words: «لا يجوز عليه قبيحٌ قط» ("nothing ugly is ever permissible for Him"). The Shaykh said: "He used «قط» in other than its placement; because he brought it with His saying «لا يجوز عليه», and «قط» is a ẓarf of past time, so only a past governs it." I say: a specific time is not meant here.
His saying: {فاستبشروا}: there is an iltifāt from the third person to the address, since in addressing them with that there is honour for them. «استفعل» here is not for request but in the sense of «أفعل», like «استوقد» and «أوقد». His saying {الذي بَايَعْتُمْ بِهِ} is an emphasis, like His saying {الذي بَنَوْاْ} [al-Tawba: 110], to specify for them this very transaction.

semin-durr:112-112.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {التائبون}: there are five possibilities in it. One: that they are a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «العابدون», with what follows being adjectives or multiple khabars according to whoever allows that. The second: that the khabar is His saying «الآمرون». The third: that the khabar is omitted, that is: "the repentant who are described with these attributes are among the people of Paradise", and His saying «وبَشِّر المؤمنين» supports it. This is according to whoever holds that this verse is cut off from what precedes and is not a condition in fighting. As for whoever claimed that it is a condition in fighting, like al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others, the iʿrāb of «التائبين» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: «هم التائبون»; this is of the type of qaṭʿ al-nuʿūt (cutting off the adjectives from the noun), because these attributes, according to those who say so, are among the attributes of the believers in His saying, the Exalted, {[اشترى] مِنَ المؤمنين أَنفُسَهُمْ} [al-Tawba: 111]. The reading of Ubayy, Ibn Masʿūd and al-Aʿmash «التائبين» with the yāʾ supports that. This reading may also be on the cutting-off, in which case it is accusative by an implied verb. al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya stated explicitly that «التائبين» in this reading is an adjective. The fifth: that «التائبون» is a badal from the attached pronoun in «يقاتلون». [Translator's note: the source's numbering jumps from the third possibility to the fifth; the fourth is presumably the cutting-off view discussed within the third.]
No attachment is mentioned for these attributes; He did not say "the repentant from such-and-such", nor "the worshippers of Allah", because that is understood, except in the forms of command and prohibition, for emphasis in that. He did not bring a conjunction between these attributes because of their fittingness to each other, except in the forms of command and prohibition because of the difference between them, for command is a demand for an action and prohibition is a demand for abandonment or restraint; and likewise «الحافظون», whose conjunction He included and whose attachment He mentioned. He brought the order of these attributes in mention in the finest arrangement, which is apparent upon reflection, for He put repentance first and then followed it with worship, to the end. It was also said: the wāw was only entered because it is the wāw of eight, as in {وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ} [al-Kahf: 22] and {وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا} [al-Zumar: 71]; when Paradise has eight gates, the wāw was brought with it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The wāw was only entered in the eighth attribute to signal that seven is, in their view, a complete number, which is why they say «سبع في ثمانية», that is, seven cubits in eight spans; and the wāw indicates that because the wāw signals that what follows it differs from what precedes it, which is why it enters in the chapter of coordinating conjunction." I say: this is a very weak statement with no verification.

semin-durr:113-113.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَوْ كانوا أُوْلِي قربى}: like his saying «أَعْطوا السائلَ ولو على فرس» ("Give the beggar, even if he is on a horse"). What is in that has already preceded, and that it is a ḥāl conjoined to an implied ḥāl.

semin-durr:114-114.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَعَدَهَآ إِيَّاهُ}: there was disagreement over the nominative and the detached accusative pronouns. It was said, and this is the apparent sense: the nominative refers to Ibrāhīm and the accusative to his father, meaning that Ibrāhīm had promised his father that he would seek forgiveness for him. The reading of al-Ḥasan, Ḥammād al-Rāwiya, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ, Abū Nahīk and Muʿādh al-Qāriʾ «وعدها أباه» with the single-dotted bāʾ supports this. It was also said: the nominative is for the father of Ibrāhīm and the accusative for Ibrāhīm; and in the exegesis it is that he had promised Ibrāhīm that he would believe, and thereby he hoped for his faith.
«الأَوَّاه» is the one who often sighs (taʾawwuh), the one who says «أَوَّاه»; it was also said: the one who says «أوَّه», which is more fitting because «أَوَّهَ» is in the sense of "I feel pain", so «الأَوَّاه» is faʿʿāl, a pattern of intensification from that; and by analogy its verb ought to be triliteral, because patterns of intensification are regular only from the triliteral. Quṭrub reported its verb as triliteral, saying: one says آهَ يَؤُوه like قام يقوم, أَوْهاً. The grammarians rejected this statement of Quṭrub, saying that no triliteral verb is said from «أَوَّه» in the sense of pain; one says only أوَّه تأَوْيهاً and تَأَوَّه تَأَوُّهاً. The rajaz poet said:
2547 - فأَوَّه الراعي وضوضى أَكْلبُه
(The shepherd sighed and his dogs howled.)
and al-Muthaqqib al-ʿAbdī said:
2548 - إذا ما قُمْتُ أرْحَلُها بليلٍ ... تأوَّهُ آهَةَ الرجلِ الحزينِ
(Whenever I rise at night to saddle her, she groans the groan of a sorrowful man.)
al-Zamakhsharī said: «أَوَّاه» is faʿʿāl from «أَوَّه», like «لأَّل» from «اللؤلؤ», and it is the one who sighs often. The Shaykh said: "His likening «أوَّاه» from «أوَّه» to «لأَّل» from «اللؤلؤ» is not good, because the root of «أوَّه» is present in the form of «أواه», whereas the root of «لؤلؤ» is missing in «لأل» because of the difference in composition, since «لأل» is triliteral and «لؤلؤ» is quadriliteral, and the condition of derivation is agreement in the radical letters." I say: «لاَّل» and «لؤلؤ» are both from the repeated quadriliteral, that is: the root is lām and hamza, and then we repeated; the utmost in the matter is that two hamzas were joined in «لآَّل» so the first was assimilated into the other, and they were distinguished in «لؤلؤ».

semin-durr:117-117.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {اتبعوه}: two possibilities. One: that it is a real following, he, peace be upon him, having gone out first and his companions following him; and the other that it is figurative, that is: "they followed his command and prohibition". "The hour of hardship" is an expression for the time of going out to the expedition, and the real hour is not meant, but like their sayings "the day of al-Kulāb" and "the evening we fought Judhām"; so «الساعة» was borrowed for that, as «الغداة» and «العشية» were borrowed in his saying:
2549 - غَدَاةَ طَفَتْ عَلْماءِ بكرُ بنُ وائلٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The morning Bakr ibn Wāʾil rose over ʿAlmāʾ…)
[and his saying]:
2550 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... عشية قارَعْنا جُذَام وحميرا
(…the evening we fought Judhām and Ḥimyar.)
[and his saying]:
2551 - إذا جاء يوماً وارثي يبتغي الغنى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If my heir comes one day seeking wealth…)
His saying: {كَادَ يَزِيغُ}: Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read «يزيغ» with the yāʾ (below), and the rest with the tāʾ (above). The first reading admits that the subject of «كاد» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), with «قلوب» nominative by «يزيغ», and the clause in the position of the accusative as its khabar; or that its subject is the pronoun of the people, or the group which the mention of the Emigrants and Helpers indicates, and therefore Abū l-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya estimated: «من بعد كاد القوم». The Shaykh said of this reading: "It is necessary that «كاد» contain the pronoun of the matter and that «قلوب» be nominative by «يزيغ», because it is impossible for «قلوب» to be the subject of «كاد» and «يزيغ» to be in the place of the khabar, since the intention for it is postponement, and it is not permissible: «مِن بعد كاد قلوب يزيغ» with the yāʾ." I say: what he mentioned is not necessary in this reading, for what has preceded: that the subject of «كاد» may be a pronoun referring to the group or the people, with the verbal clause as its khabar, and there is no objection preventing that. His statement "because it is impossible for «قلوب» to be the subject of «كاد»" means that if we made «قلوب» the subject of «كاد», «يزيغ» would necessarily be a fronted khabar and so would necessarily govern a pronoun referring to «قلوب», and were that so the verb would necessarily be feminine, because it would then be predicated of a pronoun of a figurative feminine, as the broken plural is treated as feminine figuratively.
