As for the reading with the tāʾ (above), it admits that «كاد» contains the pronoun of the matter, as before, with «قلوب» nominative by «تزيغ», feminine because of the feminine plural; and that «قلوب» is its subject and «تزيغ» a fronted khabar, with no objection in that, since the verb has been made feminine. The Shaykh said: "On each of these three parsings there is a difficulty, according to what is established in the science of grammar, that the khabar of the verbs of approximation can only be an imperfect verb governing a pronoun of its subject; some stated this absolutely, and some restricted it to those other than «عسى» among the verbs of approximation; and it is not to be indirect (sababī), unlike «كان», whose khabar may govern the pronoun and the indirect element of the subject of «كان». So when we estimate the pronoun of the matter in it, the clause is in the position of the accusative as khabar, and the nominative is not a pronoun referring to the subject of «كاد», nor even indirect to it.
"This also applies in the tāʾ reading. As for the medial placement of the khabar, it is built on the permissibility of such a construction as «كان يقوم زيد», and there is disagreement in it, and the sound view is prohibition. As for the last possibility, it is very weak in that a pronoun is implied in «كاد» which has no referent except in imagination, and in that the khabar of «كاد» would govern an indirect element."
I say: how can he say "the sound view is prohibition" when this construction is present in the Qur'an, as in His saying, the Exalted, {مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 137] and {كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنَا} [al-Jinn: 4], and in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
2552 - وإن تَكُ قد ساءَتْكِ مني خَليقةٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(If some trait of mine has displeased you…)
This construction undoubtedly occurs; they only differed in its estimate: whether it is of the type of fronting the khabar or not. Whoever prevented it did so because it is like the chapter of mubtadaʾ and khabar, and a plain khabar, whenever it is so, cannot be fronted before the mubtadaʾ lest it be confused with the chapter of the agent, and so likewise after it is abrogated. Whoever allowed it did so for the safety from confusion.
Then the Shaykh said: "What rescues from these difficulties is believing that «كاد» is redundant, its meaning being intended, with no governing then of a subject or khabar, so it is like «كان» when added, its meaning intended and without governing. The reading of Ibn Masʿūd «من بعد ما زاغَتْ», omitting «كاد», supports this interpretation. The Kufans held its redundancy in His saying, the Exalted, {لَمْ يَكَدْ يَرَاهَا} [al-Nūr: 40], despite its being affected by a governor and governing what follows; so it is more fitting to claim its redundancy when it is neither governing nor governed." I say: the majority rejected its redundancy, and among the Basrans al-Akhfash held it, and made from it {أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا} [Ṭā Hā: 15]. The discussion of that has preceded at the beginning of this book.
al-Aʿmash and al-Jaḥdarī read «تُزيغ» with a ḍamma on the tāʾ, as if he made «أزاغ» and «زاغ» the same in meaning. Ubayy read «كادَتْ» with the feminine tāʾ.

semin-durr:118-118.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَعَلَى الثلاثة}: it may be conjoined to «النبيّ», that is: "He turned in mercy to the Prophet and to the three"; and it may be conjoined to the pronoun in «عليهم», that is: "then He turned to them and to the three", and therefore the preposition is repeated.
The majority of people read «خُلِّفوا», passive, doubled, from «خلَّفه يُخَلِّفه». Abū Mālik read likewise except that he lightened the lām. ʿIkrima, Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, ʿUmar ibn ʿUbayd, ʿIkrima ibn Hārūn al-Makhzūmī and Muʿādh al-Qāriʾ read «خَلَفوا», active, light, from «خَلَفَه», the meaning being "those who became corrupt", from «خُلوف فم الصائم». The meaning may be that they stayed behind the fighters in Medina. Abū l-ʿĀliya and Abū l-Jawzāʾ read likewise except that they doubled the lām. Abū Razīn, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and his two sons Zayd and Muḥammad al-Bāqir and his son Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq read «خالفوا», with an alif, that is: they did not go along with the fighters in going out. al-Bāqir said: "Had they been left behind, it would not have been theirs." «الظن» here is in the sense of knowledge, as in the saying:
2553 - فقلتُ لهم ظُنُّوا بأَلْفَي مُدَجَّجٍ ... سَرَاتُهمُ كالفارِسي المُسَرَّدِ
(So I said to them: think of two thousand armoured men, whose leaders are like the Persian mail-coat strung together.)
It was also said: it is in its basic sense.
His saying: {أَن لاَّ مَلْجَأَ}: «أنْ» is the lightened one, standing in place of the two objects, «لا» and what is in its scope is the khabar, and «من الله» is its khabar. It cannot be attached to «مَلْجَأ» with «إلا إليه» as the khabar, because then it would have to be declined (given tanwīn), since it would be an extended noun. Some said it is permissible to liken the extended noun to the muḍāf, so that its tanwīn and nūn are removed, as in the saying:
2554 - أراني ولا كفرانَ لله أيَّةً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I see myself, and there is no ingratitude to Allah, a sign…)
and the saying «لا صَمْتَ يومٌ إلى الليل» with «يوم» nominative; the discussion of that has preceded. His saying «إلا إليه» is an exception from that omitted general term, that is: "there is no refuge to anyone except to Him", like «لا إله إلا الله».

semin-durr:120-120.t:
«الظَّمأُ» is thirst. One says: ظَمِىء يَظْمَأُ ظَمَأً, so he is ظمآنُ and she is ظمأى. It has two forms: the short and the lengthened; ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read with the lengthened form, like سَفِه سَفاهاً. «الظِّمْءُ» is the interval between two drinkings.
«مَوْطِئاً» is mafʿil from «وَطِىءَ». It may be a maṣdar in the sense of «الوَطْء», or a place. The first is clearer, because the agent of «يغيظ» refers to it without interpretation, unlike its being a place, in which case it refers to the maṣdar, which is «الوَطْءُ» indicated by «المَوْطِىءُ».
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُغيظ» with a ḍamma on the yāʾ; they are two forms: غاظَه and أغاظه.
«النَّيْلُ» is a maṣdar; it may be in its basic sense, and may stand in the place of the direct object. Its yāʾ is not a substitute for a wāw as some claimed, but «ناله ينولُه» is another root and another meaning, which is handing over (munāwala); one says نِلْتُه أَنُوْله, that is, "I took it in hand" (تناولته); and نِلْتُه أنيله, that is, "I attained it".

semin-durr:121-121.t:
«الوادي»: al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الوادي» is every opening between mountains and hillocks that serves as a channel for the torrent; in origin it is fāʿil from «ودى» when it flows, and from it «الوَدِيّ»; it became widespread in the usage of the Arabs in the sense of land." It is pluralised as «أودية», which is not by analogy; its analogy would be «الأَوادي», like «أَواصل» as the plural of «واصل», the original being «وَوَاصِل», the first wāw being changed to hamza. al-Naḥḥās said: "I know no fāʿil and afʿila other than it." This was supplemented against him, and they added «نادٍ» and «أندية», reciting:
2555 - وفيهم مقاماتٌ حِسانٌ وجوهُهمْ ... وأنديةٌ ينتابها القولُ والفعلُ
(Among them are assemblies with handsome faces, and gathering-places frequented by word and deed.)
«النادي» is the assembly. al-Farrāʾ said that it is pluralised as «أَوْداء», like «صاحب» and «أصحاب», and recited for Jarīr:
2556 - عَرَفْتُ ببُرْقَةِ الأَوْداءِ رَسْماً ... مُحيلاً طال عهدُكَ مِنْ رسومِ
(At the stony ground of the valleys I recognised a trace, effaced, long since you knew such traces.)
I say: al-Rāghib added to fāʿil and afʿila: «ناجٍ» and «أنْجِيَة», so three words are complete in fāʿil and afʿila. One says «وَدَاه», that is, "he destroyed him", as if they conceived of it as making blood flow; and «الدِّيَة» (blood money) was called diya because it is in return for the flowing of blood; and from it «الوَدْيُ», which is the male's fluid during play and the water that comes out with urine; and «الوَدِيُّ» with a kasra on the dāl and shadda on the yāʾ is the young palm trees.
His saying: {ذلك بِأَنَّهُمْ} [al-Tawba: 120]: mubtadaʾ and khabar; the reference by it is to what is contained in the negation of staying behind, namely the obligation to go out with him.
His saying: {إِلاَّ كُتِبَ}: this clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from «ظَمَأ» and what is conjoined to it, that is: "no thirst befalls them without being written". The pronoun in «به» is singular although things precede it, treating it like a demonstrative, that is: "a righteous deed was written for them thereby". The pronoun may refer back to the preceding righteous deed, and it may refer to one of the two maṣdars understood from «ينفقون» and «يقطعون», that is: "without being written for them through spending or through crossing".
His saying: {لِيَجْزِيَهُمُ}: attached to «كُتِب». In this clause there is eloquence and rhetorical beauty not hidden from whoever reflects on it, especially one trained by what has preceded in this work.

semin-durr:122-122.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَوْلاَ نَفَرَ مِن كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ}: «لولا» is of urging (taḥḍīḍ), and what is meant is the command. «منهم» may be an adjective of «فرقة» and may be a ḥāl from «طائفة», because in origin it is an adjective of it; on both estimates it is attached to an omitted element. What ought to be said is that «من كل فرقة» is a ḥāl from «طائفة», and «منهم» is an adjective of «فرقة»; and «من كل» may be attached to «نَفَرَ».
His saying: {لِّيَتَفَقَّهُواْ}: there are two views regarding this pronoun. One: that it is for the group that goes out, on the basis that what is meant by going out is going out to seek knowledge, which is the apparent sense. It was also said: the pronoun in «ليتفَّقهوا» refers to the group that stays, and that in «رَجَعوا» to the group that goes out, what is meant by going out being going out to jihad; the meaning is that when those who go out to fight depart, their brothers remain learning jurisprudence from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when the fighters return, the teachers warn them, that is, teach them jurisprudence and the law.

semin-durr:123-123.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلِيَجِدُواْ}: it is of the type of «لا أُرَيَنَّك ههنا» ("let me not see you here"), and its explanation has preceded.
His saying: {غِلْظَةً}: the majority read it with a kasra, which is the stronger dialect. al-Aʿmash, Abān ibn Taghlib and al-Mufaḍḍal, both from ʿĀṣim, read «غَلْظة» with a fatḥa, which is the dialect of the Hijaz. Abū Ḥaywa, al-Sulamī, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and al-Mufaḍḍal and Abān in a report from them, read «غُلظة» with a ḍamma, which is the dialect of Tamīm. Abū ʿAmr reported the three dialects. «الغِلظة» in origin applies to bodies, and was borrowed here for severity, endurance and fortitude.

semin-durr:124-124.t: His saying, the Exalted: {زَادَتْهُ}: the majority have «أيُكم» nominative as a mubtadaʾ with what follows as khabar. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read it accusative by ishtighāl, but the verb is estimated postponed after it because it has the heading of the speech; and accusative, according to al-Akhfash, in this type is better than nominative, because he treats the interrogative noun like nouns preceded by an interrogative particle such as «أزيداً ضربته» in preferring the implied verb.

semin-durr:126-126.t: His saying, the Exalted: {أَوَلاَ يَرَوْنَ}: Ḥamza read «ترون» with the tāʾ of address, which is an address to those who believed, and the rest with the yāʾ of the third person, referring back to {الذين فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ}. The seeing here may be of the heart or of the eye.

semin-durr:127-127.t: His saying, the Exalted: {هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ}: in the position of the accusative by an implied saying, that is: «يقولون: هل يراكم». The clause of the saying is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and «مِنْ أحد» is the agent.

semin-durr:128-128.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ}: an adjective of «رسول», that is: from the purest of the Arabs. Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū l-ʿĀliya, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Maḥbūb from Abū ʿAmr, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qusayṭ al-Makkī, and Yaʿqūb in some of his chains read — and it is the reading of the Messenger of Allah, Fāṭima and ʿĀʾisha — with a fatḥa on the fāʾ, that is: "from the most noble of you", from «النَّفاسة» (preciousness).
His saying: {عَزِيزٌ}: there are several possibilities in it. One: that «عزيز» is an adjective of «رسول»; against which it is that something other than a plain adjective is placed before the plain adjective, and it may be answered that «من أنفسكم» is attached to «جاء», and «ما» may be a maṣdar-forming particle or in the sense of «الذي»; on both estimates it is the agent of «عزيز», that is: "your distress is grievous to him" or "that which you suffer is grievous to him", that is, their distress pains him, so the ʿāʾid is omitted by gradation; this is like the saying:
2557 - يَسُرُّ المرءَ ما ذهب الليالي ... وكان ذهابُهنَّ له ذهاباً
(A man is pleased by the passing of the nights, though their passing is a passing for him.)
that is, "the passing of the nights pleases him". «عزيز» may also be a fronted khabar, with «ما عَنِتُّم» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause an adjective of «رسول». al-Ḥawfī allowed that «عزيز» be a mubtadaʾ with «ما عنتُّم» as its khabar, and in it is beginning with an indefinite noun because of its governing the prepositional phrase after it. The meaning of «العنت» has preceded. The more probable is that «عزيز» is an adjective of «رسول»; because of His saying after it «حريصٌ», so it is not made a khabar for anything else, and the claim that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is «هو حريصٌ», has no need.
«بالمؤمنين» is attached to «رؤوف». It is not permissible for the matter to be one of tanāzuʿ (competition of governors), because one of its conditions is that the governed term come after the two governors, even though some have differed and allowed «زيداً ضربتُ وشتمته» on the basis of tanāzuʿ; and if we build on this weaker view, it would be a case of the second governor acting, not the first, as is known: whenever the first acts, a pronoun is implied in the second without omission.

semin-durr:129-129.t: The majority have a kasra on the mīm of «العظيم», as an adjective of «العرش». Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with a ḍamma, making it an adjective of «الرب», and this was also reported as a reading from Ibn Kathīr. Abū Bakr al-Aṣamm said: "This reading is more pleasing to me, because making «العظيم» an attribute of Allah, the Exalted, is better than making it an attribute of the Throne."

semin-durr:1-1.t:
The majority read «براءة» in the nominative, with two views. The first is that it is nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is His saying «إلى الذين». The mubtadaʾ may be an indefinite because it has been specified by the description of the preposition and its genitive noun after it. The second is that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "these verses are a repudiation (barāʾa)." «من الله» may be attached to «براءة» itself, because it is a maṣdar, and this root takes «مِنْ»: you say baritʾtu min fulān abraʾu barāʾatan, that is: the tie between us was cut. On this basis, this may be the justification for the indefinite as mubtadaʾ in the first view. «إلى الذين» is attached to an omitted word on the first view, since it falls as the khabar, and to «براءة» itself on the second. One says baritʾtu and baraʾtu min al-dayn, with kasra and fatḥa. Al-Wāḥidī said: "There is in it only one dialect: kasra on the ʿayn in the past and fatḥa in the future," but it is not so; the lexicographers reported both.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «براءةً» in the accusative by an implied verb, that is: "hear a repudiation." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "That is: hold fast to a repudiation, and it has the sense of incitement (ighrāʾ)."
«مِنِ الله» was also read, with kasra on the nūn of «مِنْ», either on the basis of the original meeting of two sākins, or by following the mīm of «مِنْ»; it is a minor dialect, for the more frequent is fatḥa with the lām of definiteness and kasra with others, as in «مِنِ ابنك», and the matter is sometimes reversed in both. Abū ʿAmr reported from the people of Najrān that they read so, with kasra on the nūn before the lām of definiteness.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَسِيحُواْ}: This is on an implied saying, that is: "it was said: travel freely." It is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to address. One says sāḥa yasīḥu siyāḥatan, suyūḥan and sayaḥānan, that is: it flowed, like the flow of water in level places. Ṭarafa said:
2447 - لو خِفْتُ هذا منك ما نِلْتَني ... حتى ترى خيلاً أمامي تَسِيحْ
(Had I feared this from you, you would not have reached me until you saw horses streaming before me.)
«أربعةَ أشهرٍ» is an adverbial of «سِيْحوا». {غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِي الله} was also read with the divine Name in the accusative, on the basis that the nūn was omitted for lightness. Its treatment has already been given.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَذَانٌ}: nominative as mubtadaʾ; «مِن الله» is either its adjective or attached to it, and «إلى الناس» is the khabar. It may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "and this is an announcement," the two prepositional phrases being attached to it, as given earlier in «براءة». The Shaykh said: "There is no ground for the saying of whoever said that it is conjoined to «براءة», just as one does not say «عمرو» is conjoined to «زيد» in «زيد قائم وعمرو قاعد»." [Translator's note: the source has «وهو [كما قال]، وهذه عبارة [الزمخشري بعينها]» with bracketed words, apparently editorial insertions, meaning "and it is as he said, and this is al-Zamakhsharī's very wording."] Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿIkrima and Abū l-Mutawakkil read «وإذْن» with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the dhāl. The majority read «أنَّ الله» with fatḥa on the hamza, in one of two ways: either it is the khabar of «أذان», that is: "the announcement from Allah is His repudiation of the polytheists" — the Shaykh weakened this view but did not state his weakening — or it is on the omission of the preposition, that is: «بأن الله». This preposition and its genitive noun is attached either to the maṣdar itself or to an omitted word as its adjective. «يومَ» is accusative by what the preposition and its genitive noun in «إلى الناس» are attached to. Some claimed that it is accusative by «أذانٌ», but this is invalid for two reasons: one, describing the maṣdar before it has acted; the other, separating it from what it governs by an outsider, which is the khabar.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj read with kasra on the hamza, which admits the two well-known schools: the school of the Basrans is the implication of a saying, and the school of the Kufans is treating the announcement (adhān) as the equivalent of a saying.
His saying: {مِّنَ المشركين} is attached to «بريء» itself, as one says "I am free of him" (bariʾtu minhu), unlike {بَرَآءَةٌ مِّنَ الله} [al-Tawba: 1], where it admits this and also admits being an adjective of «براءة».
His saying: {وَرَسُولِهِ}: The majority read it in the nominative, with three views. The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, that is: "and His Messenger is free of them," omitted because it is indicated. The second: that it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in the khabar, and this is allowed because of the separation that justifies conjunction, so its nominative is as agent on this view. The third: that it is conjoined to the position of the ism of «أنَّ», according to those who allow that with the fatḥa form by analogy with the kasra form. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The school of the Ustadh, meaning Ibn al-Bādhish, in accord with Sībawayh's words, is that what «أنَّ» enters upon has no position, since it is declined and the effect of the governor has appeared in it, and that there is no difference between «أَنَّ» and «ليت», and the consensus is that what these enter upon has no position." The Shaykh said: "There is a rejoinder to it, because the reason for «أنَّ» having no position for what it enters upon is not the appearance of the governor's effect, as shown by «ليس زيد بقائم» and «ما في الدار مِنْ رجل», in which the effect of the governor appears and both have a position; and his saying 'by consensus', meaning that there is no position for what «ليت» enters upon by consensus, is not so, because al-Farrāʾ disagreed and made the ruling for «ليت» and all its sisters the ruling of kasra «إنَّ»."
I say: his statement "as shown by «ليس زيدٌ بقائم»" and so on — the difference between them may be apparent, for this governor, although its effect appears, is in the ruling of the non-existent, since it is redundant; that is why we take the position into account with it, unlike «أنَّ» with fatḥa, which is a non-redundant governor. His statement "there is no difference between «أنَّ» and «ليت»" should have been rebutted, for the difference stands: the ruling of the mubtadaʾ has been abrogated with «ليت», «لعل» and «كأن», in form and meaning, unlike with «إنَّ» and «أنَّ», with which its meaning remains.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «ورسولَه» in the accusative, with two views, the more apparent being that it is conjoined to the divine Name; the second, that it is mafʿūl maʿahu, as al-Zamakhsharī said. Al-Ḥasan read «ورسولِه» in the genitive, with two views: one, that it is an oath-object, that is: "by His Messenger, the matter is so," its answer being omitted for the meaning to be understood; the second, that it is by adjacency (jiwār), as they made adjectives and emphatics follow by adjacency, whose treatment has already been given. This reading is unlikely to be sound from al-Ḥasan, because of the ambiguity, so that it is reported that a Bedouin heard a man read «ورسولِه» in the genitive. The Bedouin said: "If Allah has disowned His Messenger, then I disown him," and the reciter seized him and took him to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him; the Bedouin related the incident, and then ʿUmar ordered that Arabic be taught. This is also reported of the Commander of the Faithful ʿAlī and of Abū l-Aswad al-Duʾalī. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It cannot be conjoined to «المشركين», because that would lead to disbelief." This is among the obvious points.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ الذين}: There are three views. The first is that it is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). The implied form is: "but those with whom you made a covenant, fulfil their covenant to them." Al-Zamakhsharī took this course, saying: "If you ask: from what is His saying {إِلاَّ الذين عَاهَدتُّم} excepted? I say: its aspect is that it is excepted from His saying {فَسِيحُواْ فِي الأرض}, since the speech is addressed to the Muslims, and its meaning is: a repudiation from Allah and His Messenger to those polytheists with whom you made a covenant, so say to them: travel freely, except those of them with whom you made a covenant and who then did not diminish you, so fulfil their covenant to them. The exception has the meaning of rectification (istidrāk), as if it were said, after they were commanded about the covenant-breakers: but those who did not break, fulfil their covenant to them and do not treat them as the others."
The second: that it is a continuous exception (muttaṣil), preceded by an omitted sentence whose implied form is: "kill the polytheists who have covenants, except those with whom you made a covenant." There is weakness in it.
The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is His saying «فأتمُّوا إليهم»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. There is something to consider in it, because the fāʾ is added where it does not belong, since the mubtadaʾ does not resemble a condition, for it refers to specific people; it can proceed only on the view of al-Akhfash, who allows its addition without restriction. The preferable view is that it is discontinuous, for if we made it continuous, excepted from the polytheists at the beginning of the sūra, it would lead to separation between the excepted and that from which it is excepted by many sentences.
His saying: {ثُمَّ لَمْ يَنقُصُوكُمْ شَيْئاً}: The majority read «يَنْقُصوكم» with the undotted ṣād, which takes one object or two. Both are possible here: «كُمْ» is an object and «شيئاً» is either a second object or a maṣdar, that is: "anything of diminution," or "neither little nor much of diminution." ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib al-Kūfī, ʿIkrima, Ibn al-Samayfaʿ and Abū Zayd read «يَنْقُضوكم» with the dotted ḍād, which is on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: "break your covenant," the muḍāf being omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. Al-Kirmānī said: "It fits the mention of the covenant," that is: breaking matches the covenant. It is close to the reading of the majority, for whoever breaks the covenant has diminished the term; but the reading of the majority is more apt because of its contrast with completion.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الأشهر}: The alif-lām may be one of reference (ʿahd), the months meant being those mentioned earlier in His saying {فَسِيحُواْ فِي الأرض أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ}. When the Arabs mention an indefinite and then wish to mention it a second time, they bring its pronoun or its word defined by «أل», and it is not permissible then to describe it by a description suggesting difference. If it were said «رأيت رجلاً فأكرَمْتُ الرجلَ الطويل» ("I saw a man and honoured the tall man"), you would not mean by the second the first; but if you describe it with what does not imply difference, it is allowed, as in your saying «فأكرمت الرجل المذكور» ("I honoured the man mentioned"). This verse is of that kind, for «الأشهر» has been described as sacred (ḥurum), which is a description understood from the drift of the speech, so it does not imply difference. It may also be that something other than the months mentioned earlier is meant, in which case «أل» is not for reference; both views are reported in the exegesis.
The "stripping off" (insilākh) here is among the finest metaphors, and Abū l-Haytham explained it, saying: "One says «أَهْلَلْنا شهرَ كذا», that is: we entered it; each night of it, until half of it has passed, we increase in garment, then we strip it off ourselves piece by piece until it ends and is stripped away." And he recited:
2448 - إذا ما سَلَخْتُ الشهرَ أَهْلَلْتُ مثلَه ... كفى قاتِلاً سَلْخي الشهورَ وإهلالي
(When I have stripped away a month I enter another like it; my stripping away months and entering them suffices as a killer.)
His saying: {كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍ}: There are two views on its being accusative. The first is that it is accusative as an adverbial of place. Al-Zajjāj said: "like «ذهبت مذهباً»." Al-Fārisī rejected this view of his, because it is a specific adverbial of place, and a specific place is not reached by the verb directly but by means of «في», as in «صَلَّيْتُ في الطريق» and «في البيت»; it is reached directly only in a limited set of words, some of which are regular and some only heard. He made this a parallel to what Sībawayh did in the verse of Sāʿida:
2449 - لَدْنٌ بهَزِّ الكفِّ يَعْسِلُ مَتْنُهُ ... فيه كما عَسَل الطريقَ الثعلبُ
(Supple when the hand shakes it, its shaft quivering in it as the fox runs along the road.)
namely that he made it one from which the preposition was omitted by latitude, not an adverbial, because it is a specific adverbial of place.
The Shaykh said: "It is accusative as an adverbial, because the meaning of «واقعدوا» is not literally to sit, but rather: lie in wait for them. If so, the governing word and the adverbial agree in root, and whenever they agree in root, in form or meaning, the verb reaches it directly. You say «جلست مجلسَ القاضي» and «قعدت مجلسَ القاضي», and the verse is of that kind."
The second is that it is accusative by the omission of the preposition, which is «على», that is: «على كلِّ مَرْصَد». This is the view of al-Akhfash, who made it like the saying of the other:
2450 - تَحِنُّ فَتُبْدِي ما بها مِنْ صَبابةٍ ... وأُخْفي الذي لولا الأسى لقَضَاني
(She yearns and shows what she has of passion, and I conceal what, but for grief, would have killed me.)
This is not regular but limited to what has been heard, as in the saying of the Exalted: {لأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ}, that is: «على صراطك»; all agreed that it is on the supposition of «على». Some said it is on the supposition of the bāʾ, that is: «بكل مرصد»; Abū l-Baqāʾ reported it. In that case the bāʾ would have the meaning of «في», so «في» should be supplied, because the meaning rests on it; and he made it parallel to the poet's saying:
2451 - نُغالي اللحمَ للأضيافِ نَيْئاً ... ونَرْخُصُهُ إذا نَضِجَ القدورُ
(We prize the meat for the guests when raw, and sell it cheap once the pots have cooked.)
Al-marṣad is of the pattern mafʿal, from raṣadahu yarṣuduhu, that is: he watched him; it suits time, place and maṣdar. ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl said:
2452 - ولقد عَلِمْتَ وما إِخالك ناسِيا ... أنَّ المنيَّةَ للفتى بالمَرْصَدِ
(You know — and I do not think you forget — that death lies in wait for the young man.)
Al-mirṣād is the place specific to lying in wait. Al-marṣad applies to the one who watches, whether singular, dual or plural, and likewise to the one watched. His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَداً} [al-Jinn: 27] can bear all that; it is as if it were originally a maṣdar, hence the singular and masculine is kept in it.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنْ أَحَدٌ}: Like His saying {إِن امرؤ هَلَكَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 176], in that it belongs to the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation) according to the majority.
His saying: {حتى يَسْمَعَ}: «حتى» may here be for the limit (ghāya) or for causation (taʿlīl), and on both views it is attached to His saying «فَأَجِرْهُ». Can this issue be an instance of conflict of governors (tanāzuʿ) or not? There is obscurity in it: in meaning it is possible to attach «حتى» to His saying «استجارك» or to «فَأَجِرْهُ», since the implied form could be: "and if anyone seeks your protection until he hears the speech of Allah, protect him until he hears the speech of Allah." The answer is that it is not allowed according to the majority, for a verbal reason of the craft, not a reason of meaning: if we made it a case of tanāzuʿ and gave the operation to the first, say, the second would need it as a pronoun, as established; then it would follow that «حتى» governs the pronoun in the genitive, and «حتى» governs it only in poetic necessity, as in the saying:
2453 - فلا واللَّهِ لا يَلْقَى أُناسٌ ... فتى حَتَّاك يا ابنَ أبي يزيدِ
(No, by Allah, no people will find a youth up to you [ḥattāka], O son of Abū Yazīd.)
As for the one who allows it to govern a pronoun, it is not barred for him, and it would be the operation of the second, by omission of it, like your saying «فرحت ومررت بزيد», that is: «فرحت به»; had it been the operation of the first, you would not omit it from the second.
His saying {كَلاَمَ الله} is of the chapter of annexing the attribute to what it describes, not of annexing the created to the Creator. «مَأْمَنَه» may be a place, that is: the place of his safety, or a maṣdar, that is: "then convey him to his safety."

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَيْفَ يَكُونُ}: There are three views on the khabar of «يكون», the most apparent being that it is «كيف» and «عهدٌ» is its ism; the khabar here must be placed first because it contains what has the head of the sentence, namely the interrogative. On this view «للمشركين» is attached either to «يكون», according to those who allow «كان» to govern an adverbial and its like, or to an omitted word, because it was originally an adjective of «عهد», and when fronted it was made accusative as a ḥāl. «عند» may be attached to «يكون», or to an omitted word as an adjective of «عَهْد», or to «عهد» itself, since it is a maṣdar. The second: that the khabar is «للمشركين»; on this «عند» has the views given earlier. We add a fourth view, that it may be an adverbial of the being-established to which «للمشركين» is attached. The third: that the khabar is «عند الله»; on this «للمشركين» is either an explanation, or attached to «يكون» according to those who allow that as above, or a ḥāl from «عهد», or attached to the being-established to which the khabar is attached. No heed is paid to the fronting of the khabar's object before the ism since it is a preposition. «كيف» on the last two views resembles an adverbial or a ḥāl, as already treated at {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [al-Baqara: 28].
They did not mention a fourth view here, which should have been the most apparent: that "being" is complete (tāmma), meaning: "how can a covenant exist for the polytheists with Allah?" The interrogative here has the meaning of negation, and for that reason the exception with «إلا» follows it. Also from its use in the sense of negation is his saying:
2454 - فهذي سيوفٌ يا صُدَيُّ بنَ مالكٍ ... كثيرٌ ولكن كيف بالسيفِ ضاربُ
(These are swords, O Ṣudayy ibn Mālik, many, but how [is there] one to strike with the sword?)
that is: there is no one striking with the sword.
His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين عَاهَدْتُمْ}: There are two views. The first is that it is a discontinuous exception, that is: "but those with whom you made a covenant, their ruling is thus and thus." The second is that it is continuous, and there are then two possibilities: one, that it is accusative on the basis of the exception from the polytheists; the other, that it is genitive as a badal from them, because the meaning of the preceding interrogative is negation, that is: "there is not for the polytheists a covenant except for those who did not break it." By analogy with Abū l-Baqāʾ's statement earlier, it would be nominative as mubtadaʾ, the sentence «فما استقاموا» being its khabar.
His saying: {فَمَا}: «ما» may be a maṣdar particle of time, in the position of accusative, that is: "so be upright to them for the duration of their uprightness to you." It may be conditional, and then there are two views on its position. One: that it is accusative as an adverbial of time, the implied form being: "at whatever time they are upright to you, be upright to them." Abū l-Baqāʾ compared it to the saying of the Exalted: {مَّا يَفْتَحِ الله لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحْمَةٍ فَلاَ مُمْسِكَ لَهَا} [Fāṭir: 2]. The second: that it is nominative as mubtadaʾ, with the well-known views on the khabar, and «فاستقيموا» is the apodosis. Al-Ḥūfī took this course, and it requires the omission of a returning pronoun, that is: "at whatever time they are upright to you in it, be upright to them." The Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik allowed that the maṣdar «ما» of time may be a conditional jussive-governing one, and recited on it:
2455 - فما تَحْيَ لا نسْأَمْ حياةً وإن تَمُتْ ... فلا خيرَ في الدنيا ولا العيشِ أجمعا
(As long as you live we will not tire of life; and if you die, there is no good in the world or in life at all.)
There is no proof in it, because the apparent sense is conditional without interpreting it as maṣdar and time. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It cannot be negative, for the meaning would be corrupted, since the meaning would become: 'be upright to them because they were not upright to you.'"

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَيْفَ وَإِن يَظْهَرُوا}: The thing asked about is omitted, as the meaning indicates it. Abū l-Baqāʾ supplied: "how can you feel secure," or "how can they have a covenant." Others supplied: "how do you not fight them." The second of Abū l-Baqāʾ's two suppositions is better, because it is of the kind of what came before, so the indication of it is stronger. Omission has often occurred in this construction, and there came earlier His saying, the Exalted: {فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 25] and {فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا} [al-Nisāʾ: 41]. The poet said:
2456 - وخبَّرْ تُماني أنَّما الموتُ بالقُرى ... فكيف وهاتا هَضْبةٌ وكَثِيبُ
(You two told me that death is in the villages; how then, when here are a hill and a dune?)
that is: "how did he die?" And al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
2457 - فكيف ولم أعلَمْهُمُ خَذَلُوكُمْ ... على مُعْظِمٍ ولا أَدِيْمَكُمُ قَدُّوا
(How [can you blame me], when I did not know them to have forsaken you in a grave matter, nor to have cut your hide?)
that is: "how do you blame me for praising them?" The Shaykh said: "Abū l-Baqāʾ supplied the verb after «كيف» as «كيف تطمئنون», and another supplied it as «كيف لا تقاتِلونهم»." I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ did not supply it with this alone, but with it and the preferred view, as I presented from him earlier.
His saying: {وَإِن يَظْهَرُوا}: This conditional sentence is in the position of accusative as ḥāl, that is: "how can they have a covenant when they are in a state contrary to that?" Its treatment was given at His saying {وَإِن يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ مِّثْلُهُ يَأْخُذُوهُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 169]. «لا يرقُبوا» is the apodosis of the condition. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «وإن يُظْهَروا» in the passive, from aẓharahu ʿalayhi, that is: He made him prevail over him.
His saying: {إِلاًّ} is the direct object of «يرقُبوا», that is: "they do not observe." About «الإِلّ» the lexicographers have several views. The first: that the covenant is meant. Abū ʿUbayda, Ibn Zayd and al-Suddī said so, and from it comes the poet's saying:
2458 - لولا بنو مالكٍ والإِلُّ مَرْقَبَةٌ ... ومالكٌ فيهمُ الآلاءُ والشَّرَفُ
(Were it not for the sons of Mālik, and the covenant is a watchtower, and Mālik, in whom are the favours and the honour.)
that is: the alliance. Another said:
2459 - وجَدْناهُما كاذِباً إِلُّهُمْ ... وذو الإِلِّ والعهدِ لا يَكْذِبُ
(We found their covenant false, whereas a man of covenant and pledge does not lie.)
and another said:
2460 - أفسدَ الناسَ خُلوفٌ خَلَفُوا ... قطعُوا الإِلَّ وأعراقَ الرَّحِمْ
(The people were corrupted by successors who came after, who cut the covenant and the roots of kinship.)
In the ḥadīth of Umm Zarʿ: «بيت أبي زرع وَفِيُّ الإِلِّ، كريم الخِلّ، بَرودُ الظلّ» ("The house of Abū Zarʿ is faithful to the covenant, generous to the friend, cool in shade"), that is: faithful to the covenant.
The second: that kinship is meant, which is al-Farrāʾ's view, and he recited the verse of Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him:
2461 - لَعَمْرك إنَّ إِلَّكَ مِنْ قريشٍ ... كإِلِّ السَّقْبِ مِنْ رَأْلِ النَّعامِ
(By your life, your kinship to Quraysh is like the kinship of the camel-foal to the ostrich chick.)
Abū ʿUbayda recited on that the saying:
2462 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... قطعوا الإِلَّ وأعراق الرَّحِمْ
(... they cut kinship and the roots of the womb.)
The third: that Allah the Exalted is meant, that is: it is one of His names, and they cited as evidence the ḥadīth of Abū Bakr when the speech of Musaylima, may Allah curse him, was presented to him: «إنَّ هذا الكلام لم يَخْرج من إلّ» ("This speech did not come from an Ill"), that is, Allah, mighty and exalted. Al-Zajjāj did not accept this, saying: "Because His names, the Exalted, are known in the Book and the Sunna, and no one has been heard to say: 'O Ill, do such-and-such for me.'"
The fourth: that al-ill is the jūʾār, which is the raising of the voice at the making of a pact, because when they wiped hands and swore pacts they cried out loudly about it; from it is the saying of Abū Jahl:
2463 - لإِلٍّ علينا واجبٍ لا نُضِيعُه ... متينٍ قُواه غيرِ منتكثِ الحبلِ
(For a pledge incumbent upon us which we will not waste, its strands firm, its rope unbroken.)
The fifth: that it is from «ألَّ البرقُ», that is, it flashed. Al-Azharī said: "Al-alīl is the gleam; one says alla yaullu, that is: it was clear and shone." It was also said that al-ill is from sharpening, and from it comes al-alla, the spear, because of its sharpness. Some set between these meanings a common measure to which all I have mentioned to you returns. Al-Zajjāj said: "The reality of al-ill, in my view, as the language indicates, is the sharpening of a thing. From that: al-alla, the spear, and uzun muʾallala (a pointed ear); al-ill extends over everything explained of covenant, kinship and jūʾār from this, so if you say of a covenant «بينهما إلٌّ», its sense is that they have sharpened [their resolve] in taking covenants, and likewise for jūʾār and kinship." Al-Rāghib said: "Al-ill: every apparent state of covenant, alliance and kinship that gleams (taillu); alla al-faras: the horse sped; al-alla: the gleaming spear." Another recited on that the saying of Ḥimās ibn Qays on the day of the conquest of Mecca:
2464 - إن يُقْبلوا اليومَ فما لي عِلَّةْ ... هذا سلاحٌ كاملٌ وأَلَّةْ
وذو غِرارَيْنِ سَريعُ السَّلَّةُ
(If they come on today, I have no excuse: here is complete armour and a spear, and a double-edged sword quick to draw.)
He said: "It was said that al-ill and al-īl are two names of Allah the Exalted, but that is not correct; and the two alalān are the two sides of the knife." End of quotation. The plural of al-ill in the small number is allun, the original being aʾlul on the pattern afʿul (like aflus); the second hamza was replaced by alif because it is sākin after another with fatḥa, and the lām was assimilated into the lām. In the large number it is ilāl, like dhiʾb and dhiʾāb. Al-all with fatḥa was said to be extreme despair. Al-Harawī said, on the ḥadīth «عَجب ربكم مِنْ ألِّكم وقُنوطكم» ("Your Lord marvelled at your all and your despair"), Abū ʿUbayd said: "The ḥadīth scholars say it with kasra on the hamza, but what is preserved with us is the fatḥa, and it is more like the maṣdars, as if He meant 'at the intensity of your despair.' It may be from raising the voice; one says alla yaullu allan, alalan and alīlan, when he raised his voice in weeping, and from it one says: 'to him belong woe and alīl,' and from it is the saying of al-Kumayt:
2465 - وأنتَ ما أنت في غَبْراءَ مُظْلمةٍ ... إذا دَعَتْ أَلَلَيْها الكاعِبُ الفُضُلُ
(And you, what are you, in a dusty, dark [year], when the plump girl calls out her cries?)
End of quotation. A group read «ألاًّ» with fatḥa, and it is as he mentioned, a maṣdar of alla yaullu, when he made a covenant. ʿIkrima read «إيلاً» with kasra on the hamza followed by a sākin yāʾ, with three views. The first: that it is a name of Allah the Exalted; what was said earlier of Jibrīl and Isrāʾīl supports that, that the meaning is "servant of Allah." The second: that it may be derived from āla yaʾūlu when it came to the end of the matter, or from āla yaʾūlu when he managed, as Ibn Jinnī said, that is: "they do not observe in you management or conciliation." On both suppositions the wāw became sākin after a kasra and was turned into yāʾ, like rīḥ. The third: that it is the doubled al-ill, but the doubling was found heavy and one of the two was replaced by a weak letter, as they say amlaytu l-kitāb and amlaltuhu. The poet said:
2466 - يا ليتَما أمُّنا شالَتْ نَعَمَتُها ... أَيْما إلى جنةٍ أَيْما إلى نارِ
(Would that our mother had had her ostrich-hen lifted, either to a garden or to a fire.)
His saying: {وَلاَ ذِمَّةً}: Al-dhimma was said to be the covenant, so it is among the things repeated for difference of wording, if we say that al-ill is also the covenant; it is like His saying, the Exalted: {صَلَوَاتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِم وَرَحْمَةٌ} [al-Baqara: 157], and his saying:
2467 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وألفى قولَها كَذِباً ومَيْنا
(... and he found her words a lie and falsehood.)
and his saying:
2468 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وهندٌ أتى مِنْ دونِها النَّأْيُ والبعدُ
(... and Hind, between whom and us came remoteness and distance.)
It was said: al-dhimma is guarantee (ḍamān); one says «هو في ذمَّتي» that is: in my guarantee, and from it the people of the dhimma (ahl al-dhimma) were named, for their entering into the guarantee of the Muslims; and one says «له عليَّ ذِمَّةٌ وذِمام ومَذَمَّة، وهي الذِّمُّ». Ibn ʿArafa said that and recited from Usāma ibn al-Ḥārith:
2469 - يُصَيِّح بالأَْسْحار في كل صَارَة ... كما ناشد الذِّمَّ الكفيلَ المعاهِدُ
(He cries out at the pre-dawn hours in every tract, as the covenanter adjures the guarantor by the dhimm.)
Al-Rāghib said: "Al-dhimām is that for the squandering of which a man is blamed (yudhammu), of covenant; likewise al-dhimma, al-madhamma and al-madhimma" — meaning with fatḥa and kasra — and it is said: «لي مَذَمَّةٌ فلا تَهْتكها». Another said: "It is called dhimma because every inviolability whose waste makes blame (dhamm) necessary for you is called dhimma," and it is pluralised as dhimm, as in his saying:
2470 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... كما ناشد الذِّمَّ. . . . . . . . . . .
(... as he adjured by the dhimm ...)
and as dhimam and dhimām. Abū Zayd said: "Madhimma with kasra is from al-dhimām and with fatḥa from al-dhamm." Al-Azharī said: "Al-dhimma: security (amān)," and in the ḥadīth: «ويَسْعى بذمَّتِهم أَدْناهم» ("The least of them strives on their behalf by their pledge"). Abū ʿUbayd said: "Al-dhimma here is security; he says: when the humblest of people gives security to a disbeliever, it takes effect upon them; for that reason ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, permitted the security of a slave on the entire army." Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "Al-dhimma: that which must be guarded and protected."
His saying: {يُرْضُونَكُم}: There are two views. One: that it is resumptive, which is the apparent view; He informed that their state is so. The second: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the subject of «لا يَرْقُبوا». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is nothing, because after their prevailing they do not please the believers."
His saying: {وتأبى}: One says abā yabā ibāʾan, that is: his refusal became intense; so every ibāʾ is refusal, but not the reverse. He said:
2471 - أبى الله إلا عَدْلَه ووفاءَه ... فلا النكرُ معروفٌ ولا العُرْفُ ضائعُ
(Allah refuses anything but His justice and His fidelity, so evil is not made good, nor is good wasted.)
and another said:
2472 - أبى الضيمَ والنعمانُ يَحْرقُ نابَه ... عليه فَأَفْضى والسيوفُ مَعَاقِلُهْ
(He refused humiliation while al-Nuʿmān gnashed his tooth against him; so he went out, his refuges being swords.)
So whoever explained it as mere refusal is not correct. The imperfect of it on yafʿal with fatḥa on the ʿayn is irregular, and likewise qalā yaqlā in one dialect.

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ جَاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ وَالْمُنَافِقِينَ وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ) (٧٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ): If it is asked: how is the wāw fitting here, when the fāʾ seems more suited to this place? There are three answers:
First: it is the wāw of the ḥāl (circumstantial); the implied sense is: "do that while they are deserving of Hell", and that state is the state of their unbelief and their hypocrisy. Second: the wāw was brought to signal that an omitted verb is intended, its implied form being: "and know that their refuge is Hell". Third: the speech is construed according to the meaning; and the meaning is that there have been combined for them the punishment of this world, through jihad and harshness, and the punishment of the Hereafter, through Hell being made a refuge for them.

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ مَا قَالُوا وَلَقَدْ قَالُوا كَلِمَةَ الْكُفْرِ وَكَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِسْلَامِهِمْ وَهَمُّوا بِمَا لَمْ يَنَالُوا وَمَا نَقَمُوا إِلَّا أَنْ أَغْنَاهُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ فَإِنْ يَتُوبُوا يَكُ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ وَإِنْ يَتَوَلَّوْا يُعَذِّبْهُمُ اللَّهُ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَمَا لَهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ) (٧٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا قَالُوا): it is the answer to an oath, and يَحْلِفُونَ stands in place of the oath.
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا نَقَمُوا إِلَّا أَنْ أَغْنَاهُمُ اللَّهُ): أَنْ together with what it governs is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «نَقَمُوا»; i.e. "and they resented nothing but Allah's enriching them". It is also said: it is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), and the direct object is omitted; i.e. "they resented faith only so that they might be enriched".

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ عَاهَدَ اللَّهَ لَئِنْ آتَانَا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ وَلَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) (٧٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَئِنْ آتَانَا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): there are two views on it. First: its implied form is "he made a covenant, and said: لَئِنْ آتَانَا". Second: that «عَاهَدَ» is in the sense of «قَالَ» ("said"), since a covenant is a saying.

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي الصَّدَقَاتِ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ إِلَّا جُهْدَهُمْ فَيَسْخَرُونَ مِنْهُمْ سَخِرَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ) (٧٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject).
And (مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ».
And (فِي الصَّدَقَاتِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَلْمِزُونَ; it is not attached to الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ, so that the two would not be separated by an extraneous element.
(وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ. It is also said: to الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ; i.e. "and they mock those who find nothing". It is also said: it is conjoined to الْمُؤْمِنِينَ. On these views, the khabar (predicate) of the first has two possibilities: first, «فَيَسْخَرُونَ», the fāʾ entering because of the resemblance to a conditional that الَّذِينَ has. Second: that the khabar is «سَخِرَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ»; and on this meaning it is possible that الَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ is in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb that سَخِرَ explains, its implied form being: "He found fault with those who mock".
It is also said: the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "among them are those who mock".

ukberi-tibyan:80-80.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ أَوْ لَا تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ إِنْ تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً فَلَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفَاسِقِينَ) (٨٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً): it is accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the number standing in place of the maṣdar; as in their saying ضَرَبْتُهُ عِشْرِينَ ضَرْبَةً ("I struck him twenty blows").

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَرِحَ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ خِلَافَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ وَكَرِهُوا أَنْ يُجَاهِدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَقَالُوا لَا تَنْفِرُوا فِي الْحَرِّ قُلْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ أَشَدُّ حَرًّا لَوْ كَانُوا يَفْقَهُونَ) (٨١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِمَقْعَدِهِمْ): i.e. "in their staying behind (bi-quʿūdihim)".
And (خِلَافَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ): an adverb (ẓarf) in the sense of خَلْفَ ("behind"); i.e. "after him", and what governs it is «مَقْعَدِ». It is also possible that what governs it is «فَرِحَ». It is also said: it is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose); on this view it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "for opposing him", and what governs it is الْمَقْعَدُ or فَرِحَ. It is also said: it is accusative as a maṣdar by a verb indicated by the speech, because their staying behind him is a lagging behind (takhallafa).

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيلًا وَلْيَبْكُوا كَثِيرًا جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ) (٨٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَلِيلًا): i.e. "a little laughter", or "a little time".
And (جَزَاءً): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:83-83.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ رَجَعَكَ اللَّهُ إِلَى طَائِفَةٍ مِنْهُمْ فَاسْتَأْذَنُوكَ لِلْخُرُوجِ فَقُلْ لَنْ تَخْرُجُوا مَعِيَ أَبَدًا وَلَنْ تُقَاتِلُوا مَعِيَ عَدُوًّا إِنَّكُمْ رَضِيتُمْ بِالْقُعُودِ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ فَاقْعُدُوا مَعَ الْخَالِفِينَ) (٨٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِنْ رَجَعَكَ اللَّهُ): it is transitive by itself, and its maṣdar (verbal noun) is رَجْعٌ; it also comes as intransitive, and its maṣdar is الرُّجُوعُ.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تُصَلِّ عَلَى أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ مَاتَ أَبَدًا وَلَا تَقُمْ عَلَى قَبْرِهِ إِنَّهُمْ كَفَرُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ فَاسِقُونَ) (٨٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْهُمْ): a naʿt (adjective) of أَحَدٍ, and «مَاتَ» is another naʿt. It is also possible that «مِنْهُمْ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مَاتَ.
(أَبَدًا): an adverb (ẓarf) for «تُصَلِّ».

ukberi-tibyan:86-86.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَجَاهِدُوا مَعَ رَسُولِهِ اسْتَأْذَنَكَ أُولُو الطَّوْلِ مِنْهُمْ وَقَالُوا ذَرْنَا نَكُنْ مَعَ الْقَاعِدِينَ) (٨٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ آمِنُوا): i.e. "believe!"; and the implied sense is: "it is said in it: believe!". It is also said: أَنْ here is maṣdariyya (the one forming a maṣdar); its implied form is: "it was sent down with 'that you believe'", i.e. with faith.

ukberi-tibyan:87-87.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَضُوا بِأَنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الْخَوَالِفِ وَطُبِعَ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ) (٨٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَعَ الْخَوَالِفِ): it is the plural of خَالِفَةٌ, which is the woman. A man may also be called خَالِفٌ and خَالِفَةٌ, but the masculine is not pluralized as خَوَالِفُ.

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءَ الْمُعَذِّرُونَ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ لِيُؤْذَنَ لَهُمْ وَقَعَدَ الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ سَيُصِيبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ) (٩٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَجَاءَ الْمُعَذِّرُونَ): it is read in many ways, which we have mentioned at His saying: (بِأَلْفٍ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ).

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَيْسَ عَلَى الضُّعَفَاءِ وَلَا عَلَى الْمَرْضَى وَلَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ مَا يُنْفِقُونَ حَرَجٌ إِذَا نَصَحُوا لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ مَا عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (٩١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذَا نَصَحُوا): what governs it is the meaning of the speech; i.e. "they do not go out at that time".

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ إِذَا مَا أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ قُلْتَ لَا أَجِدُ مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ تَوَلَّوْا وَأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ حَزَنًا أَلَّا يَجِدُوا مَا يُنْفِقُونَ) (٩٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الضُّعَفَاءِ, and so enters into the khabar (predicate) of لَيْسَ. If you wish, you may conjoin it to الْمُحْسِنِينَ, in which case the mubtadaʾ (subject) is مِنْ سَبِيلٍ. It is also possible that the mubtadaʾ is omitted; i.e. "and upon those who . . ." up to the end of the ṣila (relative clause), "is no blame" or "no way". The answer of إِذَا is «تَوَلَّوْا»; and there is a discussion about it which we have mentioned at His saying: (كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا).
(وَأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ): the clause is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).
And (مِنَ الدَّمْعِ): like the one in al-Māʾida.
And (حَزَنًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl, or accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar by a verb indicated by what precedes it.
(أَلَّا يَجِدُوا): attached (mutaʿalliq) to حَزَنٍ, the preposition being omitted; and it may be attached to تَفِيضُ.

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا السَّبِيلُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَسْتَأْذِنُونَكَ وَهُمْ أَغْنِيَاءُ رَضُوا بِأَنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الْخَوَالِفِ وَطَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ) (٩٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَضُوا): it may be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with قَدْ intended along with it.

ukberi-tibyan:94-94.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَعْتَذِرُونَ إِلَيْكُمْ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ قُلْ لَا تَعْتَذِرُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكُمْ قَدْ نَبَّأَنَا اللَّهُ مِنْ أَخْبَارِكُمْ وَسَيَرَى اللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ وَرَسُولُهُ ثُمَّ تُرَدُّونَ إِلَى عَالِمِ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) (٩٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَدْ نَبَّأَنَا اللَّهُ): this verb may take three objects. The first of them is «نَا», and the other two are omitted, their implied form being: "news from your news, established (as fact)".
And (مِنْ أَخْبَارِكُمْ): a pointer to what is omitted; «مِنْ» is not redundant (zāʾida), since if it were redundant it would be the second object, with the third object omitted, and that is wrong, because in this chapter, when the second object is mentioned, mentioning the third becomes necessary. It is also said: «مِنْ» is in the sense of عَنْ ("about").

ukberi-tibyan:95-95.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ لَكُمْ إِذَا انْقَلَبْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لِتُعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ فَأَعْرِضُوا عَنْهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ رِجْسٌ وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ) (٩٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَزَاءً): a maṣdar (verbal noun); i.e. "they are requited with that a requital"; or it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الْأَعْرَابُ أَشَدُّ كُفْرًا وَنِفَاقًا وَأَجْدَرُ أَلَّا يَعْلَمُوا حُدُودَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ) (٩٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَجْدَرُ أَنْ لَا يَعْلَمُوا): i.e. "بِأَنْ يَعْلَمُوا" ("more apt in that they know"). «[Translator's note: the text as printed reads بِأَنْ يَعْلَمُوا without the negative لَا; the intended gloss is presumably بِأَنْ لَا يَعْلَمُوا, "more apt in that they do not know", i.e. the preposition bāʾ is omitted before أَنْ.]»

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ مَا يُنْفِقُ مَغْرَمًا وَيَتَرَبَّصُ بِكُمُ الدَّوَائِرَ عَلَيْهِمْ دَائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ وَاللَّهُ سُمَيْعٌ عَلِيمٌ) (٩٨). «[Translator's note: سُمَيْعٌ in the quotation as printed is a misprint for سَمِيعٌ.]»
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِكُمُ الدَّوَائِرَ): the bāʾ may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to (يَتَرَبَّصُ), or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الدَّوَائِرِ.
(دَائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ): it is read with ḍamma on the sīn, meaning harm; it is in reality a maṣdar (verbal noun): one says سُؤْتُهُ سُوءًا وَمَسَاءَةً وَمَسَائِيَةً ("I harmed him").
And it is read with fatḥa on the sīn, meaning corruption and baseness.

ukberi-tibyan:99-99.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَيَتَّخِذُ مَا يُنْفِقُ قُرُبَاتٍ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَصَلَوَاتِ الرَّسُولِ أَلَا إِنَّهَا قُرْبَةٌ لَهُمْ سَيُدْخِلُهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (٩٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُرُبَاتٍ): it is the second object of «يَتَّخِذُ».
And (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): a naʿt (adjective) of قُرُبَاتٍ, or an adverb (ẓarf) for «يَتَّخِذُ», or for قُرُبَاتٍ.
(وَصَلَوَاتِ الرَّسُولِ): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to مَا يُنْفِقُ, its implied form being: "and the prayers of the Messenger as means of nearness (qurubāt)".
And قُرْبَةٌ is with sukūn on the rāʾ; it has also been read with ḍamma on it by way of vowel harmony (itbāʿ).

ukberi-tibyan:100-100.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالسَّابِقُونَ الْأَوَّلُونَ مِنَ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصَارِ وَالَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُمْ بِإِحْسَانٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي تَحْتَهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا ذَلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ) (١٠٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالسَّابِقُونَ): it may be maʿṭūf (conjoined) to His saying «مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ», its implied form being: "and among them are the forerunners".
It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), and regarding the khabar (predicate) there are three views. First: «الْأَوَّلُونَ»; and the meaning is: "the forerunners to the Hijra are the first of the people of the religion", or "the forerunners to Paradise are the first to the Hijra". Second: the khabar is «مِنَ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصَارِ», and the meaning in it is the announcement that the forerunners of this community are from the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār.
Third: that the khabar is «رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ». And «وَالْأَنْصَارُ» is read in the nominative, either as conjoined to «السَّابِقُونَ», or as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ»; and that is on the first two views.
And بِإِحْسَانٍ is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «اتَّبَعُوهُمْ».
(تَجْرِي تَحْتَهَا): and «مِنْ تَحْتِهَا»; the meaning in both is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِمَّنْ حَوْلَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ مُنَافِقُونَ وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ مَرَدُوا عَلَى النِّفَاقِ لَا تَعْلَمُهُمْ نَحْنُ نَعْلَمُهُمْ سَنُعَذِّبُهُمْ مَرَّتَيْنِ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَى عَذَابٍ عَظِيمٍ) (١٠١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمِمَّنْ): مَنْ is in the sense of الَّذِي ("who/those who"); and (مُنَافِقُونَ) is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate).
And (مَرَدُوا): a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "and among the people of Medina are a people who have persisted". It is also said: مَرَدُوا is a naʿt of مُنَافِقُونَ, a separation having been made between the two; and مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "among the people of Medina are a people likewise".
(لَا تَعْلَمُهُمْ): another naʿt, like مَرَدُوا.
And (نَعْلَمُهُمْ): in the sense of نَعْرِفُهُمْ ("We know them / recognise them"), so it takes a single object.

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَآخَرُونَ اعْتَرَفُوا بِذُنُوبِهِمْ خَلَطُوا عَمَلًا صَالِحًا وَآخَرَ سَيِّئًا عَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) (١٠٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَآخَرُونَ اعْتَرَفُوا): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to مُنَافِقُونَ. It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with اعْتَرَفُوا its naʿt (adjective) and «خَلَطُوا» its khabar (predicate).
(وَآخَرَ سَيِّئًا): conjoined to «عَمَلًا»; had it been with the bāʾ, it would also be permissible: you say خَلَطْتُ الْحِنْطَةَ وَالشَّعِيرَ and خَلَطْتُ الْحِنْطَةَ بِالشَّعِيرِ ("I mixed the wheat and the barley" / "I mixed the wheat with the barley").
(عَسَى اللَّهُ): the clause is resumptive. It is also said: خَلَطُوا is a ḥāl (circumstantial), with قَدْ intended along with it, i.e. "they confessed their sins, having mixed", and «عَسَى اللَّهُ» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ صَلَاتَكَ سَكَنٌ لَهُمْ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ) (١٠٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ): «مِنْ» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to خُذْ, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «صَدَقَةً».
(تُطَهِّرُهُمْ): in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of صَدَقَةٍ.
It may also be resumptive, the tāʾ being for the second person; i.e. "you purify them".
(وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ): the tāʾ is for the second person and nothing else, because of His saying «بِهَا». It is possible that «تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of صَدَقَةٍ even while we say that the tāʾ in both is for the second person; because His saying «تُطَهِّرُهُمْ» has the implied form "by it", indicated by the second «بِهَا»; and since both contain a pronoun referring to the ṣadaqa, it may be a naʿt of it.
The clause may also be a ḥāl from the agent pronoun in «خُذْ».
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ صَلَاتَكَ): it is read in the singular and the plural, and both are clear.
And (سَكَنٌ): in the sense of "that in which repose is found (maskūn ilayhā)"; for that reason it was not made feminine. It is like الْقَبْضُ in the sense of الْمَقْبُوضُ ("what is seized").

ukberi-tibyan:104-104.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَأْخُذُ الصَّدَقَاتِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ) (١٠٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُوَ يَقْبَلُ): هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and يَقْبَلُ is the khabar (predicate). It is not permissible for «هُوَ» to be a separating pronoun (faṣl), because يَقْبَلُ is neither definite nor close to being definite.

ukberi-tibyan:106-106.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ لِأَمْرِ اللَّهِ إِمَّا يُعَذِّبُهُمْ وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ) (١٠٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «وَآخَرُونَ اعْتَرَفُوا». And مُرْجَوْنَ is with the hamza, according to the original form, and without hamza; its origin has been mentioned in al-Aʿrāf.
(إِمَّا يُعَذِّبُهُمْ وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ): إِمَّا here is for doubt, and the doubt goes back to the creature. When إِمَّا is for doubt, it may be followed by a noun and it may be followed by a verb; but if it is for choice (takhyīr) and a verb comes after it, أَنْ accompanies it, as in His saying: (إِمَّا أَنْ تُلْقِيَ); and this has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:107-107.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مَسْجِدًا ضِرَارًا وَكُفْرًا وَتَفْرِيقًا بَيْنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَإِرْصَادًا لِمَنْ حَارَبَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَيَحْلِفُنَّ إِنْ أَرَدْنَا إِلَّا الْحُسْنَى وَاللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ) (١٠٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا): it is read with the wāw, and there are two views on it. First: it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ»; i.e. "and among them are those who took".
Second: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is (أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَانَهُ), i.e. "among them", the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) having been omitted because it is known.
It is also read without the wāw; and it is a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar (أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ) as stated before.
(ضِرَارًا): it may be the second object of اتَّخَذُوا, and likewise what comes after it. These maṣdars (verbal nouns) all stand in the place of the active participle, i.e. "harming" and "dividing". They may also all be mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).

ukberi-tibyan:108-108.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا تَقُمْ فِيهِ أَبَدًا لَمَسْجِدٌ أُسِّسَ عَلَى التَّقْوَى مِنْ أَوَّلِ يَوْمٍ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَقُومَ فِيهِ فِيهِ رِجَالٌ يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَتَطَهَّرُوا وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُطَّهِّرِينَ) (١٠٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَمَسْجِدٌ): the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); it is also said: the answer to an omitted oath. And «أَسَّسَ» is a naʿt (adjective) of it. «[Translator's note: the verb is printed here as أَسَّسَ (active); in the āya it is the passive أُسِّسَ.]»
And (مِنْ أَوَّلِ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَسَّسَ. The implied form according to some of the Basrans is "from the founding of the first day", because they hold that «مِنْ» does not enter upon time, and that this belongs only to مُنْذُ. This is weak here, because the implied "founding" is not a place, such that «مِنْ» could be for the starting point of its extent. What shows that «مِنْ» may enter upon time is its occurrence in the Qurʾan entering upon «قَبْلَ» where time is meant, and that is frequent in the Qurʾan and elsewhere.
The khabar (predicate) is (أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَقُومَ). The first «فِيهِ» is attached to «تَقُومَ», and the tāʾ is addressing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
(فِيهِ رِجَالٌ): there are three views on it. First: it is a naʿt of مَسْجِدٌ that has come after the khabar. Second: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in the first «فِيهِ», and what governs it is «تَقُومَ». Third: it is resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:109-109.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَمَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَانَهُ عَلَى تَقْوَى مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوَانٍ خَيْرٌ أَمْ مَنْ أَسَّسَ بُنْيَانَهُ عَلَى شَفَا جُرُفٍ هَارٍ فَانْهَارَ بِهِ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ) (١٠٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى تَقْوَى): it may be in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «أَسَّسَ», i.e. "upon the intention of piety"; the implied form being: "intending piety by his building".
It may also be an object of أَسَّسَ.
(جُرُفٍ): with ḍamma and with sukūn; they are two dialectal forms.
And regarding (هَارٍ) there are two views. First: its origin is «هَوَرَ» or «هَيَرَ» on the pattern faʿal; when the weak letter was vowelled and what precedes it had fatḥa, it was changed to alif. This is recognised by the accusative, nominative and genitive, like their saying:
كَبْشٌ صَافٌ, i.e. صَوِفٌ ("a woolly ram"), and يَوْمٌ رَاحٌ, i.e. "having wind (rūḥ)". Second: that its origin is هَاوِرٌ or هَايِرٌ; then the middle radical (ʿayn) of the word was moved back so that it came after the rāʾ, and the wāw was changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it; then it was dropped because of its being vowelless together with the vowelless tanwīn. So its pattern after the [metathesis (al-qalb)] is fāliʿ, and after the dropping fāl. The middle radical of the word is wāw or yāʾ: one says تَهَوَّرَ الْبِنَاءُ and تَهَيَّرَ ("the building collapsed").
(فَانْهَارَ بِهِ): بِهِ here is a ḥāl; i.e. "it collapsed while he was with it".
«[Translator's note: the word for "metathesis" (الْقَلْبِ) appears in square brackets in the source edition.]»

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ اشْتَرَى مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ يُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ وَعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ وَالْقُرْآنِ وَمَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ مِنَ اللَّهِ فَاسْتَبْشِرُوا بِبَيْعِكُمُ الَّذِي بَايَعْتُمْ بِهِ وَذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ) (١١١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ الْجَنَّةَ): the bāʾ here is for exchange (muqābala); the implied form is: "in return for their being entitled to Paradise".
(يُقَاتِلُونَ): resumptive.
(فَيَقْتُلُونَ وَيُقْتَلُونَ): it is like the one at the end of Āl ʿImrān regarding the variant readings.
(وَعْدًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun); i.e. "He promised them that as a promise"; and (حَقًّا) is its naʿt (adjective).

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (التَّائِبُونَ الْعَابِدُونَ الْحَامِدُونَ السَّائِحُونَ الرَّاكِعُونَ السَّاجِدُونَ الْآمِرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَالنَّاهُونَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَالْحَافِظُونَ لِحُدُودِ اللَّهِ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) (١١٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (التَّائِبُونَ): it is read in the nominative, i.e. "they are the repentant". It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being الْآمِرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ and what follows it; but that is weak.
It is also read with the yāʾ, by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean") or أَمْدَحُ ("I praise"); and it may be genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الْمُؤْمِنِينَ. (وَالنَّاهُونَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ): the wāw entered on the eighth attribute only to signal that seven, for them, is a complete number; that is why they say "seven in eight", i.e. seven cubits by eight spans. The wāw indicated this only because the wāw signals that what comes after it is other than what comes before it; that is why it entered into the chapter of conjunction proper (ʿaṭf al-nasaq).

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ وَالْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصَارِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ فِي سَاعَةِ الْعُسْرَةِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا كَادَ يَزِيغُ قُلُوبُ فَرِيقٍ مِنْهُمْ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّهُ بِهِمْ رَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ) (١١٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا كَادَ يَزِيغُ قُلُوبُ فَرِيقٍ مِنْهُمْ): regarding the subject of كَادَ there are three views. First: it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause after it is in the position of the accusative. Second: its subject is an implied pronoun, its implied form being: "after the people had almost …", and on this view the referent is the pronoun in مِنْهُمْ. Third: its subject is الْقُلُوبُ, and يَزِيغُ is intended to come after it, containing an agent pronoun. That is acceptable only on the reading with tāʾ; on the reading with yāʾ it is weak — besides which the basis of this construal is itself weak, as we have shown at His saying: (مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ).

ukberi-tibyan:118-118.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَعَلَى الثَّلَاثَةِ الَّذِينَ خُلِّفُوا حَتَّى إِذَا ضَاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَرْضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتْ وَضَاقَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ وَظَنُّوا أَنْ لَا مَلْجَأَ مِنَ اللَّهِ إِلَّا إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ لِيَتُوبُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ) (١١٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَعَلَى الثَّلَاثَةِ): if you wish, you may conjoin it to النَّبِيِّ ﷺ, i.e. "He turned in mercy to the Prophet and to the three"; and if you wish, to «عَلَيْهِمْ», i.e. "then He turned to them and to the three".
(لَا مَلْجَأَ مِنَ اللَّهِ): the khabar (predicate) of «لَا» is «مِنَ اللَّهِ».
(إِلَّا إِلَيْهِ): an exception, like لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ.

ukberi-tibyan:120-120.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَا كَانَ لِأَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُمْ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ أَنْ يَتَخَلَّفُوا عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَرْغَبُوا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ عَنْ نَفْسِهِ ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ لَا يُصِيبُهُمْ ظَمَأٌ وَلَا نَصَبٌ وَلَا مَخْمَصَةٌ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَطَئُونَ مَوْطِئًا يَغِيظُ الْكُفَّارَ وَلَا يَنَالُونَ مِنْ عَدُوٍّ نَيْلًا إِلَّا كُتِبَ لَهُمْ بِهِ عَمَلٌ صَالِحٌ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) (١٢٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَوْطِئًا): it may be a place, in which case it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); or it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), like الْمَوْعِدُ.

ukberi-tibyan:122-122.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ لِيَنْفِرُوا كَافَّةً فَلَوْلَا نَفَرَ مِنْ كُلِّ فِرْقَةٍ مِنْهُمْ طَائِفَةٌ لِيَتَفَقَّهُوا فِي الدِّينِ وَلِيُنْذِرُوا قَوْمَهُمْ إِذَا رَجَعُوا إِلَيْهِمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَحْذَرُونَ) (١٢٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِرْقَةٍ مِنْهُمْ): «مِنْهُمْ» may be a naʿt (adjective) of فِرْقَةٍ, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «طَائِفَةٌ».

ukberi-tibyan:123-123.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ يَلُونَكُمْ مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ وَلْيَجِدُوا فِيكُمْ غِلْظَةً وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ) (١٢٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (غِلْظَةً): it is read with kasra on the ghayn, with fatḥa and with ḍamma, and all are dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:127-127.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا مَا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ نَظَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَى بَعْضٍ هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ مِنْ أَحَدٍ ثُمَّ انْصَرَفُوا صَرَفَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ) (١٢٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ): its implied form is: "saying: هَلْ يَرَاكُمْ".

ukberi-tibyan:128-128.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ) (١٢٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ): there are two views on it. First: it is a naʿt (adjective) of رَسُولٌ, and «مَا» is maṣdariyya (forming a maṣdar), its position being nominative by عَزِيزٌ. Second: that «مَا غَنِمْتُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ» a fronted khabar (predicate), the clause being a naʿt of «رَسُولٌ». «[Translator's note: «مَا غَنِمْتُمْ» is as printed; the āya reads مَا عَنِتُّمْ.]»
(بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to «رَءُوفٌ».
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَرَاءَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ إِلَى الَّذِينَ عَاهَدْتُمْ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ (١) فَسِيحُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِي اللَّهِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْزِي الْكَافِرِينَ) (٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَرَاءَةٌ): there are two views on it. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a disavowal" (هَذَا, or هَذِهِ), and «مِنَ اللَّهِ» is a naʿt (adjective) to it; and «إِلَى الَّذِينَ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to بَرَاءَةٌ, as you say بَرِئْتُ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ كَذَا ("I declare to you my disavowal of such-and-such"). The second: it is a mubtadaʾ, and «مِنَ اللَّهِ» is a naʿt to it, and «إِلَى الَّذِينَ» is the khabar. It was read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, «مِنِ اللَّهِ» with kasra on the nūn, according to the basic rule for the meeting of two vowelless letters. And (أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ) is an adverb (ẓarf) for فَسِيحُوا.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ تَابُوا وَأَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَاةَ فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ وَنُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ) (١١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَإِخْوَانُكُمْ): i.e. "then they are your brothers".
And (فِي الدِّينِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to إِخْوَانُكُمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ نَكَثُوا أَيْمَانَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ عَهْدِهِمْ وَطَعَنُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ فَقَاتِلُوا أَئِمَّةَ الْكُفْرِ إِنَّهُمْ لَا أَيْمَانَ لَهُمْ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَنْتَهُونَ) (١٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَئِمَّةَ الْكُفْرِ): it is the plural of إِمَامٍ, and its origin is أَئِمَّةٌ «[Translator's note: so in the text; the underlying form meant is presumably أَأْمِمَةٌ, as the following explanation shows]», like خِبَاءٍ and أَخْبِيَةٍ. The vowel of the first mīm was transferred to the vowelless hamza, and [the mīm] was assimilated into the other mīm. Whoever pronounces both hamzas fully (taḥqīq) brings them out according to the original; and whoever changes the second into a yāʾ does so because of the kasra transferred to it. It is not permissible here to make it "between-between" (bayna bayna), as was done with the hamza of أَئِذَا, because the kasra here is transferred, whereas there it is original. Had the second hamza here been lightened according to the rule, it would have become an alif because what precedes it has fatḥa; but that was abandoned so that it might bear the vowel of the mīm in the original form.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَا تُقَاتِلُونَ قَوْمًا نَكَثُوا أَيْمَانَهُمْ وَهَمُّوا بِإِخْرَاجِ الرَّسُولِ وَهُمْ بَدَءُوكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ أَتَخْشَوْنَهُمْ فَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تَخْشَوْهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) (١٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ): it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf).
(فَاللَّهُ أَحَقُّ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there are two views on the khabar (predicate). The first: it is «أَحَقُّ», and «أَنْ تَخْشَوْهُ» is in the position of the accusative or the genitive, i.e. "that you should fear Him" (بِأَنْ تَخْشَوْهُ); and there is an omission in the statement, i.e. "more deserving than others that you should fear Him". Or أَنْ تَخْشَوْهُ is a mubtadaʾ that is a badal (substitute) from the name of Allah, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), and أَحَقُّ is the khabar, the implied wording being: "the fear of Allah is more deserving". The second: «أَنْ تَخْشَوْهُ» is a mubtadaʾ, and أَحَقُّ is its khabar placed before it, and the clause is the khabar of the name of Allah.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَذَانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ إِلَى النَّاسِ يَوْمَ الْحَجِّ الْأَكْبَرِ أَنَّ اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ وَرَسُولُهُ فَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ غَيْرُ مُعْجِزِي اللَّهِ وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ) (٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَذَانٌ): like «بَرَاءَةٌ». And «إِلَى النَّاسِ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَذَانٌ, or is a khabar (predicate) for it. (أَنَّ اللَّهَ بَرِيءٌ): the well-known [reading] is with fatḥa on the hamza, and there are two views on it. The first: it is the khabar of الْأَذَان, i.e. "the announcement from Allah is His disavowal of the polytheists". The second: it is an adjective (ṣifa), i.e. "and an announcement consisting in the disavowal". It is also said that the implied wording is: "and an announcement from Allah of the disavowal", so the bāʾ is attached to the maṣdar (verbal noun) itself. (وَرَسُولُهُ): it is read in the nominative, and there are three views on it. The first: it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the pronoun in بَرِيءٌ, and what comes between them functions like an emphasis (tawkīd); for this reason the conjoining is acceptable. The second: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and His Messenger is free [of them]".
